sections.heading: CAT 2026 Fellow Programmes in Management (FPM/ PhD)

content.text: CAT 2026 scores are also used for doctoral-level admissions at various IIMs:

Note: Separate advertisements may be issued for programmes other than PGP, specific to each IIM. Candidates must check the concerned IIM's website before applying to confirm updated eligibility and admission process details.

sections.heading: CAT 2026 Eligibility Criteria

items: Candidate must hold a Bachelor's Degree with at least 50% marks or equivalent CGPA (45% for SC, ST, and PwBD candidates), from a university incorporated by an Act of Parliament/State legislature or deemed under Section 3 of the UGC Act, 1956, or an equivalent qualification recognised by the Ministry of Education, Government of India.
Candidates in the final year of their Bachelor's degree, or those awaiting results after completing degree requirements, can also apply.
Such provisional candidates, if selected, must submit a certificate from their Principal/Registrar (by the date specified by the respective IIM) confirming completion of all degree requirements.

content.text: Candidates must fulfil any one of the following:

items: Completed Bachelor's degree with the required percentage of marks.
Completed a professional degree (CA/CS/ICWA (CMA)/Fellow of the Institute of Actuaries of India (FIAI)) with the required percentage.
Currently in the final year of a Bachelor's degree with the required percentage.

content.text: SC/ST/PwBD candidates require a minimum of 45%; General, EWS, and NC-OBC candidates require a minimum of 50%.

sections.heading: How Percentage/ CGPA Is Calculated

content.text: Percentage of marks is calculated based on the practice followed by the candidate's own University/Institution. Where grades/CGPA apply, conversion follows the University/Institution's certified procedure. If no such conversion scheme exists, equivalence is calculated by dividing the candidate's CGPA by the maximum possible CGPA and multiplying by 100.

Important: Meeting the minimum eligibility criteria does not guarantee shortlisting by IIMs. Candidates must maintain a valid, unique email account and mobile number throughout the entire selection process.

sections.heading: CAT 2026 Reservation Criteria
Specified Disability Categories (PwBD)

items: Blindness and low vision
Deaf and hard of hearing
Locomotor disability including cerebral palsy, leprosy cured, dwarfism, acid attack victims, and muscular dystrophy
Autism, intellectual disability, specific learning disability, and mental illness
Multiple disabilities from the above categories
Other specified disabilities mentioned in the Schedule of the RPwD Act, 2016

content.text: A "Person with Benchmark Disability" means a person certified with not less than 40% of a specified disability. The applicable Central Government list as on the last date of CAT registration is binding - no subsequent changes will apply for CAT 2026 or later selection processes.

sections.heading: NC-OBC/EWS Certificate Requirements

items: NC-OBC certificates must be issued on or after April 1, 2026.
EWS certificates must be valid for the year 2026–27 and specifically assessed for financial year 2025–26.

content.text: Candidates who applied for a valid NC-OBC/EWS certificate on or after April 1, 2026 but haven't received it by the time of registration may still apply by uploading a single PDF containing:

items: A properly filled "Undertaking for NC-OBC/EWS Certificate" (available on the official CAT 2026 website)
The older NC-OBC/EWS certificate issued prior to April 1, 2026
A copy of the communication/acknowledgement/screenshot confirming submission of the certificate application

content.text: Failure to upload the complete set of documents may result in disqualification from the entire admission process. No category change will be entertained after registration.

sections.heading: CAT 2026 Application Fee

content.text: The fee is paid only once, regardless of the number of IIMs/programmes a candidate applies to. SC, ST, and PwBD candidates must upload their category certificates at the time of registration. Fees once paid are non-refundable under any circumstances.

sections.heading: How to Apply for CAT 2026

items: Registration opens at 10:00 a.m. on August 3, 2026, and closes at 5:00 p.m. on September 15, 2026, on the official website https://iimcat.ac.in.
At the time of registration, candidates must select five preferred test cities from a drop-down menu.
After registration closes, candidates will be allotted one of their five preferred cities, subject to availability. In rare cases, a nearby city may be allotted instead.
Admit cards can be downloaded from November 4, 2026, until November 29, 2026.
Full step-by-step details will be available in the official CAT 2026 registration guide.

sections.heading: CAT 2026 Test Centres

content.text: CAT 2026 will be conducted across approximately 170 test cities in India. The list of test cities will be available on the official CAT website, and the exact test centre name will be indicated on the candidate's Admit Card. IIMs reserve the right to add, remove, change, or cancel any test centre/city, and may change the test time or date at their discretion.

sections.heading: CAT 2026 Result and Scorecard

items: CAT 2026 results are expected to be declared in the first week of January 2027.
Scorecards will be made available on the official CAT website; candidates may also be intimated via SMS.
The CAT 2026 score is valid only until December 31, 2027.
No queries regarding scorecard issuance will be entertained after this validity period.

sections.heading: CAT 2026 Admission Process

content.text: Each IIM independently sets its own eligibility criteria, academic cut-offs, and relative weightage, and follows its own selection process. CAT 2026 performance is an important component, but IIMs may also consider prior academic performance, relevant work experience, and other inputs at various shortlisting stages. Candidates should refer to the individual admission policies published on each IIM's website.

sections.heading: Use of CAT 2026 Score by Non-IIM Institutions

content.text: CAT 2026 scores can also be used by listed non-IIM member institutions that have registered to accept them. The complete list of such institutions is available at https://iimcat.ac.in. IIMs have no role in the selection process followed by these non-IIM institutions.

links.text: https://iimcat.ac.in

sections.heading: Important Instructions for CAT 2026 Candidates

items: Any incorrect information or process violation detected at any stage will lead to immediate disqualification, and the candidate will not be allowed to appear for CAT in future.
If such violations go undetected during the current process but are discovered later, disqualification will apply with retrospective effect.
Candidates must retain the Information Bulletin for future reference.
Any dispute concerning CAT 2026 is subject to the jurisdiction of competent courts within Indore only.
Candidates must declare and maintain a valid, unique email account and mobile number throughout the selection process.

detail.short_info: Haryana NEET UG Round 3 Counselling 2026 registration and choice filling are open from September 28 to October 10. Check important dates, registration steps, seat allotment and joining deadline.

content.text: Pt. B. D. Sharma University of Health Sciences (UHSR), Rohtak has released the schedule for Haryana NEET UG Round 3 Counselling 2026. Registration, editing, choice filling and choice locking run from September 28, 2026 to October 10, 2026 (till 11:59 PM). The provisional seat allotment will be released on October 12, 2026.

This counselling is for eligible NEET UG 2026 candidates seeking MBBS or BDS admission in government, government-aided, private medical and private dental colleges, and specified private and minority universities in Haryana. Always confirm details on the official counselling website, uhsrugcounselling.com, before acting.

sections.heading: How to Register for Haryana NEET UG Round 3 Counselling 2026

content.text: The whole process is online. Follow these steps:

items: Visit the official counselling website, uhsrugcounselling.com.
Click the Round 3 registration link.
Enter your NEET UG 2026 roll number and the other required details.
Upload the required documents in the prescribed format.
Pay the required security amount online.
Select your preferred MBBS and BDS colleges and courses.
Arrange the colleges in the order you prefer.
Lock your choices before the October 10 deadline.
Download the confirmation page and keep it for future use.

sections.heading: Choice Filling Is Fresh for Round 3

content.text: You must submit new choices in Round 3. Choices filled in Round 1 or Round 2 will not be considered. If you want an upgrade, plan your preference list carefully before you lock it.

sections.heading: Haryana NEET UG Round 3 Seat Allotment 2026

content.text: The provisional seat allotment will be released on October 12, 2026. If you find a problem with your allotment, you can submit a grievance on the same day. Candidates who receive a seat must then pay the provisional tuition fee between October 12 and October 14, 2026 (till 11:00 PM).
The source does not give the seat matrix, previous-year cut-offs, or tuition fee amounts. These details are not available in the official source used for this article.

sections.heading: Important Rules for Haryana NEET UG Round 3 Counselling 2026

items: Round 1 or Round 2 candidates who did not get a seat do not need to register again.
Fresh candidates must register within the Round 3 window.
Fresh choices are mandatory because old choices will not be considered.
Candidates who want an upgrade must submit their willingness online.
Paying the security deposit is compulsory.
If you do not join after being allotted a seat, your security deposit is forfeited and you cannot take part in the stray vacancy round.
Check the official UHSR counselling website regularly for updates and notices.

sections.heading: NMAT 2026 Important Dates
NMAT 2026 Exam Pattern

content.text: NMAT 2026 is a computer-adaptive test that continuously adjusts question difficulty based on a candidate's previous responses. The exam consists of 108 questions across three sections, to be completed within 120 minutes.

items: Negative Marking: None.
Section Weightage: Equal weightage is given to all sections.
Section Order: Candidates can choose their preferred order for attempting sections.
Attempts: Up to 2 retakes are allowed (3 attempts in total) to improve performance.
Test Centres: The exam will be conducted at 64 test centres across 59 cities in India.

sections.heading: How to Apply for NMAT 2026

content.text: NMAT 2026 applications are accepted only in online mode through the official GMAC website. Candidates can follow these steps to register:

items: Visit the official GMAC website at mba.com.
Click on the NMAT 2026 registration link available on the homepage.
A new page will open; enter the required registration details.
Once registration is complete, fill in the application form.
Make the payment of the applicable application fee.
Click submit and download the confirmation page.
Keep a hard copy of the confirmation page for future reference.

sections.heading: NMAT 2026 Important Instructions

items: Complete registration before the closing date of 10 October 2026.
Scheduling of the exam slot must be completed by 22 October 2026.
The exam will be delivered anytime within the window of 2 November 2026 to 20 December 2026, based on the candidate's chosen slot.
Retain the downloaded confirmation page/receipt after submitting the application.
Refer only to the official mba.com website for updates, as third-party sources may not reflect the latest changes.

sections.heading: Why Take the NMAT Exam

content.text: NMAT by GMAC offers a few structural advantages to candidates:

items: Score-Friendly Format: No negative marking and equal weightage across all three sections.
Flexible Attempt Strategy: Candidates can choose their section order and attempt the exam up to 3 times.
Fast Results: Instant score preview after the test, with the official scorecard available for download within 48 hours.
Wide Reach: Test centres are available across 59-70+ cities in India, giving candidates flexibility in choosing a convenient location and date.
Preparation Support: Official prep material, including the NMAT Official Guide and both free and paid practice exams, is made available to registered candidates.

sections.heading: HPBOSE D.El.Ed Counselling 2026: Seat-Allotment Procedure

content.text: As per the official prospectus, counselling works as follows:

items: HPBOSE prepares a merit list based purely on total marks scored in the CET (no interview is conducted).
Candidates are called for counselling strictly in order of merit, category-wise, as per the reservation roster.
The date, time and venue for each counselling round is announced only on the official HPBOSE website - no individual letters, faxes or phone calls are sent to candidates.
At counselling, eligibility is finally verified against original documents.

Seats are allotted according to the candidate's stated institution preference and the seats available at that candidate's turn. This preference can be exercised only once - once a seat is accepted, it is final, and the candidate cannot request a change of institution.
A candidate who accepts a seat in one round cannot participate in later rounds for re-allotment.
Unfilled or vacated seats are carried forward to the next round strictly by merit.
There is no migration allowed between institutions after admission - neither between DIETs nor between private colleges.

sections.heading: How to Apply / Register for HPBOSE D.El.Ed CET and Counselling

items: Visit the official HPBOSE website: hpbose.org.
Click on the "CET / Vacancy" section, then select the D.El.Ed (CET) 2026 link.
Register and fill in personal, educational, category and exam-centre preference details in capital letters exactly as per your Matriculation certificate.
Upload a scanned photograph (JPG, under 20 KB, 3.5 cm x 4.5 cm) and signature (JPG, under 15 KB, 3.5 cm x 1.5 cm).
Pay the application fee online via net banking, debit card or credit card.
Submit the declaration and download/print the confirmation page for your records.
After the result and merit list are announced, regularly check hpbose.org for your counselling call - no separate communication is sent by post or courier.
Attend counselling in person on the notified date with all original documents, and exercise your institution preference to get your seat allotted.

sections.heading: Important Instructions for Candidates

items: The information provided in the online application (name, date of birth, category, etc.) is treated as final and generally cannot be changed once the correction window closes.
No separate letter, fax, email or phone call is sent for any round of counselling - candidates must track hpbose.org themselves.
There is no job guarantee from the Government of Himachal Pradesh after completing the D.El.Ed course.
Attendance requirement during the two-year course is 90%, with a 50% relaxation available for pregnancy/maternity cases on the Principal DIET's recommendation.
All seats are reserved for bonafide residents of Himachal Pradesh.
Any dispute regarding the CET or counselling falls under the jurisdiction of Dharamshala courts.

content.text: The HP PAT 2026 merit list is published alongside the result on hptechboard.com. It ranks all qualified candidates based on their total marks obtained in the entrance examination. Understanding how ties are resolved helps candidates know exactly where they stand.
In cases where two or more candidates score identical marks, the board applies a tie-breaking formula in the following order of priority:

items: Marks in Chemistry - The candidate with higher Chemistry marks ranks higher.
Marks in Physics - If Chemistry marks are also equal, Physics scores are compared.
Marks in Biology/Mathematics - The next tiebreaker if Physics scores are also tied.
Marks in English - Applied if the above three subjects also result in a tie.
Age - In case of a further tie, the older candidate is given the higher rank.

sections.heading: How to Calculate Marks Using HPCET 2026 Answer Key

content.text: Once the tentative answer key is downloaded, candidates can estimate their HPCET 2026 score by applying the marking scheme to their responses. The marking scheme for each paper is given in the official HPCET 2026 information brochure, and candidates must follow that pattern only.
The general process is as follows:

items: Note down the total number of questions and marks per question for your paper as mentioned in the HPCET 2026 exam pattern.
For every correct answer that matches the option given in the answer key, add the full marks allotted per question.
For every wrong answer, deduct marks as per the negative marking specified in the brochure.
No marks are added or deducted for questions which were left unanswered.
After going through all questions, total your marks to get your approximate score in HPCET 2026 for that specific course.

content.text: For example, if a paper carries 100 questions with 2 marks each and 0.5 marks negative per wrong answer, and a candidate gets 70 questions correct and 20 wrong, the estimated score will be: Correct: 70 × 2 = 140 Wrong: 20 × 0.5 = 10 (to be deducted) Estimated score = 140 − 10 = 130
This calculated score is only indicative; the final result will be based on the University’s evaluation and the final answer key.

sections.heading: HPCET 2026 Answer Key Objection Process (Tentative)

Candidates are therefore advised to carefully read the instructions provided with the HPCET 2026 answer key notice on the official website.
Typically, the objection process includes the following steps:

items: Objections must be submitted within a specified time window after the release of the tentative answer key.
Candidates have to mention the question number, booklet code, the answer given in the provisional key and the answer they believe is correct, along with supporting proof from authentic sources.
There may be an objection fee per question, which can be refunded if the challenge is found valid, depending on University rules.

content.text: After the objection window is closed, expert committees examine all challenges. Based on their recommendations, HPTU may revise the answers and publish the final answer key. The result is then prepared strictly on the basis of this final key, and further objections are normally not entertained.

content.text: This section gives users a broader picture and also helps internal linking to your exam overview pages.
HPCET 2026 Courses Offered
HPCET 2026 is conducted for admission to various undergraduate and postgraduate courses offered by Himachal Pradesh Technical University and its affiliated colleges. Major programmes include:

items: Bachelor of Technology (B.Tech)
Bachelor of Pharmacy (B.Pharmacy)

content.text: You can add internal links from each course name to your detailed course or admission pages.
Basic Eligibility for HPCET 2026 (UG & PG)
The detailed eligibility criteria are provided in the HPCET 2026 information brochure, and candidates must strictly verify them before applying. However, in broad terms:

items: For B.Tech and B.Pharmacy: Candidates must have passed 10+2 or equivalent examination from a recognised board with the required combination of subjects and minimum aggregate marks stipulated by HPTU.
For MCA, MBA, MBA (T&HM), M.Sc Physics and M.Sc Environmental Sciences: Candidates should possess a relevant bachelor’s degree with the minimum percentage specified in the prospectus.

content.text: For precise eligibility (including subject combination, age limit and relaxation details), candidates should always refer to the official HPCET 2026 prospectus available on the University website.
HPCET 2026 Exam Pattern & Marking Scheme
HPCET is conducted in offline mode as a pen‑and‑paper OMR based test. The exam pattern varies slightly from course to course, but some common features are:

items: The question paper consists of objective type multiple-choice questions.
The medium of the question paper is generally English.
Each question carries equal marks and there is negative marking for incorrect answers as per the official scheme for that particular programme.

content.text: For course-wise exam pattern, distribution of questions by subject and detailed marking scheme, candidates should check the dedicated “HPCET 2026 Exam Pattern” notification or your separate exam pattern article.

sections.heading: HPCET 2026 Result, Cut Off and Counselling (Next Steps)

content.text: This section satisfies the natural follow-up questions users have after checking the answer key.
HPCET 2026 Result Date (Expected Overview)

After the final answer key is published and the OMR sheets are evaluated, HPTU declares the HPCET 2026 result on its official website. The result link is usually made available in the “Results” or “HPCET” section, where candidates can log in and download their scorecard.

The exact date for the declaration of the HPCET 2026 result will be notified by the University through an official notice. Candidates should regularly visit the website or follow trusted education portals for timely updates.
HPCET 2026 Cut Off and Merit List
Once the results are announced, the University releases course-wise and category-wise cut off marks or merit lists. These cut offs are determined based on several factors, such as:

items: Number of candidates appearing for the exam
Total seats available in a particular course
Difficulty level of the question paper
Previous year cut-off trends and reservation norms

content.text: Candidates securing marks equal to or above the notified cut off will be considered for counselling and further admission processes.
HPCET 2026 Counselling Process (Short Summary)
Eligible candidates who qualify as per the HPCET 2026 cut off must participate in the University’s counselling process. The broad steps in counselling generally include:

items: Online registration for counselling within the stipulated dates
Payment of counselling fee (if any)
Filling and locking choices of courses and colleges
Verification of documents at designated centres or online, as per the procedure
Seat allotment based on merit, preferences and reservation policy

content.text: After seat allotment, candidates must confirm their admission by reporting to the allotted institute within the prescribed time along with original documents and fees.

sections.heading: HPCET 2026 - Eligibility Criteria

content.text: The minimum eligibility criteria for HPCET 2026 are as per AICTE/PCI/UGC norms. Candidates appearing in their final 10+2 or graduation examination in March/April 2026 are also eligible to apply, subject to fulfilling eligibility at the time of admission. Check course-wise eligibility below:

rows: 10+2 with Physics / Mathematics / Chemistry / Computer Science / Electronics / IT / Biology / Informatics Practices / Biotechnology / Technical Vocational / Agriculture / Engineering Graphics / Business Studies / Entrepreneurship. B.Sc. with Physics, Chemistry & Mathematics OR Honors in Physics. Min. 50% marks in aggregate over 3 years (45% reserved).

sections.heading: How to Apply for HPCET 2026 - Step-by-Step Guide

content.text: Applications are accepted only in online mode via the HPTU official website. Follow the steps below carefully to fill the HPCET 2026 application form without errors:

items: Visit the official HPTU website www.himtu.ac.in and navigate to the HPCET 2026 application page. Click on One Time Registration (OTR) under the "Services" section.
Click "Register →" and then "As Student". New users must click "New User? Sign up for Citizen Login".
You will be redirected to the Him Access Portal. Choose the Aadhaar number option, provide eKYC consent, enter OTP, then provide your mobile number and email to generate a unique Him Access ID.
Login "As Student" using your Him Access ID / registered mobile number or other available option.
Update your profile in four tabs: Applicant Details, Contact Details, Qualifications (10th, 12th, graduation if applicable), and Upload Photo & Signature (JPG/JPEG/PNG, 60-100 KB).
Click "Complete Profile" → Logout → Login again → navigate to "Courses List".
Under UG/PG list, click "Apply" against your desired course or combined course option (e.g., B.Tech & B.Pharmacy both, MBA & MCA, etc.).
Fill the HPCET 2026 Application Form: select quota (AIQ / HPSQ / NRI / KM), category, minimum qualification, sub-category etc. Ensure all entries match your profile/qualification details.

Tick the declaration checkbox, then click "Save Draft". Check under "My Applications", use "Edit Application" if corrections are needed, then click "Submit Application". After submission, no further edits are allowed.
Note down the Application Number (format: HPCET26XXXXXX) displayed on screen. Go to "My Applications" → click "₹ Pay XXXX" → Proceed to Payment and complete the fee payment via the payment gateway.

After successful payment, download and print the application form PDF. If the PDF icon does not appear, click the payment button again to refresh payment status. If not generated within 2 working days, email: [email protected] with your Form Number, transaction ID, and payment screenshot.

items: Recent passport-size photograph (JPG/JPEG/PNG, 60-100 KB)
Candidate's signature in prescribed format (JPG/JPEG/PNG, 60-100 KB)
Aadhaar Card (for Him Access Portal registration)
Class 10 (Matric) mark sheet and certificate
Class 12 (10+2) mark sheet and certificate
Graduation degree mark sheet (for PG course applicants - MCA, MBA, M.Sc.)
Caste/Category certificate - SC/ST/OBC/EWS (if applicable)
BPL certificate (if claiming BPL fee concession)
Valid photo ID proof (Aadhaar/Voter ID/Passport)

sections.heading: HPCET 2026 - Exam Pattern (Course-wise)

content.text: HPCET 2026 is conducted in offline (OMR-based) mode in English language. The exam pattern varies by course. There is negative marking in all courses. Refer to the course-wise patterns below:
1. B.Tech & B.Pharmacy (Allopathy) - Direct Entry
Duration: 3 Hours 15 Minutes | Marking: +4 for correct, −1 for wrong, 0 for unattempted. In Section B, if more than 30 questions are attempted, only the first 30 are evaluated.
2. B.Sc. (HM&CT) / BHMCT
Duration: 2 Hours | Marking: +1 for correct, −0.25 for wrong, 0 for unattempted.
3. MBA / MBA (T&HM) / MCA
Duration: 2 Hours | Marking: +4 for correct, −1 for wrong, 0 for unattempted.
4. M.Sc. Physics

rows: Mathematical Methods, Classical Mechanics & General Properties of Matter
Atomic & Molecular Physics, KTG & Thermodynamics, Solid State & Electronics

content.text: Duration: 2 Hours | Marking: +1 for correct, −0.25 for wrong, 0 for unattempted.
5. M.Sc. Environmental Sciences
Duration: 2 Hours | Marking: +1 for correct, −0.25 for wrong, 0 for unattempted.

content.text: The HPCET 2026 Result is tentatively expected by 21 May 2026 on the official HPTU website. detail.title: Ladakh MBBS BDS Admission 2026 - Overview
detail.short_info: Ladakh's Health & Medical Education Department has revised the Central Pool MBBS and BDS admission guidelines for 2026-27, replacing the old category-wise roster with a single NEET merit list.

content.text: The Health & Medical Education (H&ME) Department, Union Territory of Ladakh, issued revised guidelines on September 22, 2026, for admission to MBBS and BDS seats under the Central Pool. The revision replaces the existing category-wise roster system with a single merit list based purely on NEET ranking. The change was made following the creation of seven new districts in Ladakh and was approved by Lieutenant Governor V K Saxena. For the 2026-27 academic session, the Centre has allotted 7 MBBS seats and 2 BDS seats to Ladakh under the Central Pool.

sections.heading: How to Apply for IUST B.Sc Nursing Admission 2026 (Step-by-Step)

items: Visit the official website www.iust.ac.in and click the "Admissions 2026" link. Register as a new user or log in if already registered.

Enter personal details exactly as per your Matriculation Certificate, and verify your phone number/email ID using the verification code sent to your registered mobile number. Note down your login ID (it will also be sent to your registered email).

sections.heading: Important Instructions

items: Admission Guidelines 2026 can be viewed/downloaded from www.iust.ac.in.
Application fee (Rs. 500, plus Rs. 200 per extra programme) is non-refundable and payable online only.

Any immoral or irrelevant content uploaded on the online application form will invite strict action under university rules.
Applications with missing documents or unpaid prescribed fee will be rejected.

Currently admitted Nursing/Paramedical students at IUST or its constituent colleges seeking a college change or course upgradation must report in person, with original documents, on or before 18-09-2026 - subject to seat availability, merit, and eligibility.
Only J&K UT domiciles are eligible for these leftover seats.

sections.heading: JKBOSE Revaluation Result 2026 - Key Highlights

content.text: This section provides a quick snapshot of the most important details related to the JKBOSE 10th and 12th Revaluation Result 2026, so students can immediately identify what applies to them.
Register for Job Alerts

sections.heading: What Is the JKBOSE Revaluation Result 2026?

content.text: The revaluation result is one of the most awaited post-declaration updates for students who were not satisfied with their original marks.

After the declaration of the JKBOSE Annual Regular Results 2026, students who were dissatisfied with their scores were given an opportunity to apply for re-evaluation of their answer scripts. During the re-evaluation process, qualified examiners re-assess the answer sheets independently to ensure no marks were missed or incorrectly totalled. The JKBOSE Revaluation Result 2026, released on 26 June 2026, reflects the outcome of this process - listing roll numbers whose results have been amended, revised, or newly declared after the re-assessment.
Important: The result declared after re-evaluation is final and binding. No further changes will be made after this notification is issued.

sections.heading: Direct PDF Download Links - JKBOSE Revaluation Result 2026

content.text: Students can access the official re-evaluation result PDFs directly from the JKBOSE portal. Use the direct links below to download the relevant notification.

items: Class 12th (HSP-II) Re-Evaluation Result - Notification No. 90 (Dated: 26-06-2026) Exam: Annual Regular 2026 (26AJTR), Jammu Division Download: Click Here
Class 10th (SSE) Re-Evaluation Result - Notification No. 90 (Dated: 26-06-2026) Exam: Annual Regular (Feb–March) 2026, Jammu Division Download: Click Here

content.text: If the direct PDF links are slow to load due to high traffic, students are advised to visit the official JKBOSE homepage at jkbose.jk.gov.in or jkbose.ac.in and navigate to the Notifications section.

sections.heading: How to Check JKBOSE Revaluation Result 2026 - Step-by-Step

content.text: Finding your result in the revaluation PDF is straightforward. Here is the complete process for Class 10th and Class 12th students.
Step 1: Click on the relevant direct PDF download link provided above (Class 10th or Class 12th).
Step 2: Open the downloaded PDF on your device. Use Ctrl+F (Windows) or Cmd+F (Mac/mobile search) to open the search function.
Step 3: Type your Roll Number in the search box and press Enter.

Step 4: Check the entry against your roll number carefully. Verify whether your result has been amended (marks changed), revised (result status updated), or declared (result published for the first time after re-evaluation).
Step 5: Take a screenshot or print a copy of the relevant page for future academic and administrative reference.
Step 6: If you find any genuine discrepancy or your roll number does not appear despite having applied for re-evaluation, contact JKBOSE directly through official channels.

sections.heading: Who Can Check This Revaluation Result?

content.text: Not every JKBOSE student is covered by this notification. Understanding eligibility helps avoid confusion.
The JKBOSE Revaluation Result Notification No. 90 dated 26 June 2026 is specifically applicable to:

items: Class 12th (HSP-II) students who appeared in the Annual Regular Examination 2026 (26AJTR) of Jammu Division and had submitted valid re-evaluation applications.
Class 10th (SSE) students who appeared in the Annual Regular (Feb–March) Examination 2026 of Jammu Division and had applied for revaluation of their answer scripts.

content.text: Students from Kashmir Division, Private, or Bi-Annual sessions should look for separate notifications on the official JKBOSE portal, as those results are issued under distinct gazette numbers.

sections.heading: What Happens After the Revaluation Result?

content.text: Understanding the next steps after the revaluation outcome is crucial for students planning their academic future.
Once the JKBOSE Revaluation Result 2026 is out, here is what students should do based on their updated result status:

items: If marks increased and you now pass: Collect your revised mark sheet from your school or JKBOSE office once it is issued. You can use this to apply for college admissions or other academic processes.

If result is unchanged or marks decrease: The re-evaluation result is final. Students who still do not meet passing criteria may consider appearing in the JKBOSE Supplementary / Part-II Examination 2026.

If result was freshly declared: Some students whose results were previously withheld may now see a result declared for the first time. These students should follow up with their school or JKBOSE for the formal mark sheet.

content.text: It is worth noting that students are required to obtain 36 marks out of 100 marks in each paper - including theory and practical marks - to pass the JKBOSE 12th exam.

sections.heading: JKBOSE Part-II / Supplementary Exam 2026

content.text: For students who remain unsuccessful even after revaluation, the upcoming Part-II examination is a vital second chance.

JKBOSE will conduct the Class 10th and 12th Part-II exams starting from June 27. The exam for Class 10 will run from June 27 to July 20, 2026. The JKBOSE 12th HSP Part-II will also be held on the same dates. Students who did not clear their original exams or remain unsatisfied with the revaluation outcome are encouraged to appear in these exams to save their academic year.

sections.heading: How to Complete Kerala PG Dental Admission 2026 Option Entry?

content.text: The earlier Round 3 option registration window ended on 12 October 2026. The following steps explain the procedure prescribed in the official notification for that window.

items: Visit the official website at cee.kerala.gov.in.
Open the PG Dental 2026 Candidate Portal.
Enter the application number and password to log in.
Select the Option Registration menu.
Choose the preferred MDS courses and dental colleges.
Arrange the options according to admission preference.
Pay the applicable option registration fee.
Complete the option registration process within the prescribed deadline.

sections.heading: Important Instructions

items: Check the deadline first. Log in to the “PG Dental 2026 - Candidate Portal” with your application number and password, then open “Option Registration”. Confirm the current closing date and time on the CEE notification, because deadlines are often extended.

Fresh options need a fresh fee. Fresh option registration is available in the third (final) round, but with a fresh option registration fee. Earlier-round fees are forfeited if you were allotted a seat in Round 2 and did not report, did not join, or quit after joining.

Fill options in strict order of preference. Choose course and college combinations carefully. Allotment follows your rank, category and the order of your list, so put your most-wanted choices first and don’t add colleges you wouldn’t join.
Save and confirm your list. Unconfirmed or unsaved options may not be considered. Take a printout or screenshot of the final list.

Prepare to join if allotted. Download the allotment memo, pay the fee or balance fee, and report to the college within the joining dates. Keep your original documents ready, including your Kerala State Dental Council registration, as admission requires the original.

sections.heading: Provisional vs Final Round 3 Allotment: What Is the Difference?

content.text: The provisional list was published first so that candidates could review it and raise grievances, where applicable. The final list follows after those grievances are looked at. Do not treat the provisional list as confirmation of admission. Check the final list before you pay fees or travel to a college.

sections.heading: What Details Are Given in the Allotment List?

items: Application number or other candidate identifier
Rank or merit information, where provided
Allotted college
Allotted course (MBBS or BDS)
Allotment status and related remarks

content.text: The exact columns in the PDF may differ. Read the notes at the top of the document.

sections.heading: Documents Required for MBBS and BDS Admission in Kerala

content.text: The official admission instructions give the final list. Candidates should keep these ready, as reported:

items: NEET UG 2026 scorecard and admit card
CEE Kerala allotment letter
Class 10 certificate or marksheet, where required
Class 12 marksheet and qualifying certificate
Transfer certificate
Valid identity proof
Category, reservation or other supporting certificates, if applicable
Any other document listed in the official notification

sections.heading: What to Do After the Round 3 Result

items: Check the final allotment list once it is published.
Download and save your allotment letter and read its instructions.
Pay the prescribed fee through the authorised method before the deadline. According to the Phase 3 notification coverage, allottees at government colleges pay the full fee to CEE.
Prepare your original documents and photocopies.
Report to the allotted college and complete admission within the joining period.

sections.heading: Important Instructions for Round 3 Candidates

items: Joining is compulsory. According to the notification coverage, a candidate who is allotted a seat in this phase and does not join by the prescribed date loses the allotment from the previous phase, the allotment in this phase and all options in that stream.
Fresh options were required. Every candidate wanting to be considered in Phase 3, including those already holding a Phase 1 or Phase 2 allotment or admission, had to register options again.
Unallotted category seats are converted in this phase under the prospectus conditions.

MCC cross-checks apply. If MCC declares candidates allotted or admitted in its Round 3 ineligible for state Round 3 counselling and shares their list, their options will not be considered in this phase.
Do not rely on social media for deadlines. Use only the official CEE Kerala website.

sections.heading: MPMSU Re-Verification 2026: How to Apply Online

content.text: The university has attached a Re-Verification user manual to the notification. It covers the online process for applying for re-verification of answer scripts. The steps below follow that manual.

sections.heading: Login Details for the Re-Verification Form

items: Login URL: mpmsu.intelliexams.com
User ID: Enrolment Number
Password: Date of Birth in DD/MM/YYYY format, or 123456

sections.heading: Step-by-Step Re-Verification Process

items: Open the login URL and click the Student Login option on the home page.
Enter your Enrolment No. and Password, then click Enter. If you forget the password, use the "Forgot Password?" link on the login page.
After logging in, open the Student Login menu and click Online Reverification Application Entry.
Your enrolment number and college name will appear automatically. Click View.
The application form will show your name, email ID, mobile number, exam series, degree, branch, semester or year, and apply type (Reverification). Check the details and click View again.
The list of subjects will appear. Select the subject or subjects for which you want re-verification.
Check the payment mode (online payment) and the fee amount shown on the screen, then click Submit.
You will be directed to the online payment gateway. Complete the payment to finish the application.

sections.heading: Important Instructions for Students

items: Use only the official links given in the notification to view results and apply for re-verification.
Keep your enrolment number and date of birth ready before logging in.
Check your name, exam series, degree, branch and year carefully on the re-verification form before submitting.
Complete the payment in the same session, and use "Online transaction status" to confirm it.
Download or reprint your application after submission for your records.

sections.heading: MP NEET UG Counselling 2026 - Seat Allotment Process

items: DME publishes the revised merit list and eligible candidates list for Round 2.
Eligible candidates complete fresh choice filling of colleges/courses in order of preference.
Candidates lock their choices before the deadline (locking cannot be changed afterward).
DME processes seat allotment based on NEET UG 2026 rank, category, locked choices, seat availability, and Madhya Pradesh's reservation policy.
The Round 2 seat allotment result is published on the official portal.
Allotted candidates report to the respective medical/dental college in person for document verification and admission within the notified reporting window.

sections.heading: How to Apply for MP NEET UG Counselling 2026 Round 2

items: Visit the official DME Madhya Pradesh counselling portal, dme.mponline.gov.in.
Click on the link for "NEET UG Counselling 2026 - Round 2 Registration" (for fresh candidates) or the registration edit option, as applicable.
Enter your NEET UG 2026 details, including roll number, application number, date of birth, and personal information.
Pay the applicable counselling registration fee and security deposit online using net banking, debit card, credit card, or UPI.
Upload scanned copies of the required documents - NEET UG 2026 scorecard, Class 10 and 12 marksheets, domicile certificate, category certificate (if applicable), and photo ID.
Complete e-verification or physical verification of documents, as required by DME.
Once the merit list is published, log in again to complete fresh choice filling and lock your preferred colleges/courses before the deadline.
Download and save a copy of the submitted registration form and payment receipt for future reference.

sections.heading: Important Instructions for Candidates

items: Round 1-registered candidates should not attempt a duplicate fresh registration; only fresh choice filling is required from them for Round 2.
Fresh choice filling and locking is compulsory for all candidates participating in Round 2, including Round 1-admitted candidates who have opted for upgradation.
Choices filled and locked in Round 1 will not automatically carry forward; they must be filled afresh for Round 2.
Keep scanned copies of all documents ready in the prescribed format and size before starting registration.
Regularly check the official DME MP portal for corrigenda, as the post-registration schedule (merit list, choice filling, allotment) is tentative and subject to change.
A seat once allotted and accepted is generally binding as per DME's seat-leaving/ resignation rules; check the bond and resignation policy before deciding to upgrade.

What Is the MP ITI Trade-Wise Merit List?

content.text: The trade-wise merit list is a rank list published separately for each trade offered across participating ITIs in Madhya Pradesh. Instead of one combined list for all trades, candidates are ranked within the specific trade(s) they applied for, based on their qualifying exam marks. This helps candidates see exactly where they stand for a particular trade at a particular institute before choice filling or seat acceptance.

items: Visit the official IIT Bombay Academic Office website: acad.iitb.ac.in/academics/calendar-and-timetable.
Look for the link titled "Mid-Semester Examination Timetable for Autumn 2026-2027 (Revised)" on the Calendar and Timetable page.
Open the linked PDF/notice to view the full paper-wise timetable, which remains the same as originally published.
Cross-check your course codes and slot timings against this revised document, and note that only the calendar dates (October 10 and 11) have changed, not the slot structure.
Check your institute email and department notice board as well, since departments may circulate the same information directly to students.

sections.heading: Important Instructions for Students

items: The mid-semester exams will be held on Saturday, October 10, and Sunday, October 11, 2026, in place of the earlier September 26-27 dates.
The timetable has not changed - students should appear for the same papers, in the same sequence, as per the original schedule, only on the new dates.

A new committee with equal student representation is preparing a revised Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for invigilators and updated academic misconduct rules; these will be placed before the Senate for approval before being implemented.
Student stakeholders were consulted before the postponement was finalised, as per the official communication.

Specific instructions on reporting time, permitted materials, seating arrangements, or ID requirements for the revised dates have not been separately detailed in the available official communication. Students should rely on their department/course instructor and the Academic Office for any such logistical details closer to the exam dates.
Students are advised to keep checking official IIT Bombay channels (Academic Office website and institute email) for the approved SOP and any further notices before October 10.

content.text: Nagaland University, the only Central University in Nagaland, has opened undergraduate admissions for the 2026-27 academic session under its Four-Year Undergraduate Programme (FYUGP) in B.Sc. Honours and B.Sc. Honours with Research. Admission is based on CUET-UG 2026 scores combined with Class XII marks, and eligible candidates can apply online at admission.nagalanduniversity.ac.in until 15th July 2026.

This guide covers everything applicants need to know eligibility, courses on offer, the full admission timeline, required documents, reservation categories, and how to apply, based entirely on the university's official admission notice.

links.text: Nagaland University FYUGP Admission 2026

sections.heading: Nagaland University FYUGP Admission 2026 - Key Highlights

content.text: Here's a quick snapshot of the admission cycle for candidates who want the essential facts at a glance before reading the detailed sections below.

rows: Four-Year Undergraduate Programme (FYUGP) – B.Sc. Honours / Honours with Research

content.text: Register for Job Alerts

sections.heading: Courses Offered Under FYUGP 2026

content.text: Applicants often want to know exactly which subjects and programme formats are available before applying. Here is what Nagaland University is offering this year.

The admissions are conducted by the University's Multi-Disciplinary Research Centre (MDRC) in accordance with the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 framework. Under this framework, the undergraduate programme offers students the flexibility to pursue Honours and Honours with Research programmes in five science disciplines Botany, Chemistry, Mathematics, Physics, and Zoology.

sections.heading: Disciplines available under FYUGP B.Sc.:

items: Botany
Chemistry
Mathematics
Physics
Zoology

content.text: Students can choose either the standard Honours track or the research-intensive Honours with Research track in any of these five subjects, in line with the NEP 2020 multidisciplinary model.

sections.heading: Eligibility Criteria for Nagaland University UG Admission 2026

content.text: Before applying, candidates should understand how selection works, since Nagaland University does not rely on Class XII marks alone.

Admissions will be granted strictly on merit based on candidates' CUET-UG scores and Class XII examination performance, as per the eligibility criteria prescribed by the respective academic departments. This means:

items: Candidates must have appeared for CUET-UG 2026 in the relevant subject combination.
Final merit is a combination of the CUET-UG score and Class XII marks.
Department-specific eligibility norms (such as required subjects in Class XII) apply, so applicants should check the specific requirements for their chosen discipline on the official portal.

sections.heading: Nagaland University UG Admission 2026: Important Dates

content.text: Timing matters a great deal in this admission cycle, as the entire process from application to final seat allotment runs on a tight schedule. The section below lays out every key date candidates need to track.

Applications are open till 15th July 2026 for FYUGP B.Sc. Honours and Honours with Research programmes. The University will publish the list of shortlisted candidates on 16th July 2026, while admissions for selected candidates will be conducted from 17th July to 20th July 2026. Admissions from the waiting list are scheduled from 21st July to 23rd July 2026.
Candidates are advised to keep checking the official admission portal regularly, as revised or extended dates (if any) are typically notified there first.

sections.heading: How to Apply for Nagaland University FYUGP Admission 2026

content.text: Applicants naturally want a simple, step-by-step way to submit their application without missing any part of the process. Here's how it works.
Interested candidates can submit their applications through the University's admission portal at admission.nagalanduniversity.ac.in. The general process is as follows:

items: Visit the official admission portal: admission.nagalanduniversity.ac.in
Register with basic personal details to create a login.
Log in and select the FYUGP B.Sc. Honours/Honours with Research programme.
Choose your preferred discipline (Botany, Chemistry, Mathematics, Physics, or Zoology).
Fill in academic details, including Class X and Class XII information and CUET-UG scorecard details.
Upload the required documents (see checklist below).
Review the form carefully before final submission, as incomplete or incorrect forms may be rejected.
Submit the application within the deadline of 15th July 2026.

sections.heading: Documents Required for Application

content.text: Missing or incorrect documents are one of the most common reasons applications get delayed or rejected, so it's worth checking this list closely before starting the form.

Applicants are required to submit a recent passport-size photograph and signature, Class X admit card and marksheet, Class XII admit card and marksheet, CUET scorecard, transfer certificate, and other applicable documents such as caste, disability, backward tribe, or gap certificates, wherever relevant.

sections.heading: Document checklist:

items: Recent passport-size photograph
Signature (scanned copy)
Class X admit card and marksheet
Class XII admit card and marksheet
CUET-UG scorecard
Transfer certificate
Caste certificate (if applicable)
Disability certificate (if applicable)
Backward tribe certificate (if applicable)
Gap certificate (if applicable)

sections.heading: Reservation Categories and Seat Allocation

content.text: Reservation norms directly affect how seats are distributed, so candidates belonging to specific categories should know exactly where they stand in the process.

Seat allocation will be carried out in accordance with the norms and reservation guidelines of Nagaland University under categories including Scheduled Tribe (ST), Scheduled Caste (SC), Other Backward Classes (OBC), Persons with Disabilities (PwD), Economically Weaker Sections (EWS), Sports Quota, Employees' Quota, and Unreserved (UR).

sections.heading: Campus Facilities for FYUGP Students

content.text: Beyond academics, prospective students and parents often want to know what kind of campus life and support infrastructure to expect at Nagaland University.

Students admitted to the programme will have access to well-equipped laboratories, digital library resources, Wi-Fi-enabled campus facilities, e-learning support, sports infrastructure, career counselling and placement assistance, as well as on-campus cafeteria and health centre facilities.

sections.heading: Key facilities include:

items: Well-equipped science laboratories
Digital library resources
Wi-Fi-enabled campus
E-learning support
Sports infrastructure
Career counselling and placement assistance
On-campus cafeteria
Health centre

sections.heading: What the Vice Chancellor Says About FYUGP 2026

content.text: University leadership statements often clarify the intent and vision behind a new admission cycle, which can help applicants understand what the programme is designed to deliver.

Welcoming applicants to the programme, Prof. Jagadish K Patnaik, Vice Chancellor of Nagaland University, invited students from across India to join the university, noting its status as the only Central University in the State of Nagaland and highlighting the implementation of FYUGP under NEP 2020 to provide a multidisciplinary, research-oriented, and student-centric learning environment. He further described admission through CUET-UG 2026 as ensuring a transparent, fair, and merit-based process that enables talented students from across the country to join the university's academic community, with B.Sc. Honours and Honours with Research programmes combining rigorous academic training with hands-on research, innovation, and skill development.

content.text: Candidates who run into issues while filling the form or have questions about eligibility should reach out directly to the department handling this admission cycle.

sections.heading: What Happens After the Odisha D.El.Ed Result: Counselling Process

content.text: Once the merit list and cut-off marks are released, SCERT Odisha is expected to conduct counselling and seat allotment for admission into the two-year D.El.Ed programme. Based on how this process is generally run for SAMS Odisha admissions, it typically includes:

items: Counselling Registration: Eligible candidates register for counselling on scert.samsodisha.gov.in during the notified window.
Choice Filling: Candidates fill and lock their preferred DIETs, BIETs, or ETEIs (teacher training institutes) in order of preference.
Seat Allotment: Seats are allotted based on rank, category, and choices filled.

items: MSP applicants from the Puducherry region must hand-deliver self-attested copies of sports certificates, along with a copy of the application, at the CENTAC office, Kamarajar Manimandapam, by 6 August 2026, 5:00 PM.
MSP candidates from Karaikal, Mahe, and Yanam must upload a single self-attested PDF through their login dashboard by the same deadline.

sections.heading: Puducherry NEET UG 2026: Topper Details

content.text: Krishanth Abhinav M topped the Union Territory of Puducherry in the Re-NEET UG 2026 result, securing All India Rank (AIR) 553 with a percentile of 99.9721, as reported by exam-tracking sources including Aakash Institute and Daily Jagran.

Source conflict note: Moneycontrol has separately reported that the Puducherry topper scored 670 marks. This specific marks figure could not be independently cross-verified against a second source at the time of writing, so it is presented here as reported by Moneycontrol rather than as a confirmed official figure. Candidates should treat the AIR/percentile (cross-verified across two sources) as more reliable than the marks figure until the official NTA scorecard or CENTAC records are checked directly.

sections.heading: What Is the CENTAC Draft Merit List 2026?

content.text: This section explains what the draft merit list is and why it matters to applicants.

The draft merit list is a preliminary ranking of candidates who applied for UG Non-NEET admission through CENTAC for the academic year 2026-2027. It is published before the final merit list so that candidates get an opportunity to verify their rank and details, and raise objections if there are discrepancies. sections.heading: Why the Draft Merit List Matters Before Final Counselling

content.text: This section explains the purpose of releasing a draft list before the final merit list and counselling process.

Publishing a draft list before finalising admissions ensures transparency and fairness in the selection process. It gives every applicant a chance to verify their marks, category, and rank, and to flag any clerical or technical errors before they affect final seat allotment. Once objections are reviewed, CENTAC will release the final merit list, which will then be used for the counselling and seat allotment process for UG Non-NEET admissions 2026-2027 in Puducherry colleges.

content.text: Candidates preparing for Round 3 counselling should keep the following dates in mind:

items: September 21, 2026: Last date for Round 1/Round 2 admitted candidates to surrender their seats at the respective college.
September 22, 2026: BFUHS Punjab B.Sc Nursing Round 3 seat matrix release date.

sections.heading: How to Fill BFUHS Round 3 Choices

content.text: While the complete step-by-step choice-filling process was not detailed in the official notification, candidates are generally expected to:

items: Visit the official BFUHS admission portal, admission.bfuhsonline.ac.in.
Log in using their PPMET 2026 counselling credentials.
Refer to the released Round 3 seat matrix PDF for available colleges, categories, and quotas.
Arrange and submit college, category, and quota preferences in order of priority.
Submit choices before the last date, September 23, 2026.

sections.heading: Important Instructions

items: Review the Round 3 seat matrix carefully for preferred colleges, categories, and quotas before entering choices.

Do not restrict choices only to seats listed in the matrix. BFUHS has previously stated that candidates may submit preferences for colleges even when a particular seat is not reflected in the tentative vacancy position.
Arrange college, category, and quota preferences carefully before final submission.
A candidate already holding a seat from Round 1 or Round 2 may participate in Round 3 if eligible for upgradation. Such movement can create fresh vacancies at other colleges.
Candidates who receive a Round 3 allotment should be prepared for document verification, eligibility checking, medical formalities, and fee payment within the prescribed timeline.

A vacancy shown under one category or quota does not automatically mean the same seat is available under another category. Candidates should verify the exact classification before submitting preferences.

rows: Verifying that every answer has been evaluated, marks are correctly totalled and carried forward to the main sheet, and no question has been left unchecked. The actual answers are not re-assessed.

items: PSEB re-checks or re-evaluates the answer script as per the option chosen.

sections.heading: Quota & Seat Distribution

content.text: Admissions to MBBS and BDS seats in Punjab are conducted under three categories of quota, all counselled centrally by BFUHS (except the All India Quota, which is filled separately by the Medical Counselling Committee):

items: 85% State Quota - for candidates who meet Punjab domicile/residency requirements, filled through BFUHS counselling.
Management Quota - offered by participating private colleges as per the BFUHS counselling prospectus; government medical/dental colleges do not offer management quota seats.
NRI Quota - for NRI-sponsored candidates, as per prospectus rules.
15% All India Quota (AIQ) - filled separately by MCC, not through BFUHS.

content.text: Reported figures for the 2026 cycle put the number of MBBS and BDS seats available under BFUHS Punjab counselling at approximately 1,750 MBBS seats and 1,260 BDS seats; candidates should confirm the exact, category-wise seat matrix from the official seat matrix released at the time of choice filling, since this is not stated in the merit list PDF itself.

sections.heading: Application Fee
How to Check Your Name and Rank in the BFUHS Merit List

items: Open the official Provisional Combined Merit List PDF using the link in the Important Links section below.
Since the document runs across many pages, use your browser or PDF reader's search function (Ctrl+F on Windows, Cmd+F on Mac) once the file is open.
Search using your NEET Roll Number or your full name exactly as it appears on your NEET UG application.
Note your Merit Number, NEET Rank, and Eligibility status for 85% State Quota seats shown against your entry.
Cross-check your NEET Marks and NEET Rank in the list against your official NEET UG 2026 scorecard to confirm accuracy.

If any detail appears incorrect, follow the official objection process by appearing in person at the Admission Branch, BFUHS, Faridkot, within the specified objection window - objections are not accepted online.

sections.heading: How to Apply for Round 1 Choice Filling

items: Log in to the BFUHS admission portal using your registered credentials.
Check the official seat matrix released for Round 1.
Arrange your preferred colleges and courses in order of priority during the choice-filling window.
Lock your choices before the deadline; unlocked or unsubmitted choices may not be considered.
Wait for the provisional seat allotment result on the scheduled date.
If allotted a seat, report to the college in person within the reporting window with all original documents.

sections.heading: Important Instructions

items: This is a provisional merit list - it is subject to change after the objection window and verification.
Objections to the merit list or seat allotment are accepted only through personal appearance at the Admission Branch, BFUHS, Faridkot, and not through email, phone, or online submission.
Use only the official BFUHS portal for registration, choice filling, and fee payment; avoid third-party links.
Failure to report to the allotted college within the prescribed dates may lead to cancellation of the allotted seat.
All admissions are strictly based on NEET UG 2026 merit - there is no separate entrance test or interview.
Always cross-verify counselling dates on the official BFUHS website, as schedules are subject to revision by the university.

sections.heading: How the BITSAT Iteration System Works

content.text: BITSAT admissions run through a multi-round, portal-based iteration system rather than a single seat allotment. Candidates register once, submit ranked programme-and-campus preferences, and the system allots and upgrades seats automatically across rounds as other candidates withdraw, freeze, or float their offers.

items: Iteration IV allots seats that became free after candidates withdrew or upgraded during the Iteration 3 withdrawal window.
Candidates already holding a seat from an earlier iteration may be automatically upgraded if a higher-preference option opens up.
No category-based reservation applies; allotment is purely merit-based on BITSAT score, Class 12 performance, and stated preferences.
BITS Pilani conducts up to six or seven iterations in a typical year, depending on vacancy movement.

sections.heading: Seat Categories You May See in the Iteration IV Result

rows: Candidate receives a seat for the first time in this round.
Candidate already had a seat from an earlier iteration and has now moved to a higher preference.
Candidate's previous allotment remains unchanged in this round.
Candidate has not yet received an allotment but remains in contention for later iterations.

sections.heading: Selection and Allotment Process

items: BITS Pilani compiles the pool of seats vacated after the Iteration 3 withdrawal window (July 19-20, 2026).
The system matches remaining/waitlisted candidates to available seats based on BITSAT score and stated preference order.
Candidates are shown as Fresh Allotment, Upgraded, Retained, or Waiting List on the portal.
Candidates with a new or upgraded seat must accept it, choose Freeze/Float, and pay the fee within the stipulated window.
Those who Freeze must physically report to their allotted campus with original documents; those who Float wait for the next iteration's result before a reporting schedule is issued.
Failure to pay the fee or report within the deadline results in automatic cancellation of the allotted seat.

sections.heading: How to Check the BITSAT 2026 Iteration IV Result (Once Released)

items: Visit the official BITS admission portal: admissions.bits-pilani.ac.in.
Look for the "Iteration IV Result" or "Iteration Result" notice/link once activated.
Log in using your application number and the fresh password/credentials sent to your registered email.
View your allotment status: Fresh Allotment, Upgraded, Retained, or Waiting List.
Download and save the provisional allotment letter for your records.
If allotted a seat, proceed to accept it, select Freeze or Float, and complete fee payment within the deadline shown.

sections.heading: What To Do While You Wait for the Result

items: Keep monitoring the official portal and your registered email regularly; BITS Pilani typically notifies candidates directly once results go live.
Avoid relying on unofficial "result out" claims from social media or unverified pages - check only the official portal or verified news trackers.
Keep your original documents, fee payment method, and login credentials ready so you can act immediately once the result is released, given the historically short acceptance windows.
If you are relying on the Iteration IV outcome to plan travel for campus reporting, hold off on finalising travel until the result and a confirmed reporting date are announced.

content.text: The Joint Seat Allocation Authority provides the official opening and closing ranks for engineering admissions. Candidates can check the NIT Trichy Computer Science and Engineering cutoff using the JoSAA 2026 rank portal.

items: Visit the official website at josaa.nic.in.

sections.heading: Important Instructions

items: Other State (OS) quota: For General-category OS, Round 1 of 2026 (13 June) closed at rank 1,317, and the final-round 2025 closing rank was 1,449. That makes it one of the toughest NIT CSE seats.

Home State (Tamil Nadu) quota: One report puts the Round 5 closing rank at 4,015 for home state and 1,373 for other state. Round 4 CSE is listed at 1034 to 3812. Home State ranks are much more relaxed than OS ranks.

Check the quota and category: The cutoff differs by quota (HS or OS), category (General, OBC-NCL, SC, ST, EWS) and gender seat type. JoSAA publishes separate opening and closing ranks for each category, so compare yourself against the right row.
Rank and percentile: CSE at OS generally needs a General rank under about 1,500. This is a rough guide, since the final cutoff is only set by the round-wise counselling outcome.

Verify on the official portal: Third-party reporting of final-round figures has been inconsistent, so verify them on the JoSAA OR-CR portal at josaa.nic.in. I couldn’t confirm an official 2026 final-round figure, and some sites mix 2025 and 2026 data.

sections.heading: How TNEA Supplementary Counselling Allotment Works

items: Eligible candidates register and pay the applicable fee for the supplementary round.
DoTE publishes the supplementary rank list based on candidates' marks and category.
Candidates fill their college and course choices online during the choice-filling window.
A tentative seat allotment is generated based on rank, choices filled, category, and seat availability, followed by a confirmation window.
The provisional seat allotment is then released, which candidates can accept, decline, or (where applicable) opt for upward movement.
Candidates who accept the seat must report to the allotted institution and complete admission formalities within the specified deadline.

sections.heading: TNEA Supplementary Counselling 2026 Provisional Allotment Result: How to Check and Download

content.text: Follow these steps to check and download the TNEA supplementary counselling provisional allotment result 2026:

items: Visit the official TNEA website at tneaonline.org or the supplementary counselling portal.
Click on the link for "TNEA Supplementary Counselling 2026 Provisional Seat Allotment Result."
Log in using your registered email ID and password.
Your allotted college and course details will be displayed on the screen.
Review the allotment carefully, including college name, branch, and category under which the seat has been allotted.
Choose the applicable option: accept the seat, accept with upward movement (if offered), or decline.
Download and save the provisional allotment letter for future reference.
Proceed to pay the requisite admission fee, if applicable, and report to the allotted institution within the given deadline.

sections.heading: Important Instructions for Candidates

items: Log in only through the official tneaonline.org or suppl.tneaonline.org portals; be cautious of unofficial third-party links claiming to show results.
Confirm the allotment within the deadline specified on the portal, as failure to do so can lead to cancellation of the allotted seat.
Keep original documents ready for verification at the time of reporting to the college.
Candidates who are not allotted a seat, or who decline their allotment, may be eligible for a refund of the initial deposit as per TNEA's standard refund procedure.
Keep checking the official website regularly, as DoTE may update dates or issue further instructions for subsequent counselling activities, including SCA to SC counselling.

content.text: The Directorate of Government Examinations (DGE), Tamil Nadu, conducts a re-totaling and revaluation process for students who are not satisfied with their marks in the TN HSE (+1 and +2) Supplementary Examination 2026. sections.heading: Quick Overview - TN HSE Supplementary Re-totaling and Revaluation Results 2026

items: Conducting Body: Directorate of Government Examinations (DGE), Tamil Nadu

sections.heading: What Is TN HSE Re-totaling and Revaluation?

content.text: Students who are not satisfied with their marks in the TN HSE Supplementary Result 2026 can apply for a review of their answer scripts. DGE Tamil Nadu offers two separate options, and a candidate can choose only one of them per subject:

items: Re-totaling: The examiner's addition of marks is rechecked to confirm the total was calculated correctly. Answers are not re-evaluated for correctness only the arithmetic is verified.
Revaluation: The answer script is reassessed to check whether all answers were evaluated and marks awarded correctly, including any previously unchecked or unmarked answers.

content.text: To apply for either process, students must first obtain a scanned copy of their evaluated answer script.

Collect your updated original marksheet from your respective school after the result is declared.

sections.heading: How to Apply for Re-totaling or Revaluation

items: Apply for a scanned copy of your answer script at the designated government examination centre or through the official website, as instructed in the notification.
Review the scanned copy to check the examiner's evaluation and marks awarded.
If you wish to proceed, submit the re-totaling or revaluation application (choose only one per subject) along with the prescribed fee within the window announced by DGE Tamil Nadu.
Retain the application receipt/acknowledgment for future reference.
Wait for the official result declaration on the DGE Tamil Nadu website.

sections.heading: Documents/Details You May Need

items: Registration number
Date of birth
TN HSE Supplementary provisional marksheet
Scanned copy application receipt (required before applying for re-totaling/revaluation)
Fee payment proof

sections.heading: Important Instructions

items: The result available online is provisional. Students must collect the original updated marksheet from their respective schools.
In case of any discrepancy in marks, name, or registration details, contact your school or the concerned District Educational Officer immediately.
Keep the registration number and date of birth ready in advance to avoid delays, especially given expected heavy website traffic right after the result is announced.
A candidate can choose either re-totaling or revaluation for a subject not both.
Regularly check the official DGE Tamil Nadu website for the latest press releases, as exact dates for the re-totaling/revaluation application window and result are announced closer to the time.

sections.heading: What Happens After the Re-totaling/Revaluation Result?

items: If your marks improve and you now meet the passing requirement (minimum 35% in each subject), your result status will be updated accordingly.
If your marks remain unchanged or you still do not meet the passing criteria, you may need to reappear in the next available examination cycle, as per DGE Tamil Nadu's rules.
Students should collect their updated original marksheet from their school after the revised result is declared.

sections.heading: How to Check Telangana NEET UG Counselling 2026 Mop-Up Allotment?

content.text: Candidates who participated in Telangana NEET UG 2026 MBBS mop-up counselling can check the college-wise seat allotment result through the official KNRUHS website.

items: Visit the official website at knruhs.telangana.gov.in.
Open the Admission Notification section.
Find the MBBS Competent Authority Quota Mop-Up Phase College-Wise Allotment List dated 15 October 2026.
Open the View Document link.
Download the allotment PDF.
Search for your NEET UG roll number or name in the document.
Check your allotted college, rank and admission category.
Save the PDF for admission reference.

sections.heading: Important Instructions

items: Check your allotment: The mop-up allotment list is a PDF on knruhs.telangana.gov.in, needs no login, and you can search it by NEET rank or roll number.

Report on time: Allotted candidates must report at the allotted college before the last date of joining, with the specified documents. The joining deadline isn’t in the sources I found, so confirm it in the allotment notification.

No free exit: The last date for free exit was 8 October 2026, so there is no free exit for seats allotted in mop-up. Candidates are not permitted to discontinue after a mop-up allotment, so join only if you are sure.
Eligibility rules: Candidates who didn’t exercise web options in the first phase are not eligible for mop-up. Candidates who joined a seat earlier and are continuing the course can take part.

Deadlines are final: The web options window ran from 5:00 PM on 12 October to 5:00 PM on 14 October 2026. Mop-up is the final counselling round for vacant MBBS seats. Read the prospectus and Government Orders on the KNRUHS website before acting.

sections.heading: How to Attend PJTAU Special Quota Counselling 2026

content.text: PJTAU Special Quota counselling is manual, not online. There is no web-options or online seat-selection process for this round. To participate:

items: Check your category, applicable quota (Non-Farmers/Farmers'/Agriculture Labourers'), and TG EAPCET-2026 rank against the schedule table above to identify your date and time slot.

Report at the University Auditorium, PJTAU, Rajendranagar, Hyderabad, at least one hour before your scheduled time.
Carry all original certificates listed above, along with two Xerox copies of relevant certificates if you belong to EWS, BC, SC, or ST categories.

Candidates who secure a seat must submit certificates and pay the prescribed fee on the spot to confirm admission.

sections.heading: Important Instructions for Candidates

items: Counselling is held manually; it is not conducted online.
Selection under EWS, BC, SC, and ST quotas is subject to clearance of social status by the respective Telangana Government Directorates.
If a candidate attends counselling late, they must submit a letter to the counselling authorities indicating their actual time of arrival.
Candidates who fail to attend on the scheduled date and time cannot claim a seat as per their merit later.
If information or certificates furnished are found to be false, the University will take appropriate legal action.
Candidates/parents should not rely on middlemen or consultants; all seats are filled only through the University's combined counselling.

Candidates may take original certificates back temporarily (by furnishing an undertaking) if they need to attend another counselling, and must return them by the stipulated day, failing which the admission stands cancelled.
