sections.heading: How to Apply for KNRUHS B.Sc Nursing 2026-27 Online

items: Visit the official application portal: tsparamed.tsche.in.
Complete Mobile and Email Registration using a valid, active mobile number and email ID; verify both using the OTPs sent to each.
Click Validate - on successful verification, you will be taken to the Registration Form.
Fill in the required details in the Registration Form and click Validate to proceed to the Payment Gateway.

Pay the Registration and Verification fee (Rs. 2,500/- for OC/BC or Rs. 2,000/- for SC/ST, plus bank charges) via the payment gateway. This fee is non-refundable, so verify your eligibility before paying.
On successful payment, note down your registration number for future reference.

Fill in the complete application form, including Intermediate Board details and the number of subjects as applicable to your board (TS/AP Board: 4 subjects; other State Boards: 4 subjects; CBSE/ICSE/NIOS/AISSCE/SSCE/HSCE/APOSS/TOSS: 3 subjects; Inter Vocational with Bridge Course: 2 subjects).
Upload your passport-size photo and signature (each under 100 KB, in JPG/JPEG format).
Click Save and Exit; you may edit your data using the Data Updation link until it is correct.
Click Upload Certificates and upload all required documents listed above.
After uploading all documents, click Save and Print, and take a printout of the filled-in application form for future reference.

sections.heading: Important Instructions

items: Use a Desktop Computer or Laptop with Internet Explorer; do not use mobiles, tabs, or iPads to fill the application.
Do not enter false information - this is liable for criminal action.
Avoid using a slow internet connection while applying.
Keep your mobile phone accessible and do not block SMS, since OTPs and allotment messages are sent via SMS.
Do not refresh or close the page during payment until you receive a "Successful Payment" confirmation message.
No individual intimations will be sent by the University - check the KNRUHS website regularly for updates.
No transfers between colleges are permitted during the course under any circumstances.
The course duration is 4 years; candidates must complete the course within double the duration, i.e., 8 years for the 4YDC course.
Ragging is strictly prohibited and can lead to cancellation of the seat and legal punishment.
Candidates must tick the Anti-Drug undertaking checkbox while applying and submit a signed Anti-Drug Undertaking at the time of admission.

sections.heading: KNRUHS TS NEET UG 2026 Phase 1 Seat Allotment: Important Dates
KNRUHS TS NEET UG 2026 Phase 1 Seat Allotment: Step-by-Step Process

items: Check allotment status: Log in to tsmedadm.tsche.in using your TS NEET UG Registration Number and password.
Pay the University Fee: Successful candidates pay ₹12,000 online to generate the provisional allotment order.
Download the allotment order: Print the official seat allotment letter along with joining instructions.
Report physically at the allotted college: Visit the college with all original certificates within the given schedule.
Complete verification and pay tuition fee: Undergo document verification and pay the applicable college tuition fee to confirm admission.

sections.heading: Important Instructions for Candidates

items: Mandatory reporting: Candidates who receive a seat but fail to pay the University Fee or physically report within the given timeframe will have their admission automatically cancelled and will be barred from exercising options in all subsequent counselling rounds, to prevent seat blocking.

Upgradation in Phase 2: Candidates seeking a college upgrade in the next round must first accept and physically report to their Phase 1 allotment, complete University Fee payment, and clear tuition fees. Skipping Phase 1 joining forfeits eligibility for all later rounds.

Service bond: Students admitted to Government Medical Colleges must submit a service bond on stamp paper at the time of reporting, committing to compulsory post-MBBS rural medical service as mandated by state health regulations.

Tie-breaking criteria: When two or more candidates have identical NEET UG scores for the same seat choice, priority goes first to higher Biology marks, then higher Chemistry marks, then fewer incorrect answers.
SMS alerts: Once the provisional list is published, KNRUHS will send automated SMS notifications to allotted candidates' registered mobile numbers.

sections.heading: How to Apply for TG ICET 2026 Spot Admission

Visit the respective college in person and meet the principal or admissions in-charge.
Carry all original certificates, along with photocopies, for on-the-spot verification.

Since each college manages its own spot admission timeline, candidates should confirm dates directly with the college and also monitor the official website, tgicet.nic.in, for any centralized updates.

content.text: These dates follow the official TGCHE counselling schedule reported at the time of writing. TGCHE can revise dates at short notice, so candidates should treat tgicet.nic.in as the final authority on timing.

sections.heading: TS ICET 2026 Counselling Fee

content.text: Candidates who already paid this counselling registration fee during Phase 1 do not need to pay it again to participate in the Final Phase. Separately, each candidate must pay the tuition fee shown on their individual provisional allotment order after seat allotment; this amount varies by college and course and is not a fixed, universal figure.

sections.heading: TS ICET 2026 Final Phase Seat Allotment Process

content.text: Seat allotment in the Final Phase works on the same principle as Phase 1. TGCHE matches candidates to seats based on:

items: The candidate's TS ICET 2026 rank
Web options (college and course preferences) entered by the candidate
Reservation category (OC, BC, SC, ST, EWS, etc.)
Local/non-local candidate status
Seat availability across participating colleges
Category-wise and course-wise cutoff ranks

content.text: Every allotment is provisional. It is confirmed only after the candidate pays the tuition fee online, completes self-reporting on the portal, and submits original documents for physical verification at the allotted college within the notified deadline.

sections.heading: Documents Required for Final Phase Reporting

content.text: Candidates should carry the original documents along with self-attested photocopies when reporting physically to the allotted college. Commonly required documents for TS ICET counselling include:

items: TS ICET 2026 hall ticket and rank card
Provisional seat allotment order (downloaded after login)
Bachelor's degree provisional certificate and consolidated marks memo
SSC/10th and Intermediate/12th certificates (for age and study proof)
Transfer certificate (TC) and study certificates, as applicable
Caste certificate (for reserved category candidates)
Income certificate, if claiming fee reimbursement
Local/non-local status certificate, where required
Recent passport-size photographs
Fee payment receipt/self-reporting confirmation

content.text: Some colleges may ask for additional documents specific to the course or category. Candidates should confirm the exact checklist with their allotted institute in advance.

sections.heading: How to Download the TS ICET 2026 Final Phase Seat Allotment Result

items: Visit the official TG ICET counselling website: tgicet.nic.in
Click on the "Candidate Login" tab on the homepage.
Enter your ROC Form Number/Hall Ticket Number, Password, and Date of Birth.
Locate and click the Final Phase "Seat Allotment Result" or "Provisional Allotment Order" link.
Your allotment order will display the allotted college, course, category, and applicable tuition fee.
Download the allotment order and save or print a copy for reporting at the college.

sections.heading: What to Do After Checking the Allotment Result

items: If allotted a seat and satisfied: Pay the tuition fee online and complete self-reporting on the portal between August 22 and 24, 2026, then report physically at the college with original documents by August 25, 2026.

If allotted a seat but seeking an upgrade: This was the Final Phase, so no further regular counselling round follows; only spot counselling for remaining vacant seats will be available after August 24, 2026.
If not allotted any seat: Watch for the TG ICET 2026 spot counselling notification, expected around August 24, 2026, for any seats still vacant after this round.
If you miss the fee payment or self-reporting deadline: The provisional allotment stands to be cancelled, and the seat can be offered to another candidate.

sections.heading: Important Instructions for Candidates

items: Seat allotment is provisional until fee payment, online self-reporting, and physical document verification are all completed.
Keep your login credentials (hall ticket number, password, date of birth) private and secure.
Regularly check tgicet.nic.in for updates, since counselling dates can shift at short notice.
Non-payment of tuition fee within the notified window can lead to automatic cancellation of the allotted seat.
Candidates upgrading from a Phase 1 seat to a Final Phase seat permanently lose the earlier seat once the new allotment is confirmed.

sections.heading: Who Was Eligible for CCMN 2026 Special Counselling

content.text: CCMN 2026 special round 1 counselling was open to candidates who had already registered for the special CCMN counselling round. Broadly, the general CCMN 2026 eligibility criteria applicable through the counselling process are:

items: Candidates belonging to General, General-EWS, and OBC categories are required to have passed a BSc or equivalent qualifying degree with at least 60% aggregate marks or 6.5 CGPA.
Candidates belonging to reserved categories (SC, ST, PWD) are required to have at least 55% aggregate marks or 6.0 CGPA.
Candidates in the final year of their qualifying degree were also allowed to apply, provided they submit their final mark sheet as required.

For certain programmes at a few participating institutes, special eligibility criteria and restrictions apply — these are listed separately on the CCMN portal under "View Special Eligibility/Restrictions."
A valid IIT JAM 2026 score is mandatory for participation in CCMN 2026 counselling.

sections.heading: Freeze, Float, Slide or Withdraw: What Candidates Can Do

content.text: After checking the special round 1 allotment result, allotted candidates must choose one of the willingness options within the given deadline:

rows: Candidate accepts the currently allotted seat and confirms admission to that institute/programme; no further participation in upcoming rounds.
Candidate accepts the current seat but remains open to a better allotment in subsequent rounds.
Candidate wants to be considered for a different programme within the same or another institute in later rounds while keeping current allotment as backup.
Candidate withdraws entirely from the allotted seat and the counselling process.

content.text: Candidates must also complete online document upload for verification within the same window, since institutes will be verifying submitted documents during this period.

Proceed to upload the required documents and submit your willingness (freeze/float/slide) or withdrawal option before the deadline.

sections.heading: What Happens After Special Round 1

content.text: The CCMN allotment process for the special rounds is typically followed by a Special Round 2 and then a National Spot Round (NSR), which is the last counselling round in the CCMN cycle. Candidates who take admission through any round are usually required to complete physical reporting at the allotted institute after the process concludes, as per institute-specific instructions.

sections.heading: Eligibility Criteria

items: Candidates must hold a valid GATE score from 2024, 2025, or 2026.

Candidates must have passed their qualifying degree with a minimum aggregate of 60% marks or 6.5 CGPA (for General/General-EWS/OBC categories) and 55% marks or 6.0 CGPA (for SC/ST/PwD categories), from a recognized university/institute.
Final-year students awaiting results may participate provisionally, subject to submitting proof of passing within the specified deadline.
NRI candidates with a degree from another country and a valid GATE/JAM score are eligible, provided the qualifying degree is recognized by the Association of Indian Universities (AIU).
Some participating institutes may apply additional, institute-specific eligibility conditions. Candidates should verify this on the respective institute's website.

content.text: For CCMT counselling registration, the following non-refundable fee structure has been specified officially. Candidates participating in the special round are required to re-register and pay the applicable registration fee again.

sections.heading: Selection Process

items: Registration: Log in using GATE credentials and complete the special round registration, paying the applicable fee.
Choice Filling and Locking: Select and lock preferred institutes and programs based on the vacant seat matrix.
Seat Allotment: Seats are allotted based on GATE merit, choices filled, and seat availability.
Response (Freeze/Slide/Float): Candidates allotted a seat choose to freeze, slide, or float, depending on whether they want to accept or wait for an upgrade.
Document Verification: Candidates report to the designated reporting centre (physically or online, as specified) for verification.
Reporting to Institute: Candidates report to the allotted institute within the specified deadline to confirm admission, failing which the seat is cancelled.

detail.title: What is CCMN Counselling 2026?
detail.short_info: Complete guide to CCMN Counselling 2026 registration dates, seat allotment results, counselling fees, documents required, participating NITs, and step-by-step procedure for M.Sc. admissions via IIT JAM scores.

content.text: CCMN (Centralized Counselling for M.Sc./M.Sc. Tech) 2026 is the official centralised admission process through which IIT JAM-qualified candidates can secure seats in M.Sc. and M.Sc. Tech programmes offered by 20 NITs and other Centrally Funded Technical Institutes (CFTIs) across India. Conducted by NIT Warangal, the CCMN 2026 process covers online registration, choice filling, seat allotment, document verification, and physical reporting all carried out in multiple rounds. The CCMN 2026 first seat allotment result was released on June 12, 2026, and document verification must be completed by June 17, 2026. The second seat allotment is scheduled for June 22, 2026.

sections.heading: What is CCMN Counselling 2026?

content.text: CCMN counselling is the centralised seat-allocation mechanism for postgraduate science programmes at NITs and CFTIs in India. This section gives you the complete picture of what CCMN is and how it works.

CCMN stands for Centralized Counselling for M.Sc./M.Sc. Tech. Administered by NIT Warangal on behalf of all participating institutes, it uses candidates' IIT JAM 2026 scores to allocate seats across M.Sc. programmes in subjects such as Chemistry, Physics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Data Science, Biotechnology, and more. The process is conducted entirely online through the official NIC portal. The CCMN counselling process 2026 consists of registration, choice filling, seat allotment, and payment confirmation, with the goal of providing admissions for M.Sc. programmes at 20 NITs and CFTIs.

sections.heading: CCMN 2026 Counselling Dates Complete Schedule

sections.heading: CCMN 2026 Eligibility Criteria

content.text: Understanding who can participate in CCMN 2026 counselling is the first step before beginning the registration process.

To be eligible for CCMN counselling 2026, students need to have appeared for the JAM exam with a valid score. From the list of courses offered by different universities, they can select programmes based on admission requirements. Candidates must also check the individual eligibility conditions of each programme they wish to apply for before submitting the CCMN 2026 application, since subject-specific requirements may vary across NITs and CFTIs.

content.text: CCMN 2026 involves several fee components that candidates must pay at different stages of the process. Here is a complete breakdown.
The CCMN 2026 counselling fees are structured as follows:
Note: The SAF, PAF, and participation fees are adjusted against the total course admission fee, making them partly recoverable.

sections.heading: CCMN Counselling Procedure 2026 Step-by-Step Guide

content.text: The CCMN 2026 counselling procedure follows a clearly defined sequence of steps. Here is exactly what candidates need to do at each stage.

sections.heading: Step 1: CCMN Registration 2026

content.text: Candidates must complete the CCMN application form with personal details including gender, JAM score, mobile number, email address, paper code, and registration number. The registration fee can be paid through the ICICI bank Eazypay system. Providing false information on the application form will lead to disqualification from consideration for admission.

sections.heading: Step 2: CCMN Choice Filling 2026

content.text: Before the submission deadline, candidates must complete the CCMN 2026 application form for counselling by selecting their preferred programme and institution. Candidates are presented with a list of options during the process and must rank them in order of priority. Choices can be modified before final submission, but if candidates forget to lock their choices before the deadline, they will be locked automatically.

sections.heading: Step 3: CCMN Seat Allotment 2026

content.text: The CCMN 2026 seat allocation list is created using the candidates' choices and JAM scores. Candidates can view the seat allotment result using their IIT JAM registration ID and password. To accept the allotted seat, candidates should select the "Freeze" option. Upon accepting the seat allotment, candidates must pay the admission fee and report to the counselling location. A provisional admission notification will be issued to candidates who have frozen their seats and paid the CCMN counselling participation fee. Candidates can also withdraw their seats following the first and second allotment rounds.

sections.heading: Step 4: Document Verification

content.text: After the seat allotment, candidates must upload documents online and complete verification through the allotted institute. Physical reporting at the finally allotted institute takes place as per the schedule of each round.

sections.heading: CCMN National Spot Round 2026

content.text: The National Spot Round (NSR) is an additional opportunity for candidates who missed out on seats in the regular rounds. Here is what you need to know.

CCMN National Spot Round 2026 counselling will take place tentatively from August 1. Candidates must fill out and submit the CCMN choice filling form and complete registration before the submission deadline. The NSR is held only after the completion of all three regular rounds of CCMN seat allotment 2026.

sections.heading: Who is Eligible for the NSR?

content.text: Eligibility for the National Spot Round is limited to the following categories of candidates: those who have not yet completed the CCMN application form 2026; those who registered for CCMN 2026 but were not allocated a seat in any round; candidates who were given a seat in an earlier round but did not pay the counselling fee; and candidates who withdrew their seats in the first, second, or third rounds of allotment.

sections.heading: What to Do After CCMT Round 1 Seat Allotment 2026?

content.text: Once the result is out, candidates must take action promptly. Here is everything you need to do after checking your allotment.

Once the seat is allocated, candidates must complete their online reporting process within the deadline. They will have to pay their seat acceptance fee and choose one of the available willingness options.
After reviewing the allotment, candidates must select one of the following three options:

sections.heading: Option 1 : Freeze

content.text: If you are fully satisfied with the allotted seat, choose Freeze. This confirms your admission to the allotted institute and branch. Once candidates freeze the option, they do not participate in subsequent rounds of counselling for seat upgradation.

sections.heading: Option 2 - Float

content.text: Choose Float if you want to retain your current allotment but also wish to be considered for a higher-preference choice in upcoming rounds. If a better seat is available in Round 2 or 3, it will be automatically upgraded; otherwise, the current seat is retained.

sections.heading: Option 3 - Slide

content.text: Choose Slide if you want to be upgraded to a better branch within the same institute in subsequent rounds. Your current seat is retained if no upgrade is available.

sections.heading: Option 4 - Surrender

content.text: Candidates can also surrender the currently allotted seat and participate only in the next round for better-preferred choices. However, a warning applies: if no seat is allotted in the next round, the surrendered seat is permanently lost.

content.text: Since regular students cannot download the admit card online, these steps are for school authorities.

items: Visit the official website of Tripura Board of Secondary Education at tbse.tripura.gov.in.
Scroll to the “What’s New” or “Announcement” section on the homepage.
Click on the activated link for “TBSE Madhyamik/HS Admit Card 2026”.
Log in using the school/centre credentials provided by the board.

Print the admit cards, sign and stamp them if required, and distribute them to students before the exam dates.

content.text: For Students (Collection Process)

items: Visit your school on the date informed by the school administration.
Collect the original TBSE admit card 2026, check all details, and keep it safe till result declaration.

sections.heading: Details Mentioned on TBSE Admit Card 2026

content.text: The TBSE Madhyamik and HS admit cards carry important personal and exam-related details.

items: Student name
Roll number and registration number
Class (Madhyamik/HS) and stream (for Class 12)
School name and code
Exam centre name, code, and address

Important exam day instructions and guidelines

sections.heading: TBSE Exam Day Guidelines 2026

content.text: TBSE clearly mentions exam-day rules on the admit card, and students must follow them to avoid disqualification.

items: Original TBSE admit card 2026 (Class 10 or Class 12)
Valid school ID card or any identity proof, if asked by the centre​
Required stationery items such as pens, pencils, eraser, geometry box, as allowed.

content.text: Reporting and Conduct

items: Reach the exam centre at least 30 minutes to 1 hour before the reporting time mentioned on the admit card.
Sit in the allotted seat as per roll number and follow invigilator instructions throughout the exam.

content.text: Allowed Items

items: Transparent water bottle, basic stationery, and necessary medical items (if permitted by centre).

content.text: Prohibited Items

items: Mobile phones, smartwatches, calculators (unless specifically allowed), electronic gadgets, or any communication devices.
Any paper, chits, books or study material inside the exam hall.

content.text: If any error is found in the TBSE Class 10 or Class 12 admit card, students should act quickly and use official channels only.

items: Immediately inform your class teacher or examination in-charge at school and show the incorrect admit card.

Students may be asked to submit a written application along with copies of previous school records (e.g., registration card, school ID).​
Collect the corrected admit card before the exam and ensure the previous incorrect copy is not used.

sections.heading: UP NEET UG Round 2: Original vs Revised Schedule
Steps to Check the Official Postponement Notice

items: Visit the official UP NEET website at upneet.gov.in and dgme.up.gov.in.

sections.heading: Important Instructions for UP NEET UG Round 2 Candidates

items: Choice locking is separate from choice saving: Choices filled between the counselling window must be explicitly "locked." If a candidate saves choices but does not manually lock them before the deadline, the system automatically locks the last saved preference list for seat allotment.

No limit on number of college preferences: There is no restriction on how many college options a candidate can add during choice filling. Adding the maximum number of valid, genuine preferences increases the chance of seat allotment.

Choices can be edited before locking: As long as a candidate has only clicked "Save Choices" and not "Lock Choices," they can log in multiple times to reorder or add colleges until the choice filling window closes.

Verify private college fee structures before locking: Candidates opting for private medical or dental colleges must carefully check the total tuition, hostel, and miscellaneous fees on dgme.up.gov.in before finalizing their choices, since fee details vary by institution.

Reporting after seat allotment is mandatory: Candidates allotted a seat in Round 2 must physically report to their assigned medical or dental college with original documents, identity proof, and the allotment letter to complete admission formalities.

sections.heading: JoSAA Round 5: How to Check the Seat Allotment Result

content.text: Candidates can follow these steps to check and download their JoSAA Round 5 seat allotment result 2026:

items: Visit the official website: josaa.nic.in.
Click on the "Seat Allotment Result" link active for Round 5.
Log in using your JEE Main 2026 application number and password (JEE Advanced candidates use the same JoSAA login).
Your Round 5 allotment status will be displayed, showing allotted institute, branch, category, and rank details.
If a seat has been allotted, download the Provisional Seat Allotment Letter / Initial Seat Allotment Intimation Slip.
Save a digital copy and print multiple physical copies for reporting and document verification.

content.text: Important: JoSAA does not send individual result notifications to candidates. It is each candidate's own responsibility to log in and check their allotment status for every round, including Round 5.

sections.heading: What Happens After the JoSAA Round 5 Result?

content.text: Once the Round 5 result is out, allotted candidates must choose one of the following options within the deadline:

rows: Accept the current seat but remain open to an upgrade in institute/branch. Since Round 5 is the final round, floating candidates will not get further upgrades through JoSAA and must proceed with reporting.
Accept the seat and lock it in permanently, with no further upgrade sought.
Confirm the current allotment while remaining open to a better course within the same institute.
Completely withdraw from JoSAA counselling. A processing fee (as specified in the official brochure) is deducted from the seat acceptance amount.

content.text: Because Round 5 is the last round of JoSAA counselling for 2026, candidates who float will not be moved to another seat afterward through JoSAA - they must still complete reporting for their current allotment to retain it.

sections.heading: Eligibility for JoSAA Seat Allotment

items: For IIT admission: A valid JEE Advanced 2026 rank is mandatory. Candidates must also be among the top 2.5 lakh JEE Main qualifiers to have been eligible for JEE Advanced.

For NIT/IIIT/GFTI admission: A valid JEE Main 2026 rank is required, along with either 75% marks in Class 12 (65% for SC/ST/PwD candidates) or a position in the top 20 percentile of the respective board.

content.text: Candidates who do not meet the minimum Class 12 qualifying criteria are not eligible for seat allotment at NITs, IIITs, and GFTIs, even if they hold a valid JEE Main rank.

sections.heading: Documents Required for JoSAA Round 5 Reporting

items: JEE Main 2026 admit card/rank card
JEE Advanced 2026 rank card (for IIT-allotted candidates)
Class 10 certificate (for date of birth proof)
Class 12 marksheet and pass certificate
Category certificate - SC/ST/OBC-NCL/EWS (if applicable)
PwD certificate (if applicable)
Passport-size photographs (scanned, as per prescribed format)
Scanned signature (as per prescribed format)

content.text: All documents must match JoSAA's prescribed file format and size specifications, which are listed in the official information brochure on josaa.nic.in.

sections.heading: Seat Vacancy and Cutoff Details for Round 5

content.text: Institute-wise and branch-wise vacancy numbers, along with the opening and closing ranks for Round 5, are published separately by JoSAA on its official Opening/Closing Rank (OR-CR) portal shortly after each round's result. These figures were not available in the sources reviewed for this article at the time of writing. Candidates should check the OR-CR section on josaa.nic.in directly for the confirmed Round 5 opening and closing ranks for their category and preferred institute.

Note: Opening/Closing Ranks for "Open" category seats represent the Common Rank List (CRL), while those for EWS, OBC-NCL, SC, and ST represent category-specific ranks. A rank suffixed with 'P' indicates it is from the Preparatory Rank List.

sections.heading: Fee Details

content.text: The exact seat acceptance fee amount for JoSAA Round 5, 2026 was not confirmed in the sources available for this article. Only the processing fee for a complete withdrawal/surrender (₹3,000, deducted from the seat acceptance amount) is specified in available reports. Candidates should refer to the official JoSAA 2026 information brochure or the fee payment section on josaa.nic.in for the exact applicable amount.

sections.heading: What Happens if You Miss the Round 5 Deadline?

content.text: If a candidate fails to complete seat acceptance, reporting, and fee payment within the Round 5 deadline (July 21, 2026), their candidature is permanently cancelled for JoSAA counselling, and they will not be considered in any further JoSAA round, since Round 5 is the last round. Such candidates may still be eligible to participate in CSAB special counselling rounds, which are conducted separately to fill vacant seats at NITs, IIITs, and GFTIs after JoSAA concludes.

sections.heading: Important Instructions for Candidates

items: Round 5 is the final round of JoSAA Counselling 2026 - there is no subsequent JoSAA round after this.

Always use the Float option (not Surrender) if you wish to remain eligible for admission while hoping for a better outcome elsewhere, since Freeze-to-Float switching is not allowed but Float-to-Freeze is.
Complete document upload and respond to any verification queries within the specified deadline, or risk elimination from counselling.

items.name: What Is the JoSAA Round 3 Cutoff 2026?

detail.title: What Is the JoSAA Round 3 Cutoff 2026?
detail.short_info: JoSAA Round 3 cutoff 2026 is out on josaa.nic.in. Check IIT, NIT, IIIT & GFTI opening-closing ranks, reporting deadline, SAF fee & Freeze/Float/Slide options.

content.text: The Joint Seat Allocation Authority (JoSAA) released the Round 3 seat allotment result and cutoff for the 2026 academic session on July 6, 2026, at 5:00 PM IST on the official portal, josaa.nic.in. The Round 3 cutoff is expressed as opening and closing ranks the range of JEE Main or JEE Advanced ranks within which a seat was offered in a specific institute, branch, category, and quota. If your rank falls within this range, your seat allotment for that combination is confirmed for this round.

This article explains what the JoSAA Round 3 cutoff means, how to check it institute-wise on the official website, how ranks are trending compared to earlier rounds, and exactly what candidates need to do next from paying the seat acceptance fee to choosing Freeze, Float, or Slide.

sections.heading: What Is the JoSAA Round 3 Cutoff 2026?

content.text: The JoSAA cutoff is not a fixed number it's a rank band published separately for every institute, academic program, quota, category, and gender combination after each counselling round. Round 3 cutoffs specifically reflect the seats that became available after Round 1 and Round 2 candidates froze, floated, withdrew, or failed to complete reporting.

items: Opening rank: the best (lowest numerical) rank at which a seat was offered in that particular institute-branch combination.
Closing rank: the last (highest numerical) rank at which the final seat was allotted in that round.
Ranks for IITs are based on the JEE Advanced 2026 All India Rank, while NITs, IIITs, and GFTIs use the JEE Main 2026 Common Rank List (CRL) or category rank.

Opening rank is the first rank that secured admission in a particular college and branch, while closing rank is the last rank that got admission for instance, if a branch's closing rank is 5,000, every candidate ranked up to 5,000 was eligible for that seat.

sections.heading: JoSAA Round 3 2026 - Key Dates at a Glance

content.text: Knowing the exact counselling timeline is critical, since JoSAA does not grant extensions for missed deadlines. The table below summarizes the confirmed schedule around Round 3.

rows: Online reporting (fee payment, document upload, willingness selection)

content.text: Register for Job Alerts

The last date to pay the seat acceptance fee and upload documents is July 8, 2026, at 5:00 PM IST, and verification queries must be answered by July 9, 2026. Round 4 results are expected on July 10, 2026, with a reporting deadline of July 12, while Round 5, the final round, is expected on July 16, 2026, with reporting closing on July 18. Candidates should treat Round 4 and 5 dates as provisional until JoSAA confirms them after Round 3 reporting closes.

sections.heading: How Many Institutes and Seats Are Part of JoSAA 2026?

content.text: Understanding the scale of the counselling process helps candidates gauge how competitive Round 3 cutoffs are likely to be across different institute categories.

JoSAA 2026 manages joint seat allocation for admission to 138 institutes for the academic year 2026-27, comprising 23 IITs, IISc Bengaluru, 31 NITs, IIEST Shibpur, 26 IIITs, and 56 Other Government-Funded Technical Institutes (Other-GFTIs). On the seat-availability side, a total of 64,219 engineering seats are available for BTech admissions this year, plus 3,104 supernumerary seats reserved specifically for female candidates, with NITs alone contributing the largest share at 25,162 seats.

sections.heading: How to Check JoSAA Round 3 Cutoff 2026 Online

content.text: The official JoSAA opening and closing rank (OR-CR) portal lets candidates filter cutoff data by institute, program, category, and round. Here's the step-by-step process to pull up your specific cutoff:

items: Visit the official portal at josaa.nic.in.
Click on the eServices (or Services) tab on the homepage menu.
Select the OR-CR link, and choose "OR-CR 2026" for the current cycle.

In the filter form, select: Round No. choose Round 3 Type of Institute IIT, NIT, IIIT, or GFTI Name of the Institute your target college Academic Program the specific branch (e.g., Computer Science, Mechanical) Seat Type/Category OPEN, OBC-NCL, SC, ST, or EWS as applicable
Round No. choose Round 3
Type of Institute IIT, NIT, IIIT, or GFTI
Name of the Institute your target college
Academic Program the specific branch (e.g., Computer Science, Mechanical)
Seat Type/Category OPEN, OBC-NCL, SC, ST, or EWS as applicable
Click Submit to view the opening rank and closing rank table for that exact combination.

content.text: The JoSAA 2026 cutoff PDFs list the institute name, academic program, quota, seat type, gender, opening rank, and closing rank, and this data is released for all 138 participating institutes. Shiksha

links.text: Shiksha

sections.heading: Round 3 Cutoff Trends: IIT vs NIT vs IIIT vs GFTI

content.text: Cutoff movement between rounds varies significantly depending on the institute type, and understanding this pattern helps candidates decide whether to Float for an upgrade or Freeze their current seat.

items: IITs: Closing ranks for top branches at premier IITs tend to barely shift across rounds. At IIT Bombay, Delhi, and Madras, Computer Science closing ranks show almost no movement across all five rounds because candidates in this rank range overwhelmingly prefer these seats, and very few vacate them. Cracku

NITs: These typically see the sharpest relaxation in Round 3. NIT seats consistently relax by 8 to 15% by Round 3, as candidates who were allotted IIT seats confirm and exit, freeing up NIT options for those just outside the Round 1 cutoff. Note that NIT cutoffs are released separately for Home State and Other State quota, so check the correct column for your domicile. CrackuMotion Blog

IIITs and GFTIs: IIITs and GFTIs also base their cutoffs on JEE Main ranks, and while GFTIs are often overlooked, several of them offer strong placement records in core engineering branches. Motion Blog

content.text: Because these estimated relaxation patterns are historical trends and not confirmed figures, always cross-check the actual Round 3 numbers published on josaa.admissions.nic.in before making a Freeze or Float decision.

sections.heading: What to Do After the Round 3 Allotment: Freeze, Float, or Slide

content.text: Once your Round 3 result is out, you must choose one of three willingness options and complete online reporting skipping this step is treated as a rejection of your seat.

items: Freeze: Choose this if your allotted seat is your genuine first choice. Freezing is final you exit the counselling process and cannot participate in Rounds 4 or 5.
Float: Keeps you eligible for a possible upgrade to a better institute or branch in Round 4 and Round 5, while safely retaining your current seat if no upgrade comes through.
Slide: Keeps you within the same institute but eligible for a preferred branch upgrade.

content.text: Float is generally the safer decision unless your current allotment is your absolute first preference, since it carries zero downgrade risk if no upgrade happens in later rounds, you simply keep your existing seat.

sections.heading: Seat Acceptance Fee (SAF) and Reporting Requirements

items: The Seat Acceptance Fee is Rs. 30,000 for General, OBC-NCL, and EWS categories, and Rs. 15,000 for SC, ST, and PwD categories.
Of this, Rs. 5,000 is a non-refundable processing charge, while the remainder is adjusted against the institute's admission fee.
If you already paid the SAF in an earlier round, it carries forward automatically, and only first-time allottees in Round 3 need to make a fresh payment.

Required documents typically include your Class 10 and 12 certificates, JEE Main/Advanced admit card and scorecard, category/PwD certificates (if applicable), a medical certificate, and passport-size photographs.

A common rejection reason: OBC-NCL and EWS certificates issued even one day before April 1, 2026, are treated as invalid and can lead to immediate seat cancellation get a fresh certificate if yours predates this.

sections.heading: What Happens Next: JoSAA Round 4 and Round 5

content.text: If you don't secure a seat in Round 3, there's no need to worry about re-registering. Candidates without an allotment in Round 3 automatically remain in the process for Rounds 4 and 5 at no additional cost. If your willingness status is set to Float or Slide, you also remain fully eligible for a further upgrade in the subsequent rounds. After Round 5 concludes, any seats that remain vacant across NITs, IIITs, and GFTIs move to the CSAB Special Round for a final round of counselling.

sections.heading: How to Use JEE Advanced Response Sheet 2026 to Estimate Score

content.text: The primary purpose of the JEE Advanced response sheet is to let candidates verify their marked responses and estimate their probable score before the results are out. Once the provisional answer key is released, candidates can compare each response with the official correct answer to calculate their marks.
Matching Responses with Provisional Answer Key
After downloading the response sheet, candidates should wait for the provisional answer key, which is scheduled to be published on May 25, 2026. When both documents are available, you can:

items: Place the response sheet and provisional answer key side by side.
For each question, check whether your recorded response matches the correct option in the answer key.
Note questions left unattempted and those where you might have chosen an incorrect option.

content.text: This process helps you understand your performance in each section and identify topics where you did well or need improvement.
Calculating Probable Marks
JEE Advanced uses its own marking scheme, including full, partial and negative marks depending on the question type. Using the response sheet and answer key:

items: Add marks for each correct response as per the marking scheme for that particular question.
Subtract marks for questions with negative marking if your response does not match the correct answer.
Sum the scores for all questions across Paper 1 and Paper 2 to get an approximate total.

content.text: This estimated score is only indicative and the final score will be based on the official evaluation and final answer key.

sections.heading: JEE Advanced 2026 Exam - Basic Details (For Reference)

content.text: JEE Advanced is conducted for admission to undergraduate programmes in engineering, sciences and architecture at the Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs). For 2026, IIT Roorkee is the organising institute and the exam consists of two compulsory papers conducted on the same day.

Each paper typically includes questions from Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics, with a mix of single-correct, multiple-correct and numerical answer types. Candidates must appear in both Paper 1 and Paper 2 to be considered for ranking, and the total score is calculated based on performance in both papers combined.

sections.heading: Important Instructions for JEE Advanced 2026 Candidates

sections.heading: CSAB 2026 Mock Seat Allotment - Allotment Process

items: Candidates register and fill/reorder institute-branch preferences on the CSAB portal.
The mock seat allotment is generated based on current preferences, JEE Main 2026 rank, category, and available seats - this shows candidates their probable allotment.
Candidates can review the mock result and revise their preference order during the editing window.
Once satisfied, candidates must lock their final choices by August 5, 2026 (2 PM); choice locking requires OTP verification sent to the registered mobile number and email ID.
After locking, no further edits are permitted for Round 1.
CSAB Special Round 1 seat allotment result will be declared on August 6, 2026, based on the final locked preferences, merit rank, category, and seat availability.
CSAB special rounds process vacant Home State quota seats first; unfilled Home State quota seats convert to Other State quota seats as per standard CSAB rules.
Candidates who already hold a JoSAA seat and opt into CSAB will retain that JoSAA seat unless a higher-preference option is allotted in CSAB Special Round 1.

sections.heading: How to Check CSAB 2026 Mock Seat Allotment Result

items: Visit the official CSAB candidate login portal: CSAB 2026 Mock Seat Allotment Login Link.
Enter your JEE Main 2026 application number and password.
Log in to access the candidate dashboard.
Check the mock seat allotment status, including the probable allotted institute and programme.
Download or save the mock allotment details for future reference.
If not satisfied with the result, go to the "Choice Filling & Display" section and use the "Move Up," "Move Down," or "Swap" options to reorder preferences.
Save every change made before logging out.
Lock the final preference list before August 5, 2026 (2 PM), using OTP verification.

sections.heading: CSAB 2026 Mock Seat Allotment: Important Instructions

items: Checking the mock allotment is entirely online; CSAB will not send email or SMS reminders about the result release.
If dissatisfied with the mock result, reorder preferences by comparing them against last year's college-wise closing ranks relative to your CRL/category rank.
Build a combined preference list covering highly preferred, moderate, and safe institute options.
If already allotted a desired seat, keep the preference sequence unchanged.
Do not remove ambitious/dream college choices just because they weren't allotted in the mock round - the final round may still offer them depending on vacancy movement.
Placing a college higher in the list does not reduce chances of getting a lower-preference seat if higher options remain unavailable.
Avoid listing any institute/branch you are unwilling to join, since accepting an allotted seat is governed by CSAB rules and may involve forfeiting the seat acceptance fee if declined improperly.
Do not log in from multiple devices/tabs simultaneously, as this may cause session timeouts and unsaved changes.
Female candidates should review both Gender-Neutral and Female-Only (supernumerary) seat options, which remain active in CSAB Special Rounds.
Candidates opting for GFTIs should check institute-specific tuition and hostel fee details on csab.nic.in before final locking.
Choice locking requires OTP verification; ensure your registered mobile number is active.
Once locked, choices cannot be edited for Round 1 under any circumstances.
CSAB counselling is conducted exclusively through csab.nic.in - never share login credentials or OTPs on third-party sites or forums.

sections.heading: Reservation Policy and Category-wise Rules

items: OBC candidates must belong to the Non-Creamy Layer (NCL) to be eligible as reserved category candidates; otherwise, they will be treated as Unreserved (UR)/General.
OBC-NCL and EWS certificates must be issued in the appropriate format on or after 01.04.2026, as per current Govt. of West Bengal guidelines.
PwD seats are filled on a horizontal basis within the respective category.

Reservation for SC/ST/EWS/PwD follows extant West Bengal Government rules; OBC reservation follows Kolkata Gazette Notification Nos. 944-BCW/MR-23/2026 and 945-BCW/MR-23/2026 (both dated 18.05.2026), and Labr/85-Emp/EC/1M-01/2025 dated 25.05.2026.
Domicile certificates issued by elected people's representatives (municipal commissioner, councilor, panchayat member, GTA, MLA, or MP) are not acceptable as domicile proof.

If a domicile certificate under Proforma b or e-District shows the parent's domicile, two original ID proofs of the parent (Voter ID, Aadhaar Card, or Passport) showing a West Bengal residential address must be produced during document verification.

sections.heading: Important Instructions

items: The Provisional Merit List has been prepared strictly as per merit.
Provisional seat allotment will be made serially from the merit list until seats in the respective categories are filled.
All admissions are provisional; if a candidate is found ineligible, or is found to have suppressed material information or submitted false information/documents, the admission will stand cancelled.
OBC candidates must submit an updated NCL certificate on the day of counselling, failing which they will be treated as UR/General.
Vacant SC seats will be filled by ST candidates and vice versa.
Reservation rules follow extant West Bengal Government policy for SC/ST/EWS/PwD and specified Gazette notifications for OBC.
A Domicile Certificate in the prescribed format is mandatory; certain issuing authorities are not accepted (see Reservation Policy section above).
Participation in counselling does not guarantee admission; the admission committee's decision is final.
The university reserves the right to increase or decrease the number of seats without assigning any reason.
Selected candidates must submit the downloaded online Anti-Ragging affidavit at first registration and each subsequent year, through www.antiragging.in and www.amanmovement.org.

sections.heading: How Is the WBCHSE Semester 3 Admit Card 2027 Issued?

content.text: Unlike some other board exams, WBCHSE does not allow individual students to log in and download their own Semester III admit card. Instead, the process works as follows:

items: WBCHSE uploads the admit cards on its official portal for registered schools.
The Head of Institution (HOI) of each school logs in using the school's official credentials on wbchse.wb.gov.in or the designated school portal.
The HOI downloads and takes a printout of the admit cards for all registered students of that school.
Schools verify the details and distribute the admit cards to students, usually after getting them signed and stamped by the Principal/HOI.
Students collect their admit card from their respective school before the exam date.

sections.heading: Details Mentioned on the WBCHSE HS Semester 3 Admit Card

items: Student's name and roll number
Registration number
School name and code
Date of birth
Subject codes/combination
Examination centre name and address
Exam dates and reporting time
Candidate's photograph and signature

sections.heading: Important Instructions for WBCHSE Semester 3 Examinees

items: Carry the school-issued admit card to the examination centre on every exam day - no student is allowed to sit for the exam without it.
Reach the examination centre well before the reporting time to complete verification procedures.
Verify all personal and subject details on the admit card before the exam begins.
Follow all examination guidelines issued by WBCHSE, including restrictions on prohibited items.
The exam is conducted in MCQ/ OMR format, so carrying a proper ink pen is essential.

content_sections.heading: Sports Eligibility for Income Tax Delhi Recruitment 2026
content_sections.text: Applicants must have recognized sporting achievements in the events and competitions prescribed by the notification. Sports performance achieved between 1 January 2020 and 15 October 2026 will be considered. The notification establishes the following order of preference for eligible sportspersons: Candidates representing India in recognized international competitions, with the required sports-authority clearance. Candidates representing a State or Union Territory in recognized Senior or Junior National Championships and securing the prescribed medal or position. Candidates representing a university in Inter-University competitions and securing the prescribed position. Candidates representing a State or Union Territory in eligible Khelo India Games competitions. Candidates representing State Schools in recognized National School Games competitions and securing the prescribed position. Candidates representing a State, Union Territory, University or State School team at the specified competition level without winning a medal or position. Important: Sporting achievement certificates must be issued by the competent authorities and submitted in the prescribed formats. Participation or achievement outside the recognized competition categories does not automatically establish eligibility.

content_sections.text: The notification specifies authorized certificate-issuing authorities for different categories of sports competitions. Candidates must use the relevant certificate forms prescribed in Annexure-II of the notification. Sports certificates issued in formats not prescribed by the notification will not be accepted.

Secretary of the concerned National Federation or State Association
Dean of Sports or another officer in overall charge of university sports
Director or Additional/Joint/Deputy Director responsible for school sports in the state public instruction or education directorate
Designated Sports Authority of India or Khelo India official, as specified

For Technical and Clerical Posts: Written merit marks = (Marks obtained out of 120 / 120) × 60. For Peon: Written merit marks = (Marks obtained out of 100 / 100) × 60. They are not automatically awarded for general experience at other institutions.

technical knowledge

content_sections.text: Assam Rifles opened online applications for Technical and Tradesman posts on 28 September 2026. Eligible candidates must complete the application process by 28 October 2026 at 11:59 PM. The recruitment rally is tentatively scheduled from 23 November 2026 onwards.

content_sections.heading: Assam Rifles Technical and Tradesman Vacancy 2026
content_sections.text: The Assam Rifles Technical and Tradesman Recruitment 2026 notification lists 354 tentative vacancies across 18 trades. Warrant Officer (Cipher) has the highest number of vacancies with 124 posts, followed by Rifleman (Electrical Fitter Signal) with 32 posts.

content_sections.heading: Assam Rifles Recruitment 2026 Category-wise Vacancy
content_sections.text: The recruitment notification provides separate category-wise vacancy allocations for Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe, Other Backward Classes, Economically Weaker Section and Unreserved candidates. There is no state-wise quota.

content_sections.heading: Assam Rifles Technical and Tradesman Eligibility Criteria 2026
content_sections.text: Candidates must meet the educational qualification and age requirements prescribed for their chosen Assam Rifles trade. The notification includes opportunities for candidates with Class 10, Class 12, relevant ITI qualifications, technical diplomas and specified healthcare qualifications. Applicants for Warrant Officer (Cipher) must have passed 10+2 with English and Mathematics from a recognized board, along with the prescribed technical qualification. The notification specifies recognized computer or information technology-related diploma qualifications. The technical trades include Electrical Fitter Signal, Lineman Field, Armourer, Engineer Equipment Mechanic, Recovery Vehicle Mechanic, Electrician Motor Vehicle, Instrument Mechanic, Metalsmith, Upholster, Store Keeper Technical, Vehicle Mechanic, Welder and Mason. Educational requirements vary by trade and generally include Matriculation with relevant ITI certification, technical training or a recognized diploma in the prescribed discipline. Important: Trade-wise educational qualifications, course durations, ITI specializations and age limits are separately prescribed in Appendix A of the official notification. Candidates must verify the exact requirements for their selected trade before applying.

content_sections.heading: Assam Rifles Technical and Tradesman Application Fee 2026
content_sections.text: The Assam Rifles Technical and Tradesman Recruitment Rally 2026 application fee is Rs. 100 for candidates required to pay the fee. SC, ST and Ex-Servicemen candidates are exempted. Candidates may pay through the online payment facility or the prescribed SBI Bank Challan option. Payment receipts must be retained for verification during the recruitment rally.

content_sections.heading: Assam Rifles Technical and Tradesman Selection Process 2026
content_sections.text: The Assam Rifles recruitment process consists of several stages to assess physical fitness, technical knowledge, trade skills and medical eligibility. Initial document verification. Physical Efficiency Test (PET). Physical Standard Test (PST). Computer Based Test (CBT). Trade Skill Test. Document Verification. Detailed Medical Examination (DME). Review Medical Examination (RME), where applicable. Candidates qualifying the preliminary physical and document checks will be considered for further stages. The Trade Skill Test is qualifying in nature. Shortlisting is based on CBT merit and the applicable recruitment conditions.

content_sections.heading: Assam Rifles Physical Efficiency Test 2026
content_sections.text: The Physical Efficiency Test requires candidates to complete the prescribed running distance within the qualifying time.

content_sections.heading: Assam Rifles Physical Standard Test 2026
content_sections.text: The Physical Standard Test includes height, chest and weight measurements. Relaxed standards apply to eligible candidates from specific regions and tribal categories. Weight must be proportionate to height and age according to the prescribed medical standards. Candidates claiming a physical standard relaxation must produce the required supporting certificate.

content_sections.heading: Assam Rifles CBT Exam Pattern 2026
content_sections.text: The Assam Rifles Technical and Tradesman Computer Based Test will consist of 100 multiple-choice questions carrying 100 marks. The examination duration is two hours, and negative marking will apply. The question paper will be based on the Food Safety Officer syllabus prescribed by the recruiting department.

tables.caption: Assam Rifles CBT Minimum Qualifying Marks

content_sections.heading: Assam Rifles Trade Skill Test 2026
content_sections.text: Shortlisted candidates must undergo the Trade Skill Test relevant to their applied post. The test consists of practical assessment of the required technical or vocational skills. The Trade Skill Test is qualifying in nature. Candidates must pass this stage to remain eligible for further recruitment formalities.

content_sections.heading: How to Apply Online for Assam Rifles Technical and Tradesman Recruitment 2026
content_sections.text: Eligible candidates can submit the Assam Rifles Technical and Tradesman Recruitment Rally 2026 application online through the official Assam Rifles website by 28 October 2026 at 11:59 PM. Visit the official Assam Rifles website at https://www.assamrifles.gov.in/ . Open the Technical and Tradesman Recruitment Rally 2026 notification. Read the complete eligibility requirements for the relevant post or trade. Select the Online Application option. Complete the application with personal, educational, contact and domicile details. Select the appropriate trade and reservation category. Complete the prescribed fee payment if applicable. Review the application carefully before submission. Submit the application and download the acknowledgement. Print the completed application form and retain the fee receipt or challan. Carry the application printout and required original documents when reporting for the recruitment rally. Important: Candidates may submit only one online application. Requests to change the trade, category or submitted information after final submission will not be accepted.

content_sections.heading: Assam Rifles Recruitment 2026 Important Documents
content_sections.text: Candidates must possess the required eligibility and identity documents when completing their application and attending the recruitment rally. Class 10 certificate for date of birth verification. Relevant educational qualification certificates and mark sheets. ITI, diploma or technical training certificates, where applicable. Domicile / Permanent Residential Certificate. SC, ST, OBC or EWS certificate, where applicable. Ex-Servicemen documents, where applicable. Online application form printout. Application fee payment receipt or SBI challan, where applicable.

The 40-mark Sports-Related Information section covers these ten areas: | Exercise Physiology (energy systems, ATP production, cardiovascular and muscular adaptations, recovery and fatigue management) Sports Psychology (motivation, personality and sports performance, managing fear, anger, anxiety, aggression and stress) Sports Training (principles of training, training components, planning and periodization, talent identification) Sports Biomechanics (motion, force, levers, Newton's laws in sports, kinematics and kinetics, injury prevention) Sports Nutrition and Yoga (macronutrients, micronutrients, hydration, diet planning for athletes, balanced diet, yogic practices) Sports Medicine (common sports injuries, first aid and emergency care, massage and rehabilitation) Organization and Administration in Sports (sports organization, event management, facility and equipment management, leadership and communication) Testing, Measurement and Evaluation (physical fitness testing, skill and performance testing, body types) Application of Digital Learning and AI in Sports (digital coaching tools, AI applications, data management and statistical analysis, computer applications) International and National sports federations and bodies, major competitions, sports awards in India, and rules and regulations of sports | Part-2 covers computer and IT basics (hardware and software, input and output, IP address, IT gadgets, e-mail, printer, tablet and mobile operation, MS-Word and MS-Excel, operating systems, social networking, e-governance), digital financial tools, future skills and cyber security, and developments such as AI, big data processing, deep learning, machine learning and Internet of Things. The remaining Part-1 subjects follow standard general studies topics as printed in the notification.

how_to_apply: The notification allows only the online application system. Applications sent by any other means are not accepted. Candidates should read the full advertisement before applying.

Visit the Commission's website upsssc.gov.in and, on the homepage under the Live Advertisement Segment, click the advertisement for Sports Directorate Main Examination (PET-2025)/22 to view or download it.
Log in using your PET-2025 registration number. An OTP is sent to the mobile number or e-mail registered in PET-2025.

Your personal details recorded in PET-2025 (name, parents' names, domicile, category, EWS, horizontal reservation details, date of birth, gender, marital status, mobile number, e-mail) are displayed automatically.
Select the posts you want to apply for. A post not selected is not considered.

For each selected post, choose Yes or No for the required educational qualification and enter the board or university name, year of passing, certificate or roll number, certificate issue date and marks details.

Check the photo and signature uploaded in PET-2025, which are displayed automatically and cannot be changed. Then enter whether you hold any preferential qualification, and check your permanent and correspondence address.
Read the declaration, tick all checkboxes, enter the verification code and click "Save and Submit".
Pay the fee through credit card, debit card, internet banking, UPI or SBI e-challan. The application is submitted automatically once the fee is paid and reconciled.
Download and print the application. Keep a copy safe, as it may be required during record verification.

If the application does not appear after payment, the fee has not been reconciled. Log in with the registration number, use "Update Your Transaction ID by Double Verification" in the Applicant Segment, and click "Verify Transaction ID".
If payment fails, a Payment Acknowledgment Receipt (PAR) appears instead of the application. Use the same option and then the "Application Fee Deposition" option to pay.
For SBI e-challan, download the challan, pay at any SBI branch, then enter the challan details through the "Update Your Transaction ID by Double Verification" option.

After the application is finally submitted, candidates can make corrections until 11-11-2026 by logging in through the Applicant's Dashboard, clicking "Modify Application" and entering the verification code and OTP. Only the following details can be corrected:
Correspondence address.
Personal details such as EWS and horizontal reservation category (Dependant of Freedom Fighter, Disabled, Ex-Servicemen, Gender, Outstanding Sportsperson, etc.).
Details of mandatory or preferential qualification entered in the application.
Marital status.
No correction is possible after the last date for correction, and the Commission does not accept separate representations for corrections.
important_instructions: Uttar Pradesh reserved-category candidates must mark their category in the application. Candidates working in central or state government service must get a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from their employer, to be shown when the Commission asks. Self-attested copies of mark sheets, certificates and degrees must be produced to verify age and qualification when requested. The examination date, time and centre are given in the admission card. The centre, date and time are not changed in any case, and candidates should not write to the Commission about it. The Commission does not correspond individually with candidates. All information is uploaded on its website, so candidates should check it regularly. An application can be cancelled if the date of birth is not given, the candidate is overage or underage, lacks the mandatory qualification, or gives false information. Giving wrong facts that cannot be proved by certificates can lead to debarment from this and all other examinations and selections of the Commission. Malpractice, indiscipline or misbehaviour in the examination can lead to cancellation of candidature and debarment. The Uttar Pradesh Public Examination (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024 applies.

content_sections.heading: UPSSSC Sports Directorate Vacancy 2026
content_sections.text: The notification advertises 108 posts. Table 1 gives the post-wise and category-wise vacancies as printed in the notification. A dash (--) means the notification shows no figure for that category. The notification states that vacancy numbers and category-wise figures may be revised in line with the latest Uttar Pradesh government rules and orders, so the total may increase or decrease. In summary: Groundsman 3 posts, Deputy Sports Officer 50 posts, Assistant Coach (Swimming) 25 posts, Assistant Coach (other 11 sports) 12 posts, and Lifeguard 18 posts. The notification does not explain what "Special Selection" means beyond using it as a post label. Table 2 of the notification gives horizontal reservation by post. Only the non-zero figures are listed below. All other horizontal categories (including all disability sub-categories not mentioned here) show 00 or no figure for every post. For Deputy Sports Officer, Assistant Coach and Lifeguard posts, the notification also lists Deaf, Hard of Hearing, Leprosy Cured, Dwarfism and Acid Attack Victims sub-categories, all with 00 vacancies. For the Dependant of Freedom Fighter and Outstanding Sportsperson categories, every post shows 00.

content_sections.heading: UPSSSC Sports Directorate Eligibility Criteria
content_sections.text: Only those candidates can apply online who hold the mandatory qualification for the advertised post, appeared in the Preliminary Eligibility Test (PET) 2025, and have a PET-2025 scorecard issued by the Commission. The notification also lists these general conditions: Applicants must be citizens of India. Candidates must hold the mandatory educational qualification and other required eligibility, with the relevant certificates, by the last date of application, 04-11-2026. Candidates for the Main Examination are shortlisted on the normalized score of PET-2025. Candidates with zero, negative or less-than-zero absolute or normalized score are not shortlisted. Candidates whose PET-2025 results are marked "Under Investigation (UI)" or "Provisional" are allowed to apply provisionally. Their shortlisting and selection depend on the outcome of the Commission's inquiry. Only one application is to be submitted for the advertised posts. If more than one is submitted, the last submitted application is accepted and the others are treated as cancelled. Candidates must check that they meet the eligibility conditions before applying. The Commission does not advise candidates on their eligibility. Male candidates with more than one living wife, and female candidates married to a man who already has a living wife, are not considered eligible unless the Governor has granted an exemption.

content_sections.heading: UPSSSC Sports Directorate Qualification
content_sections.text: The notification gives mandatory (essential) qualifications and, separately, preferential qualifications for each post. The notification states that, other things being equal, preference in direct recruitment is given to candidates with the preferential qualifications. Post-wise details are below. Equivalence of coaching-diploma institutions: the Director (Sports), Uttar Pradesh Sports Directorate, Lucknow, has informed the Commission through letters dated 14-07-2025 (attached as Annexure-1 for Deputy Sports Officer and Annexure-2 for Assistant Coach) that, besides the institutes named above, the National Sports University, Imphal, under the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, Government of India, is also recognised. The notification says any other institution will be intimated later if it is received. The notification states that the Commission's decision on a candidate's eligibility or ineligibility is final. Candidates whose application lacks the mandatory qualification, or who give false information, are liable to have their candidature cancelled.

rows.mandatory_qualification: High School examination pass certificate from Madhyamik Shiksha Parishad, Uttar Pradesh, or an equivalent certificate from a recognised institution. Practical experience in preparing and marking playing fields and courts for outdoor and indoor games. Knowledge of grafting and budding of grasses and plants such as roses, varieties of flowers and seeds, seed protection, and their sowing, transplanting and grafting.

Graduate from a recognised university. Diploma in coaching in the relevant sport from Netaji Subhas National Institute of Sports (NIS) Patiala, Bangalore or Kolkata, Lakshmibai National Institute of Physical Education (LNIPE) Thiruvananthapuram, LNIPE Gwalior, or an equivalent institution recognised by the Government of India from time to time. Two years of coaching experience.

content_sections.text: The age limit differs by post. The notification gives the age as on a reference date, as shown below. For Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and other categories notified by the government from time to time, the upper age limit is relaxed by the number of years specified. content_sections.text: At the application stage, only an online processing fee of Rs. 25.00 is charged. The application fee itself is Rs. 00 for every category. content_sections.heading: UPSSSC Sports Directorate Selection Process
content_sections.text: Selection for the advertised posts is based on a written examination, conducted under the Uttar Pradesh Group "C" direct recruitment rules, the Uttar Pradesh Sports Directorate service rules (1982 and 1986, as amended), and the new two-tier examination system adopted by the state government. The notification names no interview, physical test or other stage. Candidates must give a preference of posts at the time of document verification (record examination). The Commission will try to allot posts as far as possible on the basis of the preferences given, taking into account post availability, merit, the post's educational qualification and the age limit. The Commission's decision is final. Candidates must submit self-attested copies of mark sheets, certificates and degrees, and the application copy, when asked. The written examination has one question paper of 100 questions and a duration of two hours (120 minutes). Questions are objective, multiple-choice type. Each question carries one mark. Each wrong answer carries negative marking of 25 percent, that is one-fourth of the marks for that question. The exam date is not specified and will be notified in due course. The notification gives a detailed syllabus. The 40-mark Sports-Related Information section covers these ten areas: Exercise Physiology (energy systems, ATP production, cardiovascular and muscular adaptations, recovery and fatigue management) Sports Psychology (motivation, personality and sports performance, managing fear, anger, anxiety, aggression and stress) Sports Training (principles of training, training components, planning and periodization, talent identification) Sports Biomechanics (motion, force, levers, Newton's laws in sports, kinematics and kinetics, injury prevention) Sports Nutrition and Yoga (macronutrients, micronutrients, hydration, diet planning for athletes, balanced diet, yogic practices) Sports Medicine (common sports injuries, first aid and emergency care, massage and rehabilitation) Organization and Administration in Sports (sports organization, event management, facility and equipment management, leadership and communication) Testing, Measurement and Evaluation (physical fitness testing, skill and performance testing, body types) Application of Digital Learning and AI in Sports (digital coaching tools, AI applications, data management and statistical analysis, computer applications) International and National sports federations and bodies, major competitions, sports awards in India, and rules and regulations of sports Part-2 covers computer and IT basics (hardware and software, input and output, IP address, IT gadgets, e-mail, printer, tablet and mobile operation, MS-Word and MS-Excel, operating systems, social networking, e-governance), digital financial tools, future skills and cyber security, and developments such as AI, big data processing, deep learning, machine learning and Internet of Things. Part-3 covers the history, culture, art, architecture, festival

content_sections.heading: Reservation Provisions in UPSSSC Sports Directorate Recruitment 2026
content_sections.text: Reservation applies to Uttar Pradesh SC, ST, OBC and EWS candidates as per the latest Uttar Pradesh government orders and the requisition received from the department. EWS candidates must have family income from all sources below Rs. 8 lakh in the financial year before the year of application and must meet the conditions of the Uttar Pradesh Public Services (Reservation for Economically Weaker Sections) Act, 2020 (10 percent reservation). They need an EWS certificate issued between 01-04-2026 and 04-11-2026, based on FY 2025-26 income and valid for FY 2026-27, in the prescribed format. Candidates who are not original residents of Uttar Pradesh do not get reservation and are treated as Unreserved. A candidate claiming more than one reservation gets only one benefit, whichever is more beneficial. Ex-Servicemen must have retired from service by 04-11-2026. Dependants of Freedom Fighters and Ex-Servicemen get reservation under the Uttar Pradesh Public Services (Physically Handicapped, Dependants of Freedom Fighters and Ex-Servicemen) Reservation Act, 1993, as amended. Women of Uttar Pradesh are placed in the categories to which they belong. For Uttar Pradesh women candidates, only a caste certificate issued on the father's side is valid. Women's reservation is subject to the final decision of the Supreme Court in Special Appeal (D) No. 475/2019. Uttar Pradesh Outstanding Sportspersons must submit a certificate in the format prescribed by the competent authority, under the Uttar Pradesh Government Departments (Direct Recruitment to Group-C Posts of Outstanding Sportspersons) Rules, 2022. Persons with disabilities must hold a disability certificate issued by the competent authority in the prescribed format, stating the type and percentage of disability. The notification says posts have been re-identified to ensure 4 percent horizontal reservation, and disabled candidates must update their disability category and sub-category in the application. Candidates selected under horizontal reservation are adjusted in their own category. The notification attaches formats for the SC/ST caste certificate, OBC caste certificate, EWS income and asset certificate and self-declaration, dependant of freedom fighter certificate, and disability certificate forms (Appendix 1 to 9 and Annexure 1 to 2).

content_sections.heading: How to Apply for UPSSSC Sports Directorate Recruitment 2026
content_sections.text: If the application does not appear after payment, the fee has not been reconciled. Log in with the registration number, use "Update Your Transaction ID by Double Verification" in the Applicant Segment, and click "Verify Transaction ID". If payment fails, a Payment Acknowledgment Receipt (PAR) appears instead of the application. Use the same option and then the "Application Fee Deposition" option to pay. For SBI e-challan, download the challan, pay at any SBI branch, then enter the challan details through the "Update Your Transaction ID by Double Verification" option. After the application is finally submitted, candidates can make corrections until 11-11-2026 by logging in through the Applicant's Dashboard, clicking "Modify Application" and entering the verification code and OTP. Only the following details can be corrected: Correspondence address. Personal details such as EWS and horizontal reservation category (Dependant of Freedom Fighter, Disabled, Ex-Servicemen, Gender, Outstanding Sportsperson, etc.). Details of mandatory or preferential qualification entered in the application. Marital status. No correction is possible after the last date for correction, and the Commission does not accept separate representations for corrections.

content_sections.heading: Important Instructions for Candidates
content_sections.text: Uttar Pradesh reserved-category candidates must mark their category in the application. Candidates working in central or state government service must get a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from their employer, to be shown when the Commission asks. Self-attested copies of mark sheets, certificates and degrees must be produced to verify age and qualification when requested. The examination date, time and centre are given in the admission card. The centre, date and time are not changed in any case, and candidates should not write to the Commission about it. The Commission does not correspond individually with candidates. All information is uploaded on its website, so candidates should check it regularly. An application can be cancelled if the date of birth is not given, the candidate is overage or underage, lacks the mandatory qualification, or gives false information. Giving wrong facts that cannot be proved by certificates can lead to debarment from this and all other examinations and selections of the Commission. Malpractice, indiscipline or misbehaviour in the examination can lead to cancellation of candidature and debarment. The Uttar Pradesh Public Examination (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024 applies.

content_sections.text: Candidates who have completed their graduation or hold a sports coaching diploma can also explore more Graduate Government Jobs and Sports Quota Government Jobs available across India.
