content_sections.heading: Selection and Interview
content_sections.text: The selection process consists of three stages: Stage-I Screening test (written examination), Stage-II Driving test, and Stage-III Interview/Viva-Voce. Stage-I Screening test (40 marks): Objective Type Multiple Choices on OMR sheet of 1 hour duration containing Road Sign recognition (20 marks) and General Knowledge (20 marks). Marks obtained in the written examination will not be counted while preparing the final merit list. Candidates equal to 5 times the number of vacancies (1:5) in order of merit in the screening test will be called for the driving test. Stage-II Driving test (40 marks): Conducted on segments viz. starting, driving, parking, and after driving (10 marks for each segment). Candidates must secure at least 50% marks (20 out of 40) to qualify. Candidates equal to 3 times the number of vacancies (1:3) in order of merit in the driving test will be called for the interview. Stage-III Interview/Viva-Voce (20 marks): Includes viva-voce and document verification. Candidates must secure at least 60% marks (12 out of 20) to qualify. Final selection is based on the total marks obtained in the driving test and interview.

The selection process has two stages: a Written Test and a Trade Test. A merit list is then prepared
and final appointment depends on document verification
medical examination and verification of character and antecedents.
Eligible candidates have to appear in the Written Test
which will be conducted in one session

either in the forenoon or afternoon of the day. The test is of objective type with multiple choice questions only. There is no negative marking for wrong answers. The examination will be conducted in Kanpur
Uttar Pradesh. The exact date

time and venue will be mentioned in the Admit Card. The question papers will be as per the syllabus in Tenth Standard / Matriculation of Central / State Boards. The question paper is in three parts. Part (i) is in English and Hindi; Parts (ii) and (iii) are in English only.

Candidates are shortlisted after the Written Test based on marks obtained and the category of reservation. Candidates shortlisted on the basis of the Written Test will be called for the Trade Test. The names of shortlisted candidates will be published either on the same day or the next day of the Written Test
and the Trade Test will be conducted after shortlisting.
After the Written Test and Trade Test
a merit list is prepared on the basis of marks obtained. If more than one candidate secures equal marks (trade-cum-station wise)
the tie is resolved in the following sequence:
Date of birth
with the older candidate placed higher. Candidate with higher marks in Numerical Aptitude. Candidate with higher marks in English Language and Comprehension.
Selected candidates will be informed of their provisional selection after completion of the selection process
and no correspondence in this regard will be entertained before that. Success in the Written Test and Trade Test confers no right of appointment unless the Government is satisfied
after such enquiry as may be considered necessary
that the candidate is suitable in all respects for the service or post. The appointment letter will be strictly based on the veracity of the documents submitted with the application
including supporting documents for eligibility criteria and the reserved category certificate (not applicable for UR candidates)
as well as the Medical Examination Report
Verification of Character and Antecedents
and any other requirement mentioned in the application and specified by the Government of India.
how_to_apply: Applications for this recruitment are to be sent by post. Follow the steps below as given in the notification.
Prepare the application in the prescribed format (Appendix 'A'), typed in English on A4 size paper.
Prepare two Admit Cards as per Appendix 'B' on A4 size paper.
Arrange all documents listed in the section below, with self-attested copies where required.
Superscribe the envelope clearly with "APPLICATION FOR THE POST OF TECHNICIAN (SKILLED)" or "APPLICATION FOR THE POST OF TECHNICIAN (SEMI SKILLED)".
Send the application only by ordinary post or Speed Post to the address given below so that it reaches before the closing date.
Application Form, duly completed on the prescribed format as per Appendix 'A', typed in English on A4 size paper.
Two (02) Admit Cards as per Appendix 'B' on A4 size paper.

One (01) self-addressed envelope of size 30 cms x 12 cms affixed with a postal stamp of Rs 60/-, for sending the admit card to eligible candidates for the written test. The applicant must ensure the address is correct and legible; the organisation will not be responsible for non-receipt of the admit card due to wrong or incorrect postal address, and no overwriting on the admit card address is permitted.

Three (03) recent passport size photographs - one affixed in the appropriate box on the Application Form and two others, self-signed, affixed in the appropriate box on each of the two Admit Cards. Additional photographs are to be provided as per the Appendix and Annexure.

NOC, for candidates working in Government Service or a Public Sector Undertaking. The closing date for receipt of applications is 21 days from the date of publication of the advertisement in Employment News. For candidates residing in the areas listed in the Important Dates section, it is 28 days from the date of publication.

The application should be neatly typed on A4 size paper using Arial font, size 12. Overwriting, crossing-out or use of correction fluid is strictly prohibited. The choice on 'Yes/No' items must be indicated by placing a tick mark. The application must be printed double-sided (back-to-back), and the applicant must affix his/her signature to every page. The candidate should not bring any other paper except the Admit Card to the examination hall.
No candidate will be allowed to leave the examination hall before expiry or the prescribed time of the paper.
The use of calculating devices including logarithm-table, calculator or electronic gadgets such as mobile phone is not allowed inside the examination hall.
Candidates must abide by the instructions given by the Supervisor / Invigilator. If any candidate is found obstructing the work of invigilator, his/her candidature will be summarily cancelled.

A candidate found in possession of any incriminating articles or materials such as reading materials, books, notes and any electronic gadgets such as mobile phones, ear buds, Bluetooth devices, pen-camera, button-hole camera, scanner and so on, whether in use or not, will be deemed to have been using unfair means and is liable to penal action as deemed fit, including cancellation of candidature and debarment from future examinations conducted by the Central Government for a period of three years.

Candidates should bring a photo-bearing identity proof in original, such as Voter ID, Passport, Driving License, PAN Card or Aadhaar Card, failing which they will not be allowed to appear in the examination.
Candidates have to darken the circle in the answer sheet with a Blue or Black Ball Point Pen in the specified space on OMR sheets while filling in their particulars and answering the questions.
Candidates must sign a declaration stating that they have read and understood the above instructions for compliance.

Annexure - I: Certificate to be submitted by Central Government civilian employees seeking age relaxation. No. 36012/22/93-Estt (SCT) dated 8.9.1993 (as amended from time to time), and is issued by the District Magistrate / Deputy Commissioner or equivalent authority with seal.

Annexure - III: Undertaking to be given by the candidate who is an Ex-Serviceman / Agniveer. The candidate understands that appointment is subject to documentary evidence of due release, retirement or discharge from the Armed Forces and entitlement to benefits under the Ex-Servicemen Re-employment in Central Civil Services and Posts rules, 1979, as amended from time to time. The candidate also undertakes not to claim a vacancy reserved for Ex-Servicemen if he/she has, before such appointment, secured civil employment (including Public Sector Undertakings, Autonomous Bodies, Statutory Bodies, Nationalised Banks and so on) by availing the benefit admissible to Ex-Servicemen / Agniveer. The candidate gives the date of appointment in the Armed Forces, date of discharge, length of service in the Armed Forces and last unit / corps.

Annexure - IV: Certificate to be submitted by an EWS candidate. It certifies that the candidate belongs to the Economically Weaker Section because the gross annual income of his/her family is below Rs 8 Lakh (Rupees Eight Lakh only) for the stated financial year and the family does not own or possess any of the following assets: 5 acres of agricultural land and above; a residential flat of 1000 sq ft and above; a residential plot of 100 sq yards and above in notified municipal corporation; or a residential plot of 200 sq yards and above in areas other than notified municipal corporation. It also certifies that the candidate belongs to a caste not recognised as Scheduled Caste / Scheduled Tribe and Other Backward Classes (Central List). The notes state that income is covered from all sources (salary, agriculture, business, profession and so on), that "Family" includes the person seeking the benefit, his/her parents and siblings below 18 years, and his/her spouse and children below 18 years, and that property held by a family in different locations or cities is clubbed while applying the land or property holding test.

content_sections.heading: DGQA Technician Eligibility Criteria
content_sections.text: The DGQA Technician eligibility conditions cover nationality, qualification, age, service-related conditions, disqualifications and medical fitness. Candidates should read each condition carefully because the notification sets specific requirements for each post and category. Only Indian nationals are eligible to apply. No person is eligible for appointment who: has entered into or contracted a marriage with a person having a spouse living; or having a spouse living, has entered into or contracted a marriage with any person, provided that the Government may exempt any person from this rule if satisfied that such marriage is permissible under the personal law applicable to such person and the other party to the marriage and that there are other grounds for doing so; or is convicted or under trial for associating with criminal offences. Candidates must be in good mental and physical health and free from any physical deformity that may interfere with the efficient discharge of duties. Provisionally shortlisted candidates will have to undergo a medical examination prescribed by the Competent Authority (Government Hospital) before an offer of appointment is issued. A candidate found unfit will not be offered an appointment. Candidates diagnosed with night blindness or colour blindness, as determined by the prescribed medical authority, will be declared medically unfit for appointment to the post. They will not be considered for selection or offered appointment, irrespective of their performance at any stage of the recruitment process. The decision of the designated Medical Board / Medical Officer regarding such visual defects is final and binding. Candidature in a reserved category remains provisional until the veracity of the supporting documents is ascertained by the authority. Candidates belonging to SC/ST/EWS/OBC/PwBD must enclose the latest copy of the caste certificate or other relevant certificate issued by a Competent Authority. The benefit of reservation under EWS is applicable upon production of an Income and Asset Certificate as per Annexure - IV issued by a Competent Authority. The notification names the following as authorities who can issue the caste certificate: Chief Metropolitan Magistrate / Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate / Metropolitan Magistrate. Revenue Officer not below the rank of Tehsildar and Sub-Divisional Officer of the area where the candidate and his/her family resides. District Magistrate / Additional District Magistrate / Collector / Deputy Collector / Commissioner / Deputy Commissioner / Additional Deputy Commissioner / First Class Stipendiary Magistrate / Sub Divisional Magistrate / Taluka Magistrate / Executive Magistrate / Extra Assistant Commissioner (not below the rank of First Class Stipendiary Magistrate). Central Government civilian employees claiming age relaxation must hold a certificate in the prescribed format (Annexure - I) from their office, showing continuous service of not less than three years

Eligible candidates must also qualify a departmental Trade Skill Test in the trade of the post for which they are being considered for appointment. content_sections.heading: DGQA Technician Selection Process
content_sections.text: The selection process has two stages: a Written Test and a Trade Test. A merit list is then prepared, and final appointment depends on document verification, medical examination and verification of character and antecedents. Eligible candidates have to appear in the Written Test, which will be conducted in one session, either in the forenoon or afternoon of the day. The test is of objective type with multiple choice questions only. There is no negative marking for wrong answers. The examination will be conducted in Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh. The exact date, time and venue will be mentioned in the Admit Card. The question papers will be as per the syllabus in Tenth Standard / Matriculation of Central / State Boards. The question paper is in three parts. Part (i) is in English and Hindi; Parts (ii) and (iii) are in English only. Candidates are shortlisted after the Written Test based on marks obtained and the category of reservation. Candidates shortlisted on the basis of the Written Test will be called for the Trade Test. The names of shortlisted candidates will be published either on the same day or the next day of the Written Test, and the Trade Test will be conducted after shortlisting. After the Written Test and Trade Test, a merit list is prepared on the basis of marks obtained. If more than one candidate secures equal marks (trade-cum-station wise), the tie is resolved in the following sequence: Date of birth, with the older candidate placed higher. Candidate with higher marks in Numerical Aptitude. Candidate with higher marks in English Language and Comprehension. Selected candidates will be informed of their provisional selection after completion of the selection process, and no correspondence in this regard will be entertained before that. Success in the Written Test and Trade Test confers no right of appointment unless the Government is satisfied, after such enquiry as may be considered necessary, that the candidate is suitable in all respects for the service or post. The appointment letter will be strictly based on the veracity of the documents submitted with the application, including supporting documents for eligibility criteria and the reserved category certificate (not applicable for UR candidates), as well as the Medical Examination Report, Verification of Character and Antecedents, and any other requirement mentioned in the application and specified by the Government of India.

content_sections.heading: CRPF Sportsperson Recruitment 2026 Selection Process
content_sections.text: Selection proceeds through Identity Check, Documentation, Physical Standard Test (PST), Sports Trial Test, and Detailed/Review Medical Examination, in sequence. All candidates undergo document verification, producing original documents/certificates relating to age, education, sports achievement, domicile and category. Candidates unable to produce the prescribed originals are eliminated at this stage; those qualified proceed to the PST. Marks are awarded for the single highest medal/position achieved during the eligible window (30 September 2024 to 30 September 2026); if a candidate has more than one medal, only the highest-scoring one counts. Sample marking tiers: Height/chest relaxations are available for several categories, including Scheduled Tribes (162.5/150 cm), ST candidates of North-Eastern States (157/147.5 cm), ST candidates of Left-Wing Extremism-affected districts (160/147.5 cm), Garhwalis/Kumaonis/Dogras/Marathas and candidates from Assam, Himachal Pradesh, J&K and Ladakh (165/155 cm), candidates from the North-Eastern States of Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim and Tripura (162.5/152.5 cm), and candidates from the Gorkha Territorial Administration area of Darjeeling district (157/152.5 cm), with corresponding chest relaxations for male candidates in several of these categories. Candidates who qualify the PST undergo the Sports Trial Test, conducted by a Board of Officers. This test is purely qualifying (pass/fail) – no marks are awarded, and total marks for the merit list come only from the achievement marking scheme above. Candidates may be subjected to a Dope Test on the day of the trial; no appeal for re-conduct of the trial test is entertained. Conducted per the Uniform Guidelines for Recruitment Medical Examination for GOs and NGOs in CAPFs and AR (MHA U.O. No. A.VI-1/2014-Rectt(SSB) dated 20.05.2015 and MHA OM No. E.32012/ADG(Med)/DME/RME/DA-1/2020(Part file)/1166 dated 31.05.2021, as amended). Minimum distance vision required is 6/6 and 6/9 in both eyes without correction; colour-blind candidates are not eligible; candidates must not have knock knee, flat foot, varicose veins or squint. Tattoos are restricted in content (secular/religious symbols only, as per Indian Army norms), location (left forearm inner aspect or dorsum of hands only) and size (less than ¼ of that body part). Candidates declared unfit in DME may undergo RME. Where marks are comparable, preference follows this order: (a) International representation with Department of Sports clearance; (b) Senior/Junior National Championship representation with a medal (Senior preferred over Junior); (c) Inter-University/Khelo India University Games medal; (d) Khelo India Youth/Winter Games medal; (e) School National Games medal; (f) participation at levels (b)–(e) without a medal, in the same order.

content_sections.heading: How to Apply for CRPF Sportsperson Recruitment 2026
content_sections.text: Visit rect.crpf.gov.in and read the instructions carefully before filling the application. Create your profile and upload a copy of the certificate/document for your sports discipline, in support of your highest medal/position or highest level of participation, before applying – applications without this upload will be rejected during scrutiny. Fill the online application form and pay the application fee (where applicable) through the website only. Submit the application before 11 November 2026, 23:59 hrs . Use the correction window (12–14 November 2026) if you need to modify your submitted application. Important: The application must be submitted ONLINE only; no offline application is accepted, and candidature of anyone submitting offline will be summarily rejected. Candidates serving in Government/Semi-Government departments must submit their application through their employer along with a No Objection Certificate (as per Annexure-A format) – applications without an NOC will not be accepted.

content_sections.heading: Documents Required (Original, at Document Verification)
content_sections.text: Educational certificates, Sports certificates, Domicile and Caste certificates, etc. Matriculation/10th class certificate, for verification of Date of Birth OBC (NCL) Certificate (Annexure-F), SC/ST Certificate (Annexure-G), or EWS Certificate valid for 2026-27 (Annexure-H), as applicable – certificates in any other format are not accepted Undertaking for OBC (NCL) reservation claim, as per Annexure-F No Objection Certificate (Annexure-B), for candidates serving in Government service, produced at the time of physical document verification Certificate for claiming height/chest relaxation (Annexure-I), if applicable Four latest passport-size photographs, matching the one submitted with the application form

content_sections.heading: Important Conditions
content_sections.text: Application Fee: Male candidates belonging to UR/OBC/EWS pay Rs. 100/- through the recruitment website; the fee is exempted for all female candidates and for SC/ST/Ex-Servicemen candidates. The fee is neither refunded nor adjusted against any other recruitment process, under any circumstances. Selected candidates must submit a bond to serve the Force for a minimum of 3 years (or a specific period as prescribed), backed by an undertaking bond of Rs. 1,00,000/-, to promote sports in the Force, before they can resign for better employment elsewhere or on any other ground. Posts carry All India service liability; selected candidates are liable to serve anywhere in India or abroad, and will be governed by the CRPF Act 1949 and Rules 1955. CRPF reserves the right to modify, cancel, postpone, or reschedule any stage of the recruitment process, and to change the sequence of the recruitment procedure, without assigning any reason. Submitting fabricated documents, or documents that have been tampered with, will lead to cancellation of candidature at any stage, including at the time of document verification or later. The Board of Officers may also recommend cases of Outstanding Sportspersons who show excellent trial performance but require some relaxation in height/chest/weight for their sport, subject to approval by the Ministry of Home Affairs.

application_fee.details: Candidates, except those entitled and desirous of applying in vacancies for the SC/ST category, are required to pay a fee of Rs. 550/- (Rupees Five Hundred and Fifty Only). SC/ST candidates are exempted from payment of the fee. The fee is paid online through net banking or by using Visa/Master/Maestro/Debit Card/UPI. The E-admit card will be issued for the examination only to those candidates who have successfully paid the examination fee and who are entitled to waiver of examination fee. | Fee once paid will not be refunded under any circumstances nor can the fee be held in reserve for any other examination or selection. Candidates applying for vacancies under the SC/ST category are entitled to waiver of examination fee. Candidates are liable to be discharged/rejected at any stage of recruitment if it is found that a false SC/ST certificate has been produced to claim waiver of examination fee/other concessions as applicable. If an online payment has been made and money has been deducted from the account (i.e. unsuccessful payment), candidates should check whether fees is auto refunded to the transaction originating account, or wait for 15 working days for automatic refund of money to the account and check transaction status in the originating account. qualification.details: Online applications are invited from male and female Indian citizens possessing the educational qualifications and age prescribed for recruitment as an Enrolled Person in the Indian Coast Guard through the Staff Selection Commission. A candidate may apply for only one post. | The notification lists the following equivalent diplomas for recruitment in the Yantrik cadre in the Electrical, Mechanical and Electronics & Telecommunication (Radio/Power) Engineering branches. | Candidates are to fill marks of all subjects as mentioned in their marksheet while filling the online application. Incorrect or incomplete filling of marks in the online application will lead to cancellation of candidature. Candidates applying for the post of Yantrik and not in possession of the original diploma certificate prior to the Stage-II recruitment process must bring and upload a provisional diploma certificate duly signed by the College/University Head during Stage-II. The selection is based on performance in Stage-I

meeting the laid down medical standards during medical examination and the number of vacancies available for the post in the respective batch. Qualification in Stage-I
II
III and IV is compulsory for recruitment in ICG.
Selection of candidates for the post of Yantrik will be only for CGEPT-01/27
and for Navik (DB) and Hygienist-I only for CGEPT-02/27. Selection of candidates for the post of Navik (GD) in either CGEPT-01/27 or CGEPT-02/27 batch will be based on order of merit

available vacancies and administrative requirement. Candidates cannot claim their selection in a particular batch. All candidates will be compulsorily subjected to identity check prior to commencement of the examination at Stage-I
II and III of CGEPT. The identity check includes verification/matching at all stages of the selection procedure.
The candidate has to upload the latest photograph during registration. A live image of the candidate will also be captured during registration

and its facial features will be matched against the uploaded photograph and the real-time photo captured during the online application. The photograph in the application form will be matched with facial features and physical appearance of the candidate at all subsequent stages. Only left thumb biometric will be captured at the Stage-I recruitment centre before the online exam. If the biometric of the left thumb is not captured during Stage-I
then the biometric of the right thumb will be captured and used for subsequent verification. Apart from left and right thumb
no other finger will be considered for biometric. It is the candidate’s responsibility to check beforehand that the biometric machines are able to capture the fingerprint image. Due to Mehndi
wax
etc.
if the biometric machine is not able to capture the fingerprint image
the candidate will not be allowed to appear in the examination. Failure in even one of the identity checks at any stage will lead to cancellation of candidature.
A Computer Based Examination (CBE) with a total of 100 questions
each carrying 01 mark

will be conducted. The question paper will be bilingual (Hindi and English) and objective type (Multiple Choice Questions). Duration of the examination is one hour. There is no negative marking for wrong answers. The detailed syllabus is available at www.ssc.gov.in. Candidates will be required to bring the following documents at the reporting centre: valid original identity proof (Aadhaar Card OR PAN Card OR Voter ID card OR Driving License OR Passport) as submitted/uploaded in the online application; one printout of E-admit card (B&W printout of E-admit card will be accepted provided the candidate’s photograph
QR codes and all other details are clearly visible/legible); and two in no. passport size colour photographs as uploaded in the online application. If the exam is conducted in multiple shifts

marks scored will be normalised and these normalised scores will be used to determine final merit and cut-off marks. The result of Stage-I will be uploaded on the candidate’s dashboard on www.ssc.gov.in.
Stage-II is held at Recruitment Centres specified by ICG. Based on performance in the Computer Based Online Examination and the handling capacity of ICG Recruitment Centres
candidates will be shortlisted for Stage-II
and an E-admit card will be issued. Stage-II of candidates shortlisted for CGEPT-01/27 and CGEPT-02/27 batches will be held conjointly. To download E-admit cards

candidates are required to upload additional documents as mentioned in para 7.5 and select a preferred date and centre in a given period. Failure to upload additional documents or submit date/centre choice within the time frame promulgated by ICG will lead to cancellation of candidature. Allocation of date and centre for Stage-II exams will be on “first come first serve” basis. Candidates will be given the option to select date and centre; date and centre where seats are available will be shown to the candidates for selection. The duration of Stage-II is 1-2 days and it involves the following examination
which are only qualifying in nature:

Basic Identity and Biometric Verification: All candidates reporting for Stage-II will be allowed to enter ICG recruitment centres post basic identity check at the entrance gate and further subjected to biometric verification. Candidates whose identity cannot be verified at the entrance gate will not be allowed to enter ICG recruitment centres and will be disqualified from the recruitment process. Physical Fitness Test (PFT): Candidates undergoing PFT will do so at their own risk. All candidates are advised to be in possession of sports rig (Shoe
T-shirt

Trouser etc.). All four tests of PFT are carried out in continuity without any break. Any break in these tests will lead to failure in PFT. Assessment and Adaptability Test: Candidates qualified in PFT will undergo an online/OMR based examination to qualify for further stages of Stage-II recruitment process. This test is qualifying in nature and the marks obtained will not be included in the final merit list. The result will be announced at the venue after the conduct of the examination. Document Verification: All information provided in the online application has to match with all original documents produced by the candidate such as Class 10th/Class 12th/Diploma marksheet
identity proof (Aadhaar Card OR PAN Card OR Voter ID card OR Driving License OR Passport/Domicile/category certificate)

content_sections.text: Candidates, except those entitled and desirous of applying in vacancies for the SC/ST category, are required to pay a fee of Rs. 550/- (Rupees Five Hundred and Fifty Only). SC/ST candidates are exempted from payment of the fee. The fee is paid online through net banking or by using Visa/Master/Maestro/Debit Card/UPI. Candidates applying for vacancies under the SC/ST category are entitled to waiver of examination fee. Candidates are liable to be discharged/rejected at any stage of recruitment if it is found that a false SC/ST certificate has been produced to claim waiver of examination fee/other concessions as applicable. content_sections.heading: ICG CGEPT Selection Process
content_sections.text: The selection is based on performance in Stage-I, Stage-II, Stage-III and Stage-IV, meeting the laid down medical standards during medical examination and the number of vacancies available for the post in the respective batch. Qualification in Stage-I, II, III and IV is compulsory for recruitment in ICG. Selection of candidates for the post of Yantrik will be only for CGEPT-01/27, and for Navik (DB) and Hygienist-I only for CGEPT-02/27. Selection of candidates for the post of Navik (GD) in either CGEPT-01/27 or CGEPT-02/27 batch will be based on order of merit, available vacancies and administrative requirement. Candidates cannot claim their selection in a particular batch. All candidates will be compulsorily subjected to identity check prior to commencement of the examination at Stage-I, II and III of CGEPT. The identity check includes verification/matching at all stages of the selection procedure. The candidate has to upload the latest photograph during registration. A live image of the candidate will also be captured during registration, and its facial features will be matched against the uploaded photograph and the real-time photo captured during the online application. The photograph in the application form will be matched with facial features and physical appearance of the candidate at all subsequent stages. Only left thumb biometric will be captured at the Stage-I recruitment centre before the online exam. If the biometric of the left thumb is not captured during Stage-I, then the biometric of the right thumb will be captured and used for subsequent verification. Apart from left and right thumb, no other finger will be considered for biometric. It is the candidate’s responsibility to check beforehand that the biometric machines are able to capture the fingerprint image. Due to Mehndi, wax, etc., if the biometric machine is not able to capture the fingerprint image, the candidate will not be allowed to appear in the examination. Failure in even one of the identity checks at any stage will lead to cancellation of candidature. A Computer Based Examination (CBE) with a total of 100 questions, each carrying 01 mark, will be conducted. The question paper will be bilingual (Hindi and English) and objective type (Multiple Choice Questions). Duration of the examination is one hour. There is no negative marking for wrong answers. The detailed syllabus is available at www.ssc.gov.in. Candidates will be required to bring the following documents at the reporting centre: valid original identity proof (Aadhaar Card OR PAN Card OR Voter ID card OR Driving License OR Passport) as submitted/uploaded in the online application; one printout of E-admit card (B&W printout of E-admit card will be accepted provided the candidate’s photograph, QR codes and all other details are clearly visible/legible); and two in no. passport size colour photographs as uploaded in the online application. If the exam is conducted in multiple shifts, marks scored will be normalised

No waiver will be given for laid down medical standards. The Indian Coast Guard (ICG) order on medical standard will be the final authority.

Height standards may be reduced by up to 05 cms for candidates having domicile of Assam, Nagaland, Mizoram, Meghalaya, Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Tripura, Garhwal, Kumaon and Sikkim. Relaxation of 05 cms is also applicable to Gorkhas. Height standards may be reduced by up to 02 cms for candidates having domicile of Ladakh, Lakshadweep & Minicoy Islands and Andaman & Nicobar Islands.

Chest wall should be well proportioned and well developed. Minimum chest circumference for male candidates should be 77 cm with chest expansion of at least 05 cm. For female candidates, the chest should be well proportioned with minimum expansion of 05 cm.
Proportionate to height and age as applicable for ICG.
The candidate should have normal hearing, i.e. able to hear focused whisper from a distance of 06 m by each ear separately.

Permanent body tattoos are not permitted on any part of the body. However, certain concessions are permitted to candidates belonging to tribal areas communities as declared by the Govt. of India. For other candidates, permanent body tattoos are only permitted on inner face of forearms i.e. from inside of elbow to the wrist and on reverse side of palm/back (dorsal) side of hand.
Should have healthy gums, good set of teeth and minimum 14 dental points.

Candidate should be fit for the Armed forces, must conform to the medical standards, have normal anatomy without loss or deformity of any appendages, and be free from any active or latent, acute or chronic, medical or surgical disability or communicable disease, infection and skin ailments. Candidate shall be physically and mentally fit to perform duty in any part of the world, in any climate and terrain places.

Any candidate if found to have predominant characteristics of the opposite gender as evident on external physical examination will be rejected as unfit. Any candidate having undergone gender reassignment surgery will be declared unfit.
Any candidate, if found to be pregnant shall be disqualified and her candidature will be rejected.

The examination covers external genitalia, hernia orifices and the perineum. Any evidence of stress urinary incontinence or genital prolapse outside introitus shall lead to disqualification of the candidate.

faq.question: Q1. What is ICG CGEPT Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: It is the recruitment of Enrolled Persons in the Indian Coast Guard (ICG) through the Coast Guard Enrolled Persons Test (CGEPT) for Batches 01/2027 and 02/2027, conducted through the Staff Selection Commission for the posts of Navik (General Duty), Navik (Domestic Branch), Yantrik and Hygienist-I.

faq.question: Q2. How many vacancies are available in ICG CGEPT Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: For CGEPT-01/27, the notification lists 117 male and 13 female vacancies for Navik (GD), and 28 Yantrik (Mechanical), 23 Yantrik (Electrical) and 09 Yantrik (Electronics) vacancies. For CGEPT-02/27, it lists 117 male and 13 female vacancies for Navik (GD), 25 for Navik (DB) and 20 for Hygienist-I. The vacancies are tentative and may change.

faq.question: Q3. What is the last date to apply for ICG CGEPT Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: The last date to apply online is 21 October 2026 (1730 hrs). Applications opened on 06 October 2026 (1100 hrs).

faq.question: Q4. What is the qualification for ICG Navik and Yantrik posts?
faq.answer: Navik (GD) requires Class 12th with Maths and Physics, Navik (DB) requires Class 10th, and Hygienist-I requires Matriculation OR ITI or equivalent. Yantrik requires Class 10th plus a 03 or 04-year AICTE-approved Diploma, or Class 10th and Class 12th plus a 02 or 03-year AICTE-approved Diploma, in the specified Electrical/Mechanical/Electronics/Telecommunication (Radio/Power) Engineering branches.

faq.question: Q5. What is the age limit for ICG CGEPT Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: Navik (GD): born between 01 November 2005 and 01 May 2009. Yantrik (01/27 batch): born between 01 May 2005 and 01 May 2009. Navik (DB) (02/27 batch): born between 01 November 2005 and 01 October 2009. Hygienist-I (02/27 batch): born between 01 November 2002 and 01 October 2009. Age relaxation is 03 years for OBC and 05 years for SC/ST.

faq.question: Q6. What is the application fee for ICG CGEPT?
faq.answer: The fee is Rs. 550/-, payable online. SC/ST candidates are exempted from payment of the fee.

faq.question: Q7. How can I apply online for ICG CGEPT Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: Candidates have to log in to www.ssc.gov.in, register, fill in the online application, upload the required documents and pay the fee (if applicable) between 06 October 2026 and 21 October 2026.

faq.question: Q8. What is the selection process for ICG CGEPT?
faq.answer: Selection is based on Stage-I (Computer Based Online Examination), Stage-II (Physical Fitness Test, Assessment and Adaptability Test, document verification and recruitment medical examination), Stage-III (identity check, document verification and pre-enrolment medicals at INS Chilka) and Stage-IV (verification and authentication of documents), along with the laid down medical standards.

faq.question: Q9. What is the salary of ICG Navik, Yantrik and Hygienist-I?
faq.answer: Yantrik basic pay is Rs. 29200/- (Pay Level-5) plus Yantrik pay of Rs. 6200/-. Navik (GD), Navik (DB) and Hygienist-I basic pay is Rs. 21700/- (Pay Level-3). Dearness Allowance and other allowances are payable as per the prevailing regulations.

faq.question: Q10. What are the passing marks in the Stage-I examination?
faq.answer: The passing marks are 40 for UR/EWS/OBC and 35 for SC/ST candidates in the 100-mark Computer Based Examination. There is no negative marking.

content_sections.heading: How to Apply for APSSB Group C 2026

Upload: scanned signature on white paper in black ink (10–50 KB, JPG/JPEG/PNG); recent passport-size photograph (50–100 KB, JPG/JPEG/PNG); and copies of the educational and technical certificates relevant to the posts applied for. PwBD or PwD candidates needing a scribe or compensatory time must opt for it in the form and upload the relevant Annexure (I, IA, II or IIA from the APSSB Candidates Corner). Pay Rs. 150 online and submit. Check every entry before submitting; details cannot be edited after the closing date, and incomplete or junk entries are rejected. Four stations of 5 minutes and 10 marks each (vital signs; maternal and child health; infection control protocol; basic procedure in midwifery), qualifying 7 marks per station. Each candidate takes three of the four stations and must score 21 out of 30 . Medical fitness test for the three police and fire-service driver posts. Stages II to V are qualifying only. Final merit is on written-examination marks alone. Provisionally shortlisted candidates upload, then produce in original with self-attested copies: two photographs; Matriculation certificate for date of birth; educational, technical and registration certificates; experience certificates; APST certificate; PRC; PwBD certificate; NOC from the head of department for serving Government employees; discharge book and PPO for ex-servicemen; admit card and application printout. content_sections.text: The examination is held in the Itanagar Capital Region . The Board may cancel a venue or divert candidates; no change of date, time or centre is accepted. Calculators, laptops, mobile phones, watches and other electronic devices are banned; possession leads to debarment and legal proceedings, and centres have no storage. content_sections.heading: Who Can Apply
content_sections.text: 9th class pass from a recognised board or institution. A valid Heavy Motor Vehicle licence is mandatory, with Heavy Goods and Heavy Passenger vehicle endorsements . At least 7 years since obtaining a motor vehicle licence , of which at least 3 years holding the HMV licence . This condition does not apply to ex-servicemen who hold an HMV licence. The valid HMV licence must be in hand for the ground test and road test. Desirable: knowledge of vehicle operation and the ability to identify and fix minor faults. 10th class pass from a recognised board or institution. A valid conductor licence under the Motor Vehicles Act 1988. Candidates who do not hold one at the time of selection must produce a valid licence within one month of appointment . 10th class pass. A valid heavy driving licence under the MV Act 1988; if selected, a conductor licence must be obtained from the Motor Vehicles Department within the time fixed. At least 5 years' experience driving heavy passenger vehicles with more than 30 seats , proved by a copy of Motor Transport Workers Welfare Fund contribution or experience certificates from Government institutions. Desirable: knowledge of vehicle operation and the ability to fix minor faults. Age: 21 to 55 years on the last date for submitting the application. No relaxation is mentioned. Physical: height 158 cm; chest 76 cm (normal). Vision (Driver and Driver-cum-Conductor): distant vision 6/6 Snellen and near vision 0.5 Snellen in each eye; full vision in each eye is required. Colour blindness, any disease of the eye or eyelids, or any defect of vision in either eye is disqualifying. A medical certificate stating these vision details must be obtained from an ophthalmologist in Government service. Health: the fitness and eyesight needed to work duties of up to 10 hours under the MV Act, certified by a doctor not below the rank of Civil Surgeon and an ophthalmologist. A fitness certificate is produced to KSRTC SWIFT at the time of appointment. Conductor and Driver-cum-Conductor: must be able to read and write Malayalam and English and know basic arithmetic (addition, subtraction, multiplication, division). Police clearance: selected candidates must produce a Police Clearance Certificate from the police station of their residence within 10 days. Anyone removed from service after appointment in KSRTC SWIFT, or who left KSRTC SWIFT without authorisation after signing its contract, is not eligible under this notification. KSRTC employees may work in KSRTC SWIFT on working arrangement or deputation under a separate agreement. They continue to draw their KSRTC salary from KSRTC and receive only the eligible incentives, allowances and batta from SWIFT. KSRTC employees with five or more years' experience are given preference.

content_sections.heading: Pay and Terms of Engagement
content_sections.text: Wage: Rs. 715 for an 8-hour duty including sign-in and sign-off, fixed under Government Order G.O.(Rt) 81/2019/Fin dated 9 July 2019. One duty a day and one weekly off; attendance as per the approved duty roster. Overtime: Rs. 130 per hour beyond 8 hours, in proportion to the extra time worked. More than 5 extra hours counts as the next duty. Rest time between services is not counted as additional duty, but extra batta is considered. Allowances: kilometre allowance, night allowance and collection batta at the rates in force; incentive batta under SWIFT's incentive scheme on additional revenue; incentives for accident-free, damage-free and punctual service, clean buses, proper uniform and good passenger relations. EPF and ESI apply. Duty pattern follows the Motor Transport Workers Act 1961 and Rules 1962. Duty assignment, route selection and duty pattern are decided by management. Security deposit: at the time of signing the contract, a demand draft for Rs. 30,000 in favour of the Chairman and Managing Director, KSRTC-SWIFT, held as interest-free security for the whole period of temporary service and refunded per the contract on resignation or on retirement at 56. Service bond: candidates who complete training must serve KSRTC SWIFT for two years, with at least 240 duties a year ; otherwise the Rs. 30,000 deposit is not refunded. No guarantee of work or permanency: the company is not bound to engage everyone on the rank list; work is given by rotation and no claim lies against this. Service under this notification gives no right to permanent appointment in KSRTC, KSRTC SWIFT or any Government institution. Removal: the company may remove, without notice, employees who are irregular in attendance, breach discipline or break the contract; such persons are not re-engaged and the deposit is not refunded.

content_sections.heading: Service Conditions to Know Before Applying
content_sections.text: The annexure sets out the working terms in detail. The points most likely to affect a decision to apply: Buses run on a bus crew management system : two sets of crew (four persons) per bus, with a reserve pool to cover leave. Crew must report to the bus bay an hour before departure, check the bus inside and out, keep it clean, display destination boards and wear the prescribed uniform. Unauthorised absence or late reporting that causes a service cancellation or delayed departure is the crew's full responsibility, and the loss is recovered from them. Damage to a bus above Rs. 1 lakh caused by the crew can lead to dismissal with no liability on the company; damage below that is recovered proportionately. Buses carry cameras. Operating or taking part in a service under the influence of alcohol means immediate dismissal without notice. Conductors remit the day's collection to KSRTC's ticket and cash section or the designated bank account and submit the receipt. Passengers found without tickets by checking inspectors lead to fines or dismissal. Crew handle passenger luggage, contact online-reservation passengers in advance, help elderly and disabled passengers, change a punctured tyre with the stepney during a breakdown, and keep a visitors' book available. Repeated complaints that damage public confidence in SWIFT services lead to forfeiture of the deposit and recovery of losses.

content_sections.heading: JKSSB Recruitment 2026 Eligibility Criteria
content_sections.text: Candidates must be Domiciles of the Union Territory of Jammu & Kashmir and must possess a valid Domicile Certificate issued by the Competent Authority in the prescribed format on or before the cut-off date, i.e., 9 October 2026 (unless extended). Age is calculated as on 1 January 2026. The maximum age limit varies by category, as shown below. Every Ex-Servicemen who has served in the Armed Forces is allowed to deduct the period of such service from their actual age; if the resultant age does not exceed the prescribed maximum age limit for the post by more than 3 years, they are deemed to satisfy the age condition, provided the candidate is not born after 1 January 2008. Qualification is specific to each post and district, as listed in the vacancy tables above (Annexure-A of the notification). Candidates declared qualified/shortlisted for Document Verification must produce original certificates as proof of having acquired the prescribed qualification strictly on or before the cut-off date. Any candidate holding a qualification other than as prescribed is not eligible, and such candidature will be summarily rejected at any stage. Candidates claiming an equivalent qualification must produce an Equivalence Certificate when required by the Board. Qualification varies by post, ranging from Matriculation (Supervisor, Senior Canning Attendant) to 10+2 with a diploma (Horticulture Technician, Junior Pharmacist, Junior Staff Nurse, and other paramedical posts) to a Graduate degree with Science (Health Educator, Junior Laboratory Assistant). Full post-wise qualification is listed in the vacancy tables.

content_sections.heading: Application of Reservation
content_sections.text: Horizontal Reservation for Ex-Servicemen (ESM) and Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD) applies to the extent communicated by the indenting departments or as per extant rules. Horizontal Reservation for Ex-Servicemen applies to posts carrying pay up to Level-6E (35900-113500). An Ex-Servicemen who has already availed Horizontal Reservation on joining a post cannot avail this benefit again for subsequent employment, and must submit a sworn affidavit and a Certificate in Form-XIV at the time of document scrutiny.

content_sections.heading: JKSSB Recruitment 2026 Application Fee
content_sections.text: Fee can be paid only through online mode (Net Banking, Credit or Debit cards). Applications submitted without the prescribed fee will be summarily rejected, with no representation entertained. Fee once paid is not refunded under any circumstances and cannot be adjusted against any other examination.

content_sections.heading: JKSSB Recruitment 2026 Salary
content_sections.text: Pay scale is specific to each post, ranging from Level-2 (Rs. 19,900–63,200) for posts like Horticulture Technician Grade-IV, FMPHW, MMPHW, Junior Laboratory Assistant, and Supervisor, up to Level-6D (Rs. 35,800–113,200) for Sanitary Inspector and Level-6 (Rs. 35,400–112,400) for Health Educator. Junior Pharmacist, Para Medical Assistant, Junior Theatre Technician, Junior Ophthalmic Technician, Junior Lab Technician, and Junior Staff Nurse carry Level-4 (Rs. 25,500–81,100). Senior Canning Attendant carries Level-2 (Rs. 19,900–63,200). Refer to the vacancy tables above for the exact pay level of each specific post.

content_sections.heading: JKSSB Recruitment 2026 Selection Process
content_sections.text: Admission to the examination is provisional; the Board does not undertake detailed scrutiny of applications for eligibility at the time of the written examination. Ineligible candidates, once identified, will not be allowed to participate in subsequent stages, and issuance of an Admit Card does not confer any right to participation in later stages of selection.

content_sections.heading: Facility for Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD)
content_sections.text: Candidates with Benchmark Disabilities who are otherwise eligible and hold a valid disability certificate may avail the facility of a Scribe and/or compensatory time of 20 minutes per hour of examination, on producing a Certificate from a competent Medical Board/Authority (Annexure-B) and an Undertaking (Annexure-C). The scribe must be arranged by the candidate, must not be a candidate for the same examination, must not be from the same institution or a relative of the candidate, and must hold a lower qualification than the candidate. Candidates must have applied as a PwBD candidate at the time of application and must submit the required documents to the Observer on the day of the examination.

content_sections.heading: Document Verification (DV)
content_sections.text: Candidates shortlisted for Document Verification must appear with original documents along with self-attested photocopies, including Birth Certificate, Domicile Certificate, Category Certificate, and qualification certificates, all of which must be legally valid on or before the cut-off date. Failure to appear for DV or to produce the required original documents on the scheduled date will result in the candidate not being considered for selection. No TA/DA is paid for participation in the written test or document verification.

content_sections.heading: JKSSB Recruitment 2026 Required Documents
content_sections.text: Domicile Certificate of Jammu & Kashmir, issued by the competent authority, valid up to the cut-off date Educational qualification certificates as prescribed for the specific post Birth Certificate/Matriculation Certificate (for date of birth) Category Certificate (SC/ST-1/ST-2/OBC/EWS/ALC-IB/RBA), in the prescribed format, valid as on the cut-off date Certificate in Form-XIV for Ex-Servicemen candidates, as per Rule 18 of Jammu and Kashmir Reservation Rules, 2005 Person with Disability Certificate (self-attested) for PwBD candidates, along with Annexure-B and Annexure-C if availing Scribe/compensatory time Bonafide Certificate (Board-prescribed format) for candidates with a degree from a University/Institute outside J&K (other than Central Universities) Two recent passport-size colour photographs (not older than 6 months, with date mentioned) Original valid photo ID proof: Aadhaar Card/e-Aadhaar printout, Voter ID Card, Driving Licence, PAN Card, Passport, School/College/University ID Card, or Employer ID Card

content_sections.heading: JKSSB Recruitment 2026 Apply Online
content_sections.text: The JKSSB Recruitment 2026 apply online window is open from 10 September 2026 to 9 October 2026 (the cut-off date for domicile, qualification, and category certificates). Candidates are advised to apply well before the closing date to avoid last-minute portal congestion.

content_sections.heading: JKSSB Recruitment 2026 Important Instructions
content_sections.text: Name, date of birth, father's name, and mother's name must be entered exactly as in the Matriculation Certificate, or candidature may be cancelled at the time of Document Verification. Requests for change or correction in the application form, once submitted, will not be entertained under any circumstances. Only one application is allowed per item number; multiple applications for the same item will lead to cancellation of candidature and debarment. Requests for modification of cadre/department preferences, once filled, will not be entertained. Applications with blurred or illegible photographs/signatures will be rejected summarily. Candidates must carry two recent passport-size photographs and an original photo ID to the examination venue, failing which they will not be allowed to appear. Use of mobile phones, smartwatches, smart glasses, AI-enabled devices, or any communication-capable device is strictly prohibited in the examination hall. Candidates found using fake/fabricated applications or misusing any dignitary's name/photo are liable for legal action under the Cyber/IT Act. The decision of the Board on eligibility, selection, examination conduct, and merit list preparation is final and binding; no enquiry or correspondence will be entertained. Grievances regarding excess fee payment can be raised through the official grievance e-mail of JKSSB only; chargeback requests are not entertained.

content_sections.heading: TNPSC Group 4 Application Fee 2026
content_sections.text: One Time Registration (OTR) is valid for five years from the date of registration. Candidates who already have a valid TNPSC OTR do not need to complete a new registration only for this examination. The ₹100 examination fee must be paid while submitting the application unless the candidate is eligible for an exemption under the TNPSC rules. Applicable fee concessions and free chances vary by category and should be checked in the official notification. Payment should be made through the online modes permitted by TNPSC. Candidates claiming fee exemption must ensure that they satisfy all applicable conditions.

content_sections.heading: TNPSC Group 4 Apply Online 2026
content_sections.text: The TNPSC Group 4 online application process started on 06 October 2026 . Eligible candidates can submit the application until 05 November 2026 at 11:59 PM . Open the official TNPSC examination application portal. Complete One Time Registration if you do not already have a valid OTR. Log in using your registered credentials. Select Combined Civil Services Examination-IV / Notification No. 11/2026. Check the post options carefully before making your selection. Enter the required personal, educational and category details. Upload the required documents in the prescribed format. Pay the examination fee or claim exemption if eligible. Review all entered details carefully. Submit the application before 05 November 2026 at 11:59 PM. Save the application number and submitted application for future reference. Candidates who need to correct eligible details after submission can use the application correction window from 09 November to 11 November 2026 . Important: One Time Registration alone is not an application for TNPSC Group 4. Candidates must separately submit the online application for Notification No. 11/2026.

content_sections.heading: TNPSC Group 4 Photo and Signature Size 2026
content_sections.text: Candidates applying for the TNPSC Group 4 Notification 2026 must upload their photograph and signature in the size, dimensions and format prescribed by TNPSC. Incorrect, unclear or improperly sized images may result in problems while submitting the online application. The photograph uploaded for the TNPSC Group 4 2026 application should be a recent colour passport-size photograph taken in a photo studio against a white background . The candidate should face the camera directly, with both ears and part of the neck clearly visible. The photograph should measure 3.5 cm in width and 4.5 cm in height (130 × 170 pixels) . The image file should be between 20 KB and 50 KB , scanned at 200 DPI and saved in JPG format. The candidate's name and the date on which the photograph was taken should be printed at the bottom of the photograph. For this recruitment, the photograph should have been taken on or after 06 October 2026 , the date of the TNPSC Group 4 notification. Of the total 4.5 cm photograph height, the candidate's image should occupy approximately 3.0 cm (115 pixels) , while the name and date portion should occupy approximately 1.5 cm (55 pixels) . For the signature image, draw a box measuring 6.0 cm × 2.0 cm on a white sheet and sign inside the box using a blue or black ink pen . Scan the signature at 200 DPI and crop the image so that only the signature box is visible. The final signature should measure approximately 230 × 75 pixels and have a file size between 10 KB and 20 KB . Save it as a JPG image before uploading. Photo Size: 20 KB to 50 KB Photo Dimensions: 130 × 170 pixels Photo Physical Size: 3.5 cm × 4.5 cm Signature Size: 10 KB to 20 KB Signature Dimensions: 230 × 75 pixels Signature Physical Size: 6.0 cm × 2.0 cm Resolution: 200 DPI File Format: JPG Important: Avoid selfies, mobile-phone photographs, photocopied photographs or photographs with unsuitable backgrounds. Upload clear images in the prescribed size and format.

content_sections.heading: TNPSC Group 4 Photo Compressor – Resize Photo and Signature Online
content_sections.text: If your TNPSC Group 4 photograph or signature is larger than the prescribed upload size, you can resize and compress the image before submitting the application. Use the TNPSC Group 4 Photo Compressor and Image Resizer to adjust the photograph or signature to the required dimensions and file size. For the TNPSC Group 4 application, resize the photograph to 130 × 170 pixels and 20 KB–50 KB . The signature should be resized to 230 × 75 pixels and 10 KB–20 KB . Open the FreeJobAlert Image Resizer . Upload your TNPSC Group 4 passport-size photograph. Set the required dimensions to 130 × 170 pixels . Keep the final file size between 20 KB and 50 KB . Download the resized image and check that your face, name and photograph date are clearly visible. Upload the final JPG image while filling the TNPSC Group 4 online application. Sign with blue or black ink inside a 6.0 cm × 2.0 cm box on white paper. Scan or create a clear digital image of the signature. Open the FreeJobAlert Image Resizer . Resize the signature to 230 × 75 pixels . Keep the final file size between 10 KB and 20 KB . Save the image in JPG format and upload it to the TNPSC application portal. Tip: After compressing the photograph or signature, open the downloaded image once and make sure it is clear and not blurred before uploading it to the TNPSC portal.

Cash: Select the cash option after submitting the online application, download and print the challan, and deposit the fee in cash at any branch of State Bank of India, Canara Bank, Union Bank of India or Central Bank of India. The fee can be paid before the last date to apply or within two days after it. If the last date for fee payment is a public holiday, the next working day is treated as the last date. content_sections.heading: KFD Forest Observer Vacancy 2026
content_sections.text: KFD Forest Observer Vacancy 2026 stands at 750 posts. Of these, 700 are in the original cadre (Non-HK) and 50 are in the Kalyana Karnataka (HK) region. The posts are spread across 13 circles, and the circle-wise numbers are given below. The notification also lists vacancies for each division, wildlife unit and research or working plan circle. The unit names below are English renderings of the Kannada names in the notification. The vacancies are filled as per the Karnataka Forest Department Services (Recruitment) (Amendment) Rules 2019 (Government notification No. FEE 203 FEG 2015 dated 06.08.2019) and the reservation rules in force. The category-wise reservation breakup of the 750 posts is not given in the provided documents, because the circle-level notification format is left blank for each circle to fill. The PCCF letter states that, because of the interim order of the Hon'ble High Court, the Scheduled Caste reservation has been temporarily limited from 17% to 15%. The 400-point roster issued by the Social Welfare Department (Government order No. SAKA 515 PAKAVI 2026 dated 08.05.2026) is to be followed. In the circles of Bengaluru, Chamarajanagar, Chikkamagaluru, Kanara, Kodagu, Mangaluru, Mysuru and Shivamogga, 50% of the Forest Observer posts in the notified wildlife divisions and tiger reserves are reserved for Local Forest Dwelling Tribes candidates (see the reservation section below). The PCCF letter dated 30.06.2026 refers to 25 backlog posts left unfilled from an earlier direct recruitment (310 Forest Watcher posts), taking the total to 775 (750 vacancies + 25 backlog). The backlog table in the provided PDF is rotated and not clearly legible, and the circle-level notification format and the extension letter refer to the 750 vacancies. This article therefore uses 750 as the vacancy figure.

content_sections.heading: KFD Forest Observer Eligibility Criteria
content_sections.text: To be eligible for KFD Forest Observer Recruitment 2026, candidates must meet all the conditions below, along with the qualification and age limit given in the next sections. The candidate must be a citizen of India. A male candidate with more than one living wife, or a female candidate married to a man who already has a wife, is not eligible for appointment without prior permission of the Government. The candidate must be mentally and physically healthy and free from any physical defect likely to interfere with efficient performance of duties. The candidate must meet the physical standards and pass the physical endurance and physical efficiency tests described below. The recruiting authority may reject a candidate as physically unfit on the advice of a medical board, and the Government's discretion is not limited by these rules. Applying online does not by itself make a candidate eligible for appointment. A candidate is considered to have accepted all the Acts, rules and regulations of the Government on applying.

content_sections.heading: KFD Forest Observer Qualification
content_sections.text: The educational qualification for KFD Forest Observer is SSLC. The candidate must hold the SSLC examination conducted by the Karnataka Secondary Education Examination Board, or an equivalent qualification, on the last date to apply. As per Government circular No. CASUE 81 SENENI 2017 dated 27.02.2018, the following are treated as equivalent to SSLC: Class 10 examination conducted by CBSE and ICSE boards, or Class 10 examination conducted by other State Government examination boards, or Secondary-level course conducted by the National Institute of Open Schooling (NIOS), or Secondary-level course conducted by the Karnataka Secondary Education Examination Board (KOS). Candidates who have not received the result of the prescribed qualification, or who do not hold the marks card, as on the last date to apply are not eligible. No other qualification is considered in place of the above. If a candidate is found to lack the prescribed qualification at any stage, the candidature is cancelled, and the decision of the recruiting authority is final.

content_sections.heading: KFD Forest Observer Age Limit
content_sections.text: The minimum age is 18 years on the date the notification is issued. The maximum age limits are given below as on the notification start date. As per Government order No. CASUE 262 SENENI 2025 dated 29.01.2026, a one-time relaxation of 5 years has been added to these limits for recruitment notifications issued up to 31.12.2027. The exact calendar date used to calculate age is not stated in the provided PDFs, as the circle-level notification format leaves the notification date blank.

content_sections.text: KFD Forest Observer Application Fee depends on the category and gender of the candidate. The fee is not refundable under any circumstances and cannot be adjusted against any other examination or recruitment of the department. Persons with disabilities are exempted from the application fee, as per Government circular No. CASUE 431 SENENI 2016 dated 28.12.2016. Payment must be made on or before the last date fixed for fee payment. Cash: Select the cash option after submitting the online application, download and print the challan, and deposit the fee in cash at any branch of State Bank of India, Canara Bank, Union Bank of India or Central Bank of India. The fee can be paid before the last date to apply or within two days after it. If the last date for fee payment is a public holiday, the next working day is treated as the last date. Applications for which the fee is not paid within the prescribed period are treated as incomplete and rejected. content_sections.heading: KFD Forest Observer Reservation Details
content_sections.text: Reservation is applied as per the Karnataka Civil Services (Direct Recruitment) (General) Rules 2021 and the Karnataka Forest Department Services (Recruitment) (Amendment) Rules 2019. The notification includes the following reservation provisions. Caste and category reservation: Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe, Category-I, IIA, IIB, IIIA and IIIB. Certificates must be in the prescribed formats: Form D for Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe, Form E for Category-I, and Form F for Category IIA, IIB, IIIA and IIIB, obtained from the Tahsildar and valid on the last date to apply. Backward class certificates are valid for 5 years. Ex-servicemen: Candidates with the prescribed discharge and no-objection documents. BSF, CRPF and CISF personnel are not treated as ex-servicemen. Persons with disabilities: For this post (Forest Watcher – Group D), only the categories LC (Leprosy Cured), AAV (Acid Attack Victims) and MI (Mental Illness) are eligible under the disability reservation, as per Government notification No. WCD 111 PHP 2022 dated 19.08.2023. Candidates must have at least 40% disability and must not have any other disability. Project-displaced families: Candidates from families displaced by projects, with the prescribed Tahsildar certificate (Form-3). Families displaced more than 25 years before the date of the rules do not qualify. Kannada medium: Candidates who studied from Class 1 to Class 10 in Kannada medium, with the prescribed certificate. Rural candidates: Candidates who studied from Class 1 to Class 10 in a rural area, with the Form-2 certificate. General candidates claiming rural reservation must also have Form-1 (non-creamy layer) and Form-2. Candidates of reserved categories whose caste certificate is rejected and who lack a Non-Creamy Layer certificate are not eligible for rural reservation. application_fee.details: The WBPSC Clerkship application fee is Rs. 110 plus service charges, wherever applicable, payable through online mode only. | The fee is not refundable and will not be held in reserve for any other examination.

age_limit.details: The age limit for WBPSC Clerkship Recruitment 2026 is not below 18 years and not more than 45 years as on 01.01.2024. (Non-Creamy Layer)/PwBD/MSP/Ex-Servicemen is entertained after the application is submitted.

qualification.education_qualification: Madhyamik or equivalent, with computer operation and typing skill
qualification.details: The qualification for direct recruitment is as follows: | Passed the Madhyamik examination of the West Bengal Board of Secondary Education or its equivalent. Elementary knowledge of computer operation, with the ability to type on a computer at 20 words per minute in English or 10 words per minute in Bengali. | Candidates must choose the typing option (English or Bengali) at the time of submitting the application. The computer and typing ability is judged only after a candidate qualifies in Part-I and Part-II. | The candidate must be a citizen of India (natural or by registration), or another national declared eligible by the Government of India. A candidate in the second category needs a certificate of eligibility issued by the Government; such a candidate may be admitted to the examination, but the offer of appointment is made only after the certificate is issued. Ability to read, write and speak Bengali is required. This is not required for candidates whose mother tongue is Nepali. Knowledge of Bengali will be tested for candidates whose mother tongue is other than Bengali or Nepali, at the time of the computer and typing test. The candidature of candidates with average or poor performance in this test is liable to be cancelled.

salary_details.details: The WBPSC Clerkship salary is in Level 6 of the pay structure, with a scale of Rs. 22,700 to Rs. 58,500. Dearness Allowance (D.A.), Medical Allowance (M.A.) and House Rent Allowance (H.R.A.) are admissible as per ROPA, 2019.

selection_process: Category Qualifying Marks
UR 40%
EWS 40%
OBC 38%
SC 35%
ST 30%
PwBD 30%
Ex-Servicemen 30%
Meritorious Sports Person 40%
The selection under WBPSC Clerkship Recruitment 2026 has two examination stages followed by a computer and typing test.

Part-I (Objective Type): held first. A limited number of candidates who obtain qualifying marks are allowed to appear in Part-II. Part-II (Conventional Type – Written): held on a later date to be notified by the Commission. Test of computer operation and typing: judged only for candidates found qualified in Part-I and Part-II.
The final merit list is prepared on the basis of total marks obtained in Part-I and Part-II

provided the candidate qualifies in the computer operation and typing test. A candidate who qualifies for Part-II but does not appear in it will not be considered for the final merit list. The selected candidates also undergo a medical examination and police verification of antecedents before appointment.
The Commission has fixed category-wise qualifying marks in aggregate
taking Part-I and Part-II together.
The Commission may further relax qualifying marks if a sizeable number of posts in reserved categories remain unfilled.
There is negative marking of 0.25 mark for each wrong answer in multiple choice questions. In Part-II
10% of full marks is deducted from a paper if the candidate writes a name
roll number or any identifying mark in the answer script. Tie-breaking: higher aggregate marks in English and Bengali/Hindi/Urdu/Nepali/Santali first
then higher marks in English

content_sections.heading: WBPSC Clerkship Eligibility Criteria
content_sections.text: The qualification for direct recruitment is as follows: Passed the Madhyamik examination of the West Bengal Board of Secondary Education or its equivalent. Elementary knowledge of computer operation, with the ability to type on a computer at 20 words per minute in English or 10 words per minute in Bengali. Candidates must choose the typing option (English or Bengali) at the time of submitting the application. The computer and typing ability is judged only after a candidate qualifies in Part-I and Part-II. The candidate must be a citizen of India (natural or by registration), or another national declared eligible by the Government of India. A candidate in the second category needs a certificate of eligibility issued by the Government; such a candidate may be admitted to the examination, but the offer of appointment is made only after the certificate is issued. Ability to read, write and speak Bengali is required. This is not required for candidates whose mother tongue is Nepali. Knowledge of Bengali will be tested for candidates whose mother tongue is other than Bengali or Nepali, at the time of the computer and typing test. The candidature of candidates with average or poor performance in this test is liable to be cancelled.

content_sections.text: The age limit for WBPSC Clerkship Recruitment 2026 is not below 18 years and not more than 45 years as on 01.01.2024. In terms of date of birth, candidates should be born not earlier than 2 January 1979 and not later than 1 January 2006. Only the age recorded in the Madhyamik or equivalent certificate is accepted, and the limits apply to all candidates, whether in Government service or not. No claim for being a member of S.C./S.T./O.B.C. (Non-Creamy Layer)/PwBD/MSP/Ex-Servicemen is entertained after the application is submitted.

content_sections.heading: WBPSC Clerkship Selection Process
content_sections.text: The selection under WBPSC Clerkship Recruitment 2026 has two examination stages followed by a computer and typing test. Part-I (Objective Type): held first. A limited number of candidates who obtain qualifying marks are allowed to appear in Part-II. Part-II (Conventional Type – Written): held on a later date to be notified by the Commission. Test of computer operation and typing: judged only for candidates found qualified in Part-I and Part-II. The final merit list is prepared on the basis of total marks obtained in Part-I and Part-II, provided the candidate qualifies in the computer operation and typing test. A candidate who qualifies for Part-II but does not appear in it will not be considered for the final merit list. The selected candidates also undergo a medical examination and police verification of antecedents before appointment. The Commission has fixed category-wise qualifying marks in aggregate, taking Part-I and Part-II together. The Commission may further relax qualifying marks if a sizeable number of posts in reserved categories remain unfilled. There is negative marking of 0.25 mark for each wrong answer in multiple choice questions. In Part-II, 10% of full marks is deducted from a paper if the candidate writes a name, roll number or any identifying mark in the answer script. Tie-breaking: higher aggregate marks in English and Bengali/Hindi/Urdu/Nepali/Santali first, then higher marks in English, then higher age. qualification.education_qualification: SSC/Xth/Matriculation or equivalent (12th pass desirable)
qualification.details: Nationality: The applicant must be a citizen of India. Essential Qualification: SSC/Xth/Matriculation or equivalent. Desirable Qualification: Intermediate/XIIth Class pass. Job Requirement: Physical maintenance of records of the section, general cleanliness and upkeep of the section, carrying files and documents to other sections, photocopying, delivering the dak, opening and closing the section/room, dusting of furniture, preparation and supply of tea/coffee to officials/guests, and any other work assigned by superior officers. Mere possession of the essential qualification does not entitle a candidate to be called for the written examination. A Screening/Selection Committee may adopt its own criteria to shortlist candidates. Candidates working on regular/permanent posts in Government Departments, Autonomous Bodies or PSUs must upload a 'No Objection & Vigilance Certificate' (Annexure-XI) stating that they will be relieved within one month of receipt of appointment orders. CSIR-NCL will not accept any person on lien or deputation basis. Applicants must disclose whether any close relatives are permanent employees of CSIR-NCL or any other CSIR laboratory/institute. If a candidate's Board/University awards CGPA/grades, the conversion into percentage as per the Board/University formula must be uploaded.

salary_details.details: Pay Level: Level 1 as per the 7th CPC Pay Matrix (Rs. 18,000 - 56,900). Total Emoluments: Approximately Rs. 40,000/- per month, calculated on the minimum of the scale including HRA in a Class 'X' city. Allowances: Dearness Allowance (DA), House Rent Allowance (HRA), Transport Allowance (TA) and other allowances admissible to central government employees and made applicable to CSIR. Council employees are also eligible for accommodation as per CSIR allotment rules, depending on availability, in which case HRA is not admissible. Other Benefits: New Pension Scheme (NPS), reimbursement of medical expenses, Leave Travel Concession (LTC) and career advancement opportunities as per extant CSIR rules. Probation: 2 years from the date of joining, which may be extended or curtailed at the discretion of the Competent Authority.
