content_sections.heading: CSIR NCL MTS Recruitment 2026 Vacancy Details
content_sections.text: A total of 24 vacancies have been notified for the Multi-Tasking Staff (MTS) post under Post Code MTS-01. Out of the 24 posts, 1 post is reserved for the PwBD (HH) category. Blind and Low Vision (B, LV). Deaf and Hard of Hearing (D, HH). Locomotor disabilities: One Arm, Both Arms, One Leg, Both Legs, One Arm and One Leg, Cerebral Palsy, Leprosy Cured, Dwarfism, Acid Attack Victims, Muscular Dystrophy (OA, BA, OL, BL, OAL, CP, LC, Dw, AAV, MDy). Autism Spectrum Disorder (Mild), Specific Learning Disability and Mental Illness (ASD (M), SLD, MI). Multiple Disabilities involving the above categories (MD).

content_sections.heading: Eligibility Criteria
content_sections.text: Nationality: The applicant must be a citizen of India. Essential Qualification: SSC/Xth/Matriculation or equivalent. Desirable Qualification: Intermediate/XIIth Class pass. Job Requirement: Physical maintenance of records of the section, general cleanliness and upkeep of the section, carrying files and documents to other sections, photocopying, delivering the dak, opening and closing the section/room, dusting of furniture, preparation and supply of tea/coffee to officials/guests, and any other work assigned by superior officers. Mere possession of the essential qualification does not entitle a candidate to be called for the written examination. A Screening/Selection Committee may adopt its own criteria to shortlist candidates. Candidates working on regular/permanent posts in Government Departments, Autonomous Bodies or PSUs must upload a 'No Objection & Vigilance Certificate' (Annexure-XI) stating that they will be relieved within one month of receipt of appointment orders. CSIR-NCL will not accept any person on lien or deputation basis. Applicants must disclose whether any close relatives are permanent employees of CSIR-NCL or any other CSIR laboratory/institute. If a candidate's Board/University awards CGPA/grades, the conversion into percentage as per the Board/University formula must be uploaded.

content_sections.heading: Salary/Stipend
content_sections.text: Pay Level: Level 1 as per the 7th CPC Pay Matrix (Rs. 18,000 - 56,900). Total Emoluments: Approximately Rs. 40,000/- per month, calculated on the minimum of the scale including HRA in a Class 'X' city. Allowances: Dearness Allowance (DA), House Rent Allowance (HRA), Transport Allowance (TA) and other allowances admissible to central government employees and made applicable to CSIR. Council employees are also eligible for accommodation as per CSIR allotment rules, depending on availability, in which case HRA is not admissible. Other Benefits: New Pension Scheme (NPS), reimbursement of medical expenses, Leave Travel Concession (LTC) and career advancement opportunities as per extant CSIR rules. Probation: 2 years from the date of joining, which may be extended or curtailed at the discretion of the Competent Authority.

content_sections.heading: Age Limit (as on 04-11-2026)
content_sections.text: SC/ST: 5 years OBC (Non-Creamy Layer): 3 years PwBD (UR): 10 years PwBD (OBC): 13 years PwBD (SC/ST): 15 years (maximum age of a PwBD applicant on the closing date must not exceed 56 years) Ex-Servicemen (UR): 3 years after deduction of the actual military service rendered from the actual age as on the closing date. Ex-Servicemen (OBC/SC/ST): 6 years for OBC and 8 years for SC/ST after deduction of the actual military service rendered. Widows/Divorced Women/Women judicially separated and not remarried: Up to 35 years (UR/OBC) and up to 40 years (SC/ST). Any other age relaxation is as per extant GoI/DoPT/CSIR recruitment rules. SC/ST/OBC (NCL) age relaxation is available only for posts reserved for the respective category. Candidates applying against posts not reserved for them are treated on par with unreserved candidates, though fee exemption still applies to eligible candidates.

content_sections.heading: Application Fee
content_sections.text: UR/OBC/EWS Candidates: Rs. 500/- (plus processing fee/transaction charges, wherever applicable) Women/SC/ST/PwBD/Ex-Servicemen Candidates: Nil Payment Mode: Online through RuPay Debit Card, Credit/Prepaid Cards, Net Banking, UPI, Wallets, NEFT and SBI Branch Payment only. The fee is non-refundable under any circumstances and cannot be adjusted against any other examination or selection. Payment attempts are limited to a maximum of six. If a payment transaction remains unresolved, the candidate must wait 20 minutes from the payment initiation time before a new attempt. No fee exemption applies to departmental candidates or candidates employed under Central/State Government, Autonomous Bodies or PSUs.

content_sections.heading: Selection Process
content_sections.text: A Competitive Written Examination will be conducted for all provisionally eligible candidates. The final merit list will be prepared only on the basis of performance in the written examination, followed by document verification. Mode: OMR based or Computer Based objective type multiple choice examination. Duration: 2 hours. Standard: Class 10th. Medium: Questions are set in both English and Hindi, except the questions on English Language. Answer Key: A tentative answer key will be made available on the CSIR-NCL recruitment website after the examination, and candidates can submit representations within the stipulated time with supporting evidence. There is no provision for re-evaluation or re-checking of scores. Normalization: If the examination is held in multiple shifts, marks will be normalized as per the CSIR formula (Annexure-XIII). Tie-break: Equal aggregate marks are resolved in this order: lesser negative marks, older candidate, candidate who acquired the essential degree earlier, and alphabetical order of first names. Document Verification: Before the offer of appointment, candidates must produce the originals of the documents uploaded with the application, failing which the candidature is likely to be rejected. No Travelling Allowance will be paid for the written examination or any other stage.

Only a single online application has to be submitted. The selection process involves a single-stage Computer Based Test (CBT) and Aptitude Test (wherever applicable)
followed by Document Verification and Medical Examination. Selection is made strictly on merit based on these stages. The date
time and venue of all activities will be fixed by RRC and intimated to eligible candidates in due course. Requests for postponement or change of venue
date and shift will not be entertained under any circumstances.

The CBT has questions and answer options only in English and Hindi. There is negative marking in the CBTs for all categories of posts: 1/3rd of the marks allotted for each question is deducted for each wrong answer. There is no supplementary exam for absentee candidates under any circumstances. Candidates absent on the scheduled date and session will be disqualified without further notice. The syllabus and examination pattern are the same as prescribed by RRB for Direct Recruitment
except the ALP category
for which a revised pattern is given in Annexure-A (as per RBE 28/2026 dated 23.03.2026).
The subject-wise distribution is indicative
and question papers may vary. There will be a separate CBT for each pay level of Technician posts. A virtual calculator is available on the computer monitor during the JE CBT.

and Basic Science and Engineering follow the RRB Direct Recruitment syllabus for ALP. The Trade Specific Section is based on the syllabus prescribed by the Directorate General of Training (DGT) under MSDE for the relevant trades
available at www.dgt.gov.in. Technician Gr-I S&T: General Awareness
Basics of Computers and Applications
Mathematics
and Basic Science and Engineering (including Electricity and Magnetism
and Electronics and Measurements). Technician Gr-III: Mathematics
and General Science (Physics
Chemistry and Life Sciences of 10th standard level) with General Awareness. Junior Engineer: General Awareness
Physics and Chemistry (up to 10th standard CBSE syllabus)
Basics of Environment and Pollution Control
and Technical Abilities framed on the syllabus of the chosen Exam Group (Civil and Allied
Electrical and Allied
Electronics and Allied
or Mechanical and Allied Engineering). NTPC (Non-Graduate): Mathematics
and General Awareness.

The topic-wise syllabus for each group is given in Annexures A to D of the official notification and is not reproduced in full here. The topics listed in the notification are illustrative and not necessarily exhaustive.
Candidates equal to 8 (eight) times the number of ALP vacancies for each notified community/category (UR
OBC (NCL)
SC
ST) are shortlisted for CBAT based on CBT marks. If more than one candidate obtains marks equal to the cut-off
all of them are shortlisted. Each test battery/section of CBAT must be cleared separately. All candidates
irrespective of community
must secure a minimum T-score of 42 in each test battery separately
with no relaxation. CBAT is only in English and Hindi
with no negative marking. The merit list is prepared only from candidates qualifying in CBAT
with 50% weightage to CBT marks and 50% weightage to CBAT score (Railway Board's letter no. 2023/E(RRB)/25/38-A dated 16.04.2026). For CBAT information
the notification refers candidates to the RDSO website (rdso.indianrailways.gov.in).
The CBTST is of qualifying nature

and its marks are not added for merit. Candidates equal to eight times the number of vacancies for each community are called. Candidates should be able to type 30 words per minute (WPM) in English or 25 WPM in Hindi on a Personal Computer without editing tools and spell check. Kruti Dev and Mangal fonts are available for Hindi typing. Exemption may be extended to candidates permanently disabled due to Blindness/Low Vision
Cerebral Palsy and Locomotor Disability with not less than 40% permanent disability
who must upload or produce the Typing Skill Test Exemption Certificate issued by the Competent Medical Board before the test.

These percentages may be relaxed by 2% for PwBD candidates if there is a shortage of PwBD candidates against the vacancies reserved for them. The marks scored in CBT are used for shortlisting candidates for further stages. Candidates equal to the number of vacancies are called for Document Verification
based on merit in CBT and the preference for post/exam group given. Tie-break: the older candidate is placed higher in merit; if the age is also the same

alphabetical order (A to Z) of the name is used. Normalization: raw marks are used for single-session papers and normalized marks for multi-session papers to compute a Merit Index. Merit Index = Sq + (St − Sq) × (M − Mq) / (Mt − Mq)
where M is the marks obtained
Mq is the qualifying marks for the general category candidate (40)
Mt is the mean marks of the top 0.1% or top 10 candidates (whichever is larger)
Sq is 350 (score assigned to Mq) and St is 900 (score assigned to Mt). A combined merit list of candidates from different disciplines/Exam Groups is prepared in descending order of the Merit Index
and allotment of preference is done on that basis. Post/Unit is allotted as per the candidate's options
subject to merit
reservation policy and vacancy position on the date of finalizing the panel. Once empanelled
candidates forfeit the right to be considered for any other post/category.

how_to_apply: Visit the official website of RRC/NCR, www.rrcpryj.org, and open the link for filling the application for GDCE Notification No. RRC/NCR/GDCE/01/2026.
Click on the "New Registration" link.
Fill in the personal information, e-mail address and mobile number. An e-mail/SMS will be received on the registered e-mail ID/mobile number with the registration number and password.
Login using the registration number and password.
Follow the instructions and complete the registration process step by step, including the post preference and exam group.
Upload the scanned copy of the photograph, self-attested certificates in proof of date of birth, educational/technical qualifications and caste certificate (SC/ST/OBC), and submit the application.

Name, Father's Name and Date of Birth must match the Matriculation or equivalent certificate as well as the service records. Candidates need not send printouts of the application or certificates to RRC by post.
Proof of Date of Birth, and disability certificate for PwBD.
Certificate of Educational/Technical Qualification for the post applied.
For SC/ST candidates: Community certificate in the prescribed format as per Annexure-G.

For OBC candidates: valid Community certificate in the prescribed format as per Annexure-H, specifically indicating that the candidate does not belong to the creamy layer, plus the self-declaration as per Annexure-H (1).

Employee Service Certificate as per Annexure-I, filled by the applicant with signature and thumb impression (same as uploaded in the application) and verified by the immediate supervisor with signature, seal and mobile number.
Passport size colour photograph and specimen signature, in JPEG format.
The application also asks for Division/PU, Community, Employee ID No., Aadhar No., two visible marks of identification, and nearest Railway Station and Station Code.
important_instructions: Applications are to be submitted online only through the link on www.rrcpryj.org. Candidates are advised to beware of fake websites and job racketeers. RRC does not appoint any agent or coaching centre for recruitment. Candidates must have their own valid and active mobile number and personal e-mail ID for the entire examination process. RRC will not entertain any request to change the mobile number or e-mail ID after submission of the application. Candidates should register well before the closing date to avoid last-minute load on the website. RRC will not bear responsibility if a candidate cannot register within the last date and time. Post preference, once opted, is treated as final and no change is permissible. Candidates with partial options are considered only for the posts/categories they opted for. Not giving an option for certain posts/categories is treated as unwillingness for them. Eligibility is considered only on the basis of information furnished in the online application. False or incorrect information or suppression of relevant information leads to rejection of candidature. Candidates should note and preserve their Registration Number for further stages. Signatures and photographs must be identical at all stages of the selection process. Candidates should keep at least 12 copies of the same photograph. Candidates must ensure they meet the medical standards for the post. Appointment is subject to medical fitness, final verification of educational and community certificates, and verification of antecedents/character. Selected employees are liable to be posted anywhere in North Central Railway, and the decision of the Railway administration is final. Selection by RRC does not confer any right of appointment. RRC only recommends names to the concerned units of North Central Railway, which issue the offer of appointment letter.
Applications are liable to be rejected on grounds including the following (the list is illustrative and not exhaustive):

Applications sent manually and not registered online. More than one application by the same candidate for the same post. Candidates submitting multiple applications, including with minor changes in information, will be summarily rejected and debarred from all future examinations of RRBs and RRCs. Not possessing the prescribed educational qualifications at the time of submitting the application. Missing or improper scanned photograph, signature, LTI and other documents. Invalid photographs (black and white, with cap or sunglasses/goggles, disfigured, small size, full body, one-side view, unrecognizable, photostat copy, group photo, selfie, photo taken by mobile, morphed photo, or no photo). Signature in capital/block/disjointed letters. Missing certificates in the prescribed format for date of birth, educational qualification and caste. Incomplete or incorrectly filled applications.
If an application is rejected, candidates can view the status and reasons online on www.rrcpryj.org, and SMS/e-mail alerts are also sent. The decision is final and binding.

E-Call Letters are to be downloaded from the official website of RRC. No call letter is sent by post. For the CBT, candidates must bring their Railway Identity card and a sparing letter (with the candidate's photo) bearing the signature and stamp of the concerned Supervisor/Controlling Officer, with the photo attested. Name, date of birth and photo on the ID must match the online application. Candidates must bring the colour photograph (35 mm x 45 mm) uploaded with the application, and an original valid Photo ID. Candidates must write the Self-Declaration paragraph, sign and affix LTI at the venue in the presence of the invigilator only. Writing it in advance or signing in capital letters leads to rejection. Banned items inside the exam hall include mobile phones, Bluetooth devices, pen drives, laptops, calculators, wrist/smart watches, other communication devices, pen/pencil, wallets/purses, belts, shoes and metallic wear including ornaments. For Document Verification, candidates must bring all required documents in original, along with two sets of self-attested photocopies. Certificates must be in English or Hindi in the prescribed formats. Candidates absent during Document Verification will have their candidature cancelled. Candidates who want to be considered against reserved vacancies or seek age relaxation must submit the relevant original certificate in the prescribed format at Document Verification; otherwise they will be considered under General (UR) if eligible.

Any candidate using unfair means, sending someone else in their place or attempting to impersonate will be debarred from all examinations of all RRCs and RRBs for lifetime, in addition to departmental disciplinary action and possible legal prosecution. The notification refers to The Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act and Rules, 2024, as amended on 31.07.2026. RRC may conduct post-examination analysis including log analysis, photograph and biometric verification and CCTV footage review.

content_sections.heading: RRC NCR GDCE Eligibility Criteria
content_sections.text: Eligible and serving regular employees (except RPF/RPSF) having lien in North Central Railway can apply against the GDCE quota. All eligible regular and serving railway employees of NCR can fill the online application form. No minimum service condition is prescribed, as per RBE 72/2024 dated 02.08.2024. Regular and eligible NCR employees who have the prescribed educational qualification for Direct Recruitment and work in grades lower than the grade/pay scale for which GDCE is being conducted can appear for all categories. Regular and eligible employees with the prescribed educational qualification for Direct Recruitment who work in the same grade/pay scale for which GDCE is being conducted can appear for selection from Non-Safety to Safety category posts as well as Safety to Safety category posts. Candidates must fulfil all notified eligibility criteria on or before the closing date for submission of the application. Date of Birth and educational qualifications must be updated in the Service Records and in HRMS; otherwise the application is liable to be cancelled. Employees in a higher grade than the grade of the notified post. Employees who do not have the requisite educational qualification, medical standard and age criteria prescribed in the notification. Trainee or Substitute employees who are not regularized. RPF/RPSF personnel (as per Railway Board's letter No. E(NG)I/2002/PM2/9 dated 11.08.2003). Law Assistant, Catering Inspector and Accounts Cadre (as per Railway Board's letter No. E(NG)I/2000/PN2/12 dated 21.08.2001, RBE No. 165/2001). Candidates appearing in, or awaiting results of, the final examination for the minimum qualification at the time of applying. Candidates who have resigned or been transferred from North Central Railway at any stage of the selection process. Candidates are not allowed to apply for the same post on which they are presently working.

content_sections.heading: RRC NCR GDCE Qualification
content_sections.text: Candidates must hold the minimum educational qualification for the post from a recognized Board/ University/ Institute as on the closing date for online application submission, as per Annexure-F. The qualification must also be endorsed in the Service Record of the employee, otherwise the candidature will be rejected. Those awaiting results of the final examination of the prescribed qualification should not apply. Qualification notes from the notification: for JE and ALP posts, higher qualifications such as B.E./B.Tech are also acceptable in lieu of a three-year Diploma in Engineering in the same disciplines. Diploma/Degree in Engineering will not be accepted in lieu of Course Completed Act Apprentices/ITI for the post of Technicians in Pay Level-2 unless otherwise specified, and a Graduate Act Apprentice will not be accepted in lieu of Course Completed Act Apprenticeship (CCAA), as per RBE 13/2019 dated 16/01/2019. Please note: Annexure-F groups the JE qualifications in merged cells, and it lists ten JE rows, while Annexure-E lists eleven JE categories (for example JE / Drawing (Electrical), JE / TMC and JE (Mech.) do not appear by the same names in Annexure-F). Candidates should check the exact qualification for their post in Annexure-F of the official notification. Candidates must indicate the ITI trade from which they wish to appear in the Qualifying Test for ALP and Technician posts, and the Exam Group for the "Technical Abilities" part of the JE examination. For ALP, candidates holding a Degree/Diploma select the relevant trade against their engineering discipline as shown below. A candidate holding more than one minimum educational qualification mapped to different Exam Groups can choose any one Exam Group, provided the candidate opts for post(s) whose educational qualification is mapped to the chosen exam group. Such candidates would still be eligible for all the opted posts as per educational qualification.

content_sections.heading: RRC NCR GDCE Age Limit
content_sections.text: The upper age limit for UR candidates is 42 years, for OBC candidates 45 years and for SC/ST candidates 47 years. The lower and upper age limits are reckoned as on 01.01.2027 (both dates inclusive). The lower limit is 18 years for all communities/categories. Note on a discrepancy in the notification: the age-group table in the notification labels the OBC column as "18 to 47 Years", while clause 2.1 and the OBC date of birth (02.01.1982) point to an upper limit of 45 years. The table above follows clause 2.1 and the date of birth; candidates should confirm this with the official notification. No age relaxation is allowed to SC/ST/OBC-NCL (Non-Creamy Layer) candidates applying against unreserved vacancies. Proof of age: any one of the Birth Certificate issued by the competent authority, OR the Class 10th (or equivalent) Certificate/Mark Sheet indicating the date of birth, OR the School Leaving Certificate clearly mentioning the date of birth, and the same recorded in the service record of the employee. Candidates should ensure that they meet the prescribed age limit as on the specified cut-off date. You can use our Age Calculator to check your exact age and confirm your eligibility before applying.

content_sections.heading: RRC NCR GDCE Reservation
content_sections.text: Vertical reservation for SC, ST and OBC (Non-Creamy Layer) is admissible wherever applicable. SC/ST candidates must furnish a Caste Certificate in the format at Annexure-G, and OBC-NCL candidates in the format at Annexure-H, at the time of Document Verification. OBC-NCL candidates must also furnish a declaration in the format at Annexure-H (1) that they do not belong to the creamy layer. The certificate should not be older than one year at the time of Document Verification. If these stipulations are not complied with, the OBC-NCL claim will not be entertained and the candidate, if otherwise fulfilling the General (UR) conditions, will be considered under General (UR) vacancies only. There is no separate reservation of posts for Economically Weaker Sections (EWS), as per Railway Board's letter No. E(NG)I-2018/PM1/23 dated 02/05/2019 (RBE No. 72/2019). The crucial date for the claim of SC/ST/OBC status or any other benefit such as reservation and age relaxation, where not specified otherwise, is the closing date for submission of online applications. Reservation for PwBD is a horizontal reservation and is applicable in GDCE, as per Railway Board's letter No. E(NG)1-2019/PM4/8 dated 27.12.2022.

content_sections.heading: RRC NCR GDCE Salary
content_sections.text: The notification does not specify the salary or pay amount for the posts. It gives only the 7th CPC pay level of each post. During any prescribed training, payment will be regulated as per extant rules. The medical standards are indicative and not exhaustive. Candidates should read Chapter 5 of the Indian Railway Medical Manual (IRMM) Volume I, which can be accessed at www.indianrailway.gov.in. A candidate who fails to pass the prescribed medical fitness for the post will not be considered suitable for empanelment. Annexure-F shows the suitability of each post for persons with benchmark disabilities. The table below lists the entries as given in the notification. "No" means the post is not marked suitable for that disability category. Abbreviations as given in the notification: AAV = Acid Attack Victim, B = Blind, BL = Both Legs, D = Deaf, DW = Dwarfism, HH = Hard of Hearing, HI = Hearing Impairment, ID = Intellectual Disability, LC = Leprosy Cured, LD = Locomotor Disability, LV = Low Vision, MD = Multiple Disability, MW = Muscular Weakness, OA = One Arm, OL = One Leg, OAL = One Arm and One Leg, PwBD = Persons with Benchmark Disabilities, VI = Visually Impairment. SD and SI are used in the notification without an expansion. Selected PwBD candidates will be medically examined by Railway Medical Authorities at the time of Document Verification, and only those conforming to the medical standards in the Indian Railway Medical Manual and other extant provisions will be eligible for appointment.

content_sections.heading: RRC NCR GDCE Selection Process
content_sections.text: Only a single online application has to be submitted. The selection process involves a single-stage Computer Based Test (CBT) and Aptitude Test (wherever applicable), followed by Document Verification and Medical Examination. Selection is made strictly on merit based on these stages. The date, time and venue of all activities will be fixed by RRC and intimated to eligible candidates in due course. Requests for postponement or change of venue, date and shift will not be entertained under any circumstances. The CBT has questions and answer options only in English and Hindi. There is negative marking in the CBTs for all categories of posts: 1/3rd of the marks allotted for each question is deducted for each wrong answer. There is no supplementary exam for absentee candidates under any circumstances. Candidates absent on the scheduled date and session will be disqualified without further notice. The syllabus and examination pattern are the same as prescribed by RRB for Direct Recruitment, except the ALP category, for which a revised pattern is given in Annexure-A (as per RBE 28/2026 dated 23.03.2026). The subject-wise distribution is indicative, and question papers may vary. There will be a separate CBT for each pay level of Technician posts. A virtual calculator is available on the computer monitor during the JE CBT. ALP: Mathematics, General Intelligence and Reasoning, and Basic Science and Engineering follow the RRB Direct Recruitment syllabus for ALP. The Trade Specific Section is based on the syllabus prescribed by the Directorate General of Training (DGT) under MSDE for the relevant trades, available at www.dgt.gov.in. Technician Gr-I S&T: General Awareness, General Intelligence and Reasoning, Basics of Computers and Applications, Mathematics, and Basic Science and Engineering (including Electricity and Magnetism, and Electronics and Measurements). Technician Gr-III: Mathematics, General Intelligence and Reasoning, and General Science (Physics, Chemistry and Life Sciences of 10th standard level) with General Awareness. Junior Engineer: General Awareness, Physics and Chemistry (up to 10th standard CBSE syllabus), Basics of Computers and Applications, Basics of Environment and Pollution Control, and Technical Abilities framed on the syllabus of the chosen Exam Group (Civil and Allied, Electrical and Allied, Electronics and Allied, or Mechanical and Allied Engineering). NTPC (Non-Graduate): Mathematics, General Intelligence and Reasoning, and General Awareness. The topic-wise syllabus for each group is given in Annexures A to D of the official notification and is not reproduced in full here. The topics listed in the notification are illustrative and not necessarily exhaustive. Candidates equal to 8 (eight) times the number of ALP vacancies for each notified community/category (UR, OBC (NCL), SC, ST) are shortlisted for CBAT based on CBT marks. If more than one candidate obtains marks equal to the cut-off, all of them are shortlisted. Each test batt

content_sections.heading: RRC How to Apply for NCR GDCE Recruitment 2026
content_sections.text: Visit the official website of RRC/NCR, www.rrcpryj.org, and open the link for filling the application for GDCE Notification No. RRC/NCR/GDCE/01/2026. Click on the "New Registration" link. Fill in the personal information, e-mail address and mobile number. An e-mail/SMS will be received on the registered e-mail ID/mobile number with the registration number and password. Login using the registration number and password. Follow the instructions and complete the registration process step by step, including the post preference and exam group. Upload the scanned copy of the photograph, self-attested certificates in proof of date of birth, educational/technical qualifications and caste certificate (SC/ST/OBC), and submit the application. Name, Father's Name and Date of Birth must match the Matriculation or equivalent certificate as well as the service records. Candidates need not send printouts of the application or certificates to RRC by post. Proof of Date of Birth, and disability certificate for PwBD. Certificate of Educational/Technical Qualification for the post applied. For SC/ST candidates: Community certificate in the prescribed format as per Annexure-G. For OBC candidates: valid Community certificate in the prescribed format as per Annexure-H, specifically indicating that the candidate does not belong to the creamy layer, plus the self-declaration as per Annexure-H (1). Employee Service Certificate as per Annexure-I, filled by the applicant with signature and thumb impression (same as uploaded in the application) and verified by the immediate supervisor with signature, seal and mobile number. Passport size colour photograph and specimen signature, in JPEG format. The application also asks for Division/PU, Community, Employee ID No., Aadhar No., two visible marks of identification, and nearest Railway Station and Station Code.

content_sections.heading: RRC NCR GDCE Important Instructions for Candidates
content_sections.text: Applications are to be submitted online only through the link on www.rrcpryj.org. Candidates are advised to beware of fake websites and job racketeers. RRC does not appoint any agent or coaching centre for recruitment. Candidates must have their own valid and active mobile number and personal e-mail ID for the entire examination process. RRC will not entertain any request to change the mobile number or e-mail ID after submission of the application. Candidates should register well before the closing date to avoid last-minute load on the website. RRC will not bear responsibility if a candidate cannot register within the last date and time. Post preference, once opted, is treated as final and no change is permissible. Candidates with partial options are considered only for the posts/categories they opted for. Not giving an option for certain posts/categories is treated as unwillingness for them. Eligibility is considered only on the basis of information furnished in the online application. False or incorrect information or suppression of relevant information leads to rejection of candidature. Candidates should note and preserve their Registration Number for further stages. Signatures and photographs must be identical at all stages of the selection process. Candidates should keep at least 12 copies of the same photograph. Candidates must ensure they meet the medical standards for the post. Appointment is subject to medical fitness, final verification of educational and community certificates, and verification of antecedents/character. Selected employees are liable to be posted anywhere in North Central Railway, and the decision of the Railway administration is final. Selection by RRC does not confer any right of appointment. RRC only recommends names to the concerned units of North Central Railway, which issue the offer of appointment letter. Applications are liable to be rejected on grounds including the following (the list is illustrative and not exhaustive): Applications sent manually and not registered online. More than one application by the same candidate for the same post. Candidates submitting multiple applications, including with minor changes in information, will be summarily rejected and debarred from all future examinations of RRBs and RRCs. Not possessing the prescribed educational qualifications at the time of submitting the application. Missing or improper scanned photograph, signature, LTI and other documents. Invalid photographs (black and white, with cap or sunglasses/goggles, disfigured, small size, full body, one-side view, unrecognizable, photostat copy, group photo, selfie, photo taken by mobile, morphed photo, or no photo). Signature in capital/block/disjointed letters. Missing certificates in the prescribed format for date of birth, educational qualification and caste. Incomplete or incorrectly filled applications. If an application is rejected, candidates can view the status and reasons online on www.rrcpryj.org, and SMS/e-ma

faq.question: Q1. What is NCR GDCE Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: NCR GDCE Recruitment 2026 is the General Departmental Competitive Examination recruitment notified by the Railway Recruitment Cell, North Central Railway, Prayagraj, under Notification No. RRC/NCR/GDCE - 01/2026 dated 28.09.2026. It invites online applications from eligible serving regular employees (except RPF/RPSF) having lien in North Central Railway for posts against the GDCE quota.

faq.question: Q2. How many vacancies are available in NCR GDCE 2026?
faq.answer: The post-wise vacancies in Annexure-E add up to 656: 428 for Assistant Loco Pilot, 61 for Technician posts, 60 for Junior Engineer posts and 107 for NTPC (Non-Graduate) posts. The notification does not state a separate grand total, and the vacancies are provisional.

faq.question: Q3. What is the last date to apply for NCR GDCE 2026?
faq.answer: The last date is 30.10.2026 at 23:59 hrs. Online applications open on 01.10.2026.

faq.question: Q4. Who can apply for NCR GDCE 2026?
faq.answer: Only eligible serving regular employees (except RPF/RPSF) having lien in North Central Railway can apply. No minimum service condition is prescribed as per RBE 72/2024 dated 02.08.2024. Outside candidates cannot apply under this notification.

faq.question: Q5. What is the qualification for NCR GDCE 2026?
faq.answer: It depends on the post. ALP and Technician posts require Matriculation/SSLC plus ITI or Course Completed Act Apprenticeship in specified trades (with Diploma or Degree options for ALP and Technician-I, and 10+2 with Physics and Maths as an option for Technician-III Sig & Tele). JE posts require a three years Diploma in the specified Engineering disciplines (B.E./B.Tech acceptable in lieu of Diploma), and the clerk posts require 12th (+2) with not less than 50% marks in the aggregate, with relaxations as stated in the notification.

faq.question: Q6. What is the age limit for NCR GDCE 2026?
faq.answer: The lower age limit is 18 years for all categories. The upper age limit is 42 years for UR, 45 years for OBC and 47 years for SC/ST, reckoned as on 01.01.2027.

faq.question: Q7. How can I apply online for NCR GDCE 2026?
faq.answer: Candidates can apply online only through the link on the official website www.rrcpryj.org. They need to complete "New Registration", log in with the registration number and password received by e-mail/SMS, fill in the details with post preference, and upload the required documents and photograph.

faq.question: Q8. What is the selection process for NCR GDCE 2026?
faq.answer: The selection process has a single-stage CBT, followed by an Aptitude Test for ALP (CBAT) or a Typing Skill Test for Junior Clerk cum Typist (CBTST), Document Verification and Medical Examination. Selection is strictly on merit.

faq.question: Q9. What is the salary for NCR GDCE 2026 posts?
faq.answer: The salary amount is not specified in the notification. The posts fall under 7th CPC Pay Levels 2 (ALP, Technician-III, Junior Clerk cum Typist), 3 (Commercial cum Ticket Clerk), 5 (Technician-I) and 6 (Junior Engineer).

faq.question: Q10. Is there negative marking in the NCR GDCE CBT?
faq.answer: Yes. 1/3rd of the marks allotted for each question is deducted for every wrong answer in the CBTs. There is no negative marking in the Computer Based Aptitude Test (CBAT).

content_sections.heading: Southern Railway Scouts and Guides Vacancy 2026
content_sections.text: The 12 Southern Railway Level 1 posts are distributed at two posts each among Chennai, Tiruchchirappalli, Madurai, Palakkad, Thiruvananthapuram and Salem divisions. The advertised posts are open to all eligible candidates irrespective of community. There is no separate reservation for any community under the Scouts and Guides Quota.

content_sections.heading: Educational Qualification
content_sections.text: Candidates must possess any one of the following qualifications: Passed Class 12 or an equivalent examination with at least 50% marks in aggregate; or Passed Matriculation from a recognized board with a Course Completed Act Apprenticeship for technician categories; or Passed Matriculation from a recognized board with an ITI qualification approved by NCVT for technician categories. The requirement of 50% marks in Class 12 is not applicable to SC, ST and ex-servicemen candidates or candidates possessing qualifications higher than Class 12. Candidates must possess one of the following qualifications: Class 10 pass; or ITI or an equivalent qualification; or National Apprenticeship Certificate granted by NCVT; or Class 10 with ITI; or Class 10 with a National Apprenticeship Certificate granted by NCVT.

content_sections.heading: Scouts and Guides Qualification
content_sections.text: Candidates must satisfy all the following Scouts and Guides requirements: Must be a President’s Scout, Guide, Rover or Ranger, or a Himalayan Wood Badge holder in any section. Must have been an active member of a Scouts organization for the last five years. Must possess a Certificate of Activeness in the prescribed format. Must have attended two events at the National Level or All Indian Railway level. Must have attended two events at the State Level.

content_sections.heading: Age Limit as on 1 January 2027
content_sections.text: Serving Railway employees with the prescribed continuous or broken service may receive relaxation up to 40 years for UR, 43 years for OBC and 45 years for SC/ST candidates. Widows, divorced women and women judicially separated but not remarried may receive relaxation up to 35 years for UR, 38 years for OBC and 40 years for SC/ST. Eligible Jammu and Kashmir domiciled candidates may receive five years of relaxation. Eligible Casual Administrative Office staff may receive age relaxation according to the prescribed conditions. Ex-servicemen will receive relaxation according to applicable service and category rules.

content_sections.heading: Deoghar Home Guard Vacancy 2026 Details
content_sections.text: The vacancies below are described in the notification as provisional in nature and may be revised (increased, decreased, or modified) without prior notice. 50% of posts in both Rural and Urban Home Guard categories are earmarked for women. In the Urban Home Guard category, 50% of vacancies are earmarked for technically skilled candidates. If suitable candidates are not available in one sub-category (technical/non-technical), the vacancy will be filled from the other. Of the posts earmarked for women, 5% are reserved for eligible divorced/deserted/widowed women candidates. If such candidates are not available, these posts revert to the general women's quota.

content_sections.heading: Deoghar Home Guard Eligibility Criteria
content_sections.text: Rural Home Guard: The candidate must be a permanent resident of the same block in Deoghar district from which they are applying, supported by a self-attested residence certificate issued by the competent authority. Urban Home Guard: The candidate must be an ordinary resident of the urban area of Deoghar district, supported by a self-attested residence certificate issued by the competent authority.

content_sections.heading: Deoghar Home Guard Age Limit
content_sections.text: Candidates must be between 19 and 40 years of age as on 01.01.2026 for both Rural and Urban Home Guard posts. The notification does not specify any separate upper age relaxation for reserved categories. To avoid any confusion regarding age eligibility, candidates can use our Age Calculator to calculate their exact age based on the prescribed cut-off date before applying.

content_sections.heading: Deoghar Home Guard Qualification
content_sections.text: Candidates must attach self-attested certificates supporting their claimed educational qualification. Candidates seeking relaxation in physical standards must attach a caste certificate issued by the competent authority. Candidates applying for the technically skilled Urban Home Guard vacancies must be skilled in a technical field and either employed in a related office or self-employed with relevant technical knowledge. The notification lists the following as generally recognised technical categories: doctor, engineer, advocate, lecturer/professor, nurse, computer operator, typist, licensed driver (HMV/LMV), cook, carpenter, cobbler, washerman, barber, electrician, gardener, plumber, and similar trades. A technical proficiency certificate issued by the competent authority is required.

content_sections.text: As stated explicitly in the notification, this is a voluntary enrolment and not a salaried government post. There is no fixed monthly salary. content_sections.heading: Deoghar Home Guard Selection Process
content_sections.text: Selection is conducted as per the Home Department, Government of Jharkhand notification No. 5442 dated 20.10.2014, through the following stages: Physical Efficiency Test (PET): Comprising a 1-mile race, high jump, long jump, and shot put, with marks awarded on a sliding scale for each event. Separate scoring standards apply for (i) Rural and Non-Technical Urban candidates, and (ii) Technically skilled Urban candidates, with separate benchmarks for male and female candidates in each. Hindi Writing Ability Test: Qualifying in nature, for candidates who clear the PET. Rural candidates are tested at a 7th-class level and Urban candidates at a 10th-class level. Full marks: 100; qualifying marks: 30. Technical Skill Test: Applicable only to technically skilled Urban Home Guard candidates who clear the PET and Hindi Writing Test. Qualifying in nature. Full marks: 100; qualifying marks: 30. Merit List, Document Verification, Medical Examination & Police Verification: A merit list is prepared based on the notified provisions after all tests are completed, and selection is made against available vacancies. Selected candidates' certificates, medical fitness, and police character verification are checked before appointment. Basic Training & Enrolment: Selected candidates undergo basic Home Guard training on the orders of JGRV Headquarters, Ranchi. On successful completion of training, they are formally enrolled as Home Guards and issued an enrolment certificate. Government servants may be enrolled as Urban Home Guards up to a limit of 10% of the total Urban Home Guard vacancies. Marks are awarded based on educational qualification:

faq.question: Q7. How can I apply online?

how_to_apply: Visit the official website, www.pgimer.edu.in, and use the Recruitment link on the home page.
Register using a valid personal email ID and mobile number (required for the initial registration and kept active throughout the process).

Fill in mandatory registration details - Advertisement No., Advertisement Date, Name (as per matriculation certificate), Date of Birth, Mobile No. & Email ID - carefully, as these cannot be changed once registered.
Log in with the User ID and password sent to your email/mobile, and complete the section-wise Application Form: personal information, qualification(s), experience(s), and document uploads.

Upload a scanned photograph in JPG/JPEG format (50–80 KB), snapped on or after 1 June 2026, with the candidate's name and the date of the photograph clearly visible; no cap or goggles (spectacles allowed); the photograph should be unattested.

Upload legible scanned copies of all required certificates (educational qualification from Matric onwards, date of birth, category certificate, experience certificates, NOC from present employer if applicable).
Submit the form and complete payment via Net Banking/Credit Card/Debit Card only.

Take a printout of the submitted application form for your records. Candidates already in government/semi-government/autonomous body employment must also forward their application through proper channel to the Administrative Officer, Recruitment Cell, within 10 days of the closing date.
important_instructions: Candidature is purely provisional at all stages; candidates not meeting the eligibility conditions will be cancelled at any stage without notice. No entries in the Registration Form or Application Form can be changed once submitted; incorrect entries may lead to rejection with no scope for reconsideration. Candidates should not bring water bottles, car key remotes, chains, mobile phones, pagers, pens, wrist watches, rings, wallets, purses, or any electronic device into the examination hall. Roll numbers/admit cards are available for download roughly one week before the exam and will not be sent by post. There is no provision for re-checking/re-evaluation of the CBT, and question papers/answer keys are not provided to candidates, though objections on specific questions may be emailed to [email protected] within 3 days of the exam. Candidates in employment must forward their application through proper channel within 10 days of the closing date; a No Objection Certificate is mandatory for departmental candidates. Canvassing in any form will disqualify the applicant, and use of unfair means or impersonation may lead to criminal prosecution and permanent debarment. Disputes are subject to the jurisdiction of Chandigarh Courts alone.

content_sections.heading: PGIMER Chandigarh Selection Process
content_sections.text: Selection is through a Computer Based Test (CBT), followed by an interview only for Group "A" posts. The CBT is in English only, held on an all-India basis at the notified examination cities. Each question carries 1 mark, with negative marking of 0.25 marks for each wrong answer. Minimum qualifying marks are 40% for General/EWS and 35% for SC/ST/OBC (separately for CBT and interview); reserved-category candidates applying against an unreserved post must secure 40%. For Group B & C (Non-Gazetted) posts, the Government of India has dispensed with the interview, so selection is based on CBT merit only. For Group A posts, there is a 15-mark interview in addition to the CBT. Shortlisting for document verification is done at 3 times the number of advertised posts (plus ties) where no skill test is prescribed, or 5 times the number of posts (plus ties) where a skill test is prescribed. Final selection is based on CBT marks only for Group B & C, and on CBT + interview marks for Group A. Tie cases are resolved first by fewer wrong answers/negative marks, then by earlier date of birth, then by higher aggregate percentage in 10+2, then by higher percentage in Matriculation. Examination cities (tentative): Amritsar, Bengaluru, Bhopal, Chandigarh/Mohali, Dehradun, Delhi/NCR, Hyderabad, Jaipur, Jammu, Kolkata, Lucknow, Patna, and Shimla. The city of examination, once chosen and allotted, cannot be changed.

content_sections.text: Candidates need to pay a non-refundable application fee online as per their category. content_sections.heading: RMLIMS Recruitment 2026 Age Limit
content_sections.text: For all posts mentioned in this recruitment, candidates must have attained the age of 18 years and must not have attained the age of 40 years as on the last date of submission of the online application. SC/ST/OBC and other specified categories of Uttar Pradesh: upper age relaxation as specified by the Government, maximum up to 5 years as per relevant Government Orders Permanent government employees with at least 3 years of regular and continuous service in the relevant field: relaxation up to 5 years Physically handicapped candidates (General category): up to 5 years for Group-B posts and 10 years for Group-C posts Physically handicapped candidates (OBC/SC/ST): up to 10 years for Group-B posts and 15 years for Group-C posts Ex-servicemen and dependents of Freedom Fighters: relaxation as per Government of India rules This age relaxation is admissible only to candidates who are domicile of Uttar Pradesh; candidates from other states are eligible to apply only against Unreserved (UR) vacancies

content_sections.heading: RMLIMS Recruitment 2026 Selection Process
content_sections.text: Selection will be made through a two-stage Computer Based Test (CBT), conducted bilingually in Hindi and English. Screening Examination: Qualifying in nature, held only to shortlist candidates for the Main Examination. Marks from this stage are not carried forward, and only 10 times the number of advertised posts (category-wise) are shortlisted for the Main Exam Main Examination: Final selection is based solely on marks obtained in this exam, prepared category-wise based on merit and reservation norms Exam Pattern: Both Screening and Mains exams carry 100 marks each, of 2 hours' duration, consisting only of Multiple Choice Questions (MCQs) — 60 marks on the subject related to the post, 10 marks each on General English, General Knowledge, Reasoning, and Mathematical Aptitude Negative Marking: 1 mark is awarded for each correct answer; 0.25 mark is deducted for each wrong answer Qualifying Marks: 50% for Unreserved and EWS candidates; 40% for SC, ST, OBC and PwBD candidates Skill Test: Conducted after the Main Exam for the Stenographer post (Stenography/Typing Test in English or Hindi, Mangal or Krutidev 10 font). Candidates equal to five times the advertised posts (category-wise) are shortlisted; the Skill Test is qualifying in nature and its marks are not counted in the final merit

content_sections.heading: Nagaland Police Constable Recruitment 2026 Important Dates
content_sections.text: Online registration for Nagaland Police Constable GD Recruitment 2026 will begin on 31 October 2026. Candidates must complete the application and pay the examination fee by the closing date of 30 November 2026. Admit cards will be generated after successful completion of the online application and may be downloaded immediately thereafter. Written examination and interview schedules will be communicated through the official Nagaland Police website and local newspapers.

content_sections.heading: Nagaland Police Constable Vacancy 2026
content_sections.text: Nagaland Police has advertised 1,137 Constable GD vacancies. Of these, 1,053 vacancies are allocated through the current recruitment under the approved tribal ratio, while 84 are backlog vacancies from the previous recruitment.

content_sections.heading: Nagaland Police Constable District-wise Vacancy 2026
content_sections.text: The 1,053 regular recruitment vacancies are distributed among participating districts according to the approved tribal ratio based on the 2011 Census. The district allocation also includes separate male and female vacancies. The original notification provides detailed tribe-wise allocations within these districts in Annexure I. Applicants must check the specific tribe and district allocation before selecting their application district.

content_sections.heading: Nagaland Police Constable Backlog Vacancy 2026
content_sections.text: The notification also provides 84 backlog Constable GD vacancies reserved for specific tribes and districts whose vacancies remained unfilled in the preceding recruitment. All 84 backlog vacancies are allocated to male candidates. Special Condition: The single Phom backlog vacancy under Mokokchung is restricted to eligible members of the Phom tribe belonging to Anaki (Old) and Anaki 'C' villages. Candidates applying for backlog posts must satisfy the exact district, residence and tribe conditions provided in Annexure III.

content_sections.heading: Nagaland Police Constable Eligibility Criteria 2026
content_sections.text: The educational qualification for Nagaland Police Constable GD Recruitment 2026 depends on the applicant's tribe classification. Candidates must also possess valid documents establishing their Indigenous Inhabitant and tribal eligibility. The educational qualification must be from a recognized board or educational authority. Where a pass certificate or provisional pass certificate has not been issued, the notification requires an appropriate certificate or letter from the concerned educational institution or authority. The recruitment is open to eligible male and female candidates from Indigenous Inhabitant Tribes of Nagaland who meet the prescribed age, education, district and physical fitness requirements. Applicants must possess an Indigenous Inhabitant Certificate and relevant tribal certificates issued by the competent authority. Eligible natives or residents of Dimapur, Chumoukedima and Niuland can apply under the combined allocation for these three districts, provided they possess the prescribed supporting certificates. The notification also provides specific arrangements for members of the Chang, Sumi and Phom tribes from identified villages in Mokokchung, Wokha and Shamator districts. Candidates affected by these provisions should refer to the detailed conditions in the official notification.

content_sections.heading: Nagaland Police Constable Age Limit 2026
content_sections.text: Serving Government employees may receive upper-age relaxation equivalent to their qualifying service, subject to a maximum of five years and the applicable Government policy. The notification also provides age-relaxation conditions for certain incumbent Nagaland Police Constables and petitioners covered by the specified Gauhati High Court judgments and orders.

content_sections.heading: Nagaland Police Constable Salary 2026
content_sections.text: The advertised Constable GD posts carry Pay Level 3, with Grade Pay Rs. 1,800 under the specified pay-band structure of Rs. 5,200–20,200.

content_sections.heading: Nagaland Police Constable Application Fee 2026
content_sections.text: The examination fee for Nagaland Police Constable Recruitment 2026 is Rs. 300 . Applicants must pay the fee online as part of the application process.

content_sections.heading: Nagaland Police Constable Selection Process 2026
content_sections.text: Selection for the Constable GD posts involves physical and medical screening, outdoor physical efficiency tests, an objective-type written examination, interview and NCC certification assessment. Candidates must qualify in the required physical and medical standards before participating in outdoor tests. Only candidates who qualify the PET will be called for the written examination.

content_sections.heading: Nagaland Police Constable Physical Standard Test 2026
content_sections.text: The notification prescribes different minimum height and chest measurements for male and female candidates. Candidates who do not meet the physical requirements may be disqualified during the recruitment process.

content_sections.heading: Nagaland Police Constable Physical Efficiency Test 2026
content_sections.text: The Physical Efficiency Test carries 45 marks and includes running, pull-ups, high jump and long jump. Male and female candidates have separate qualifying standards. Disqualification: Male candidates taking longer than 12 minutes 30 seconds and female candidates taking longer than 12 minutes will be disqualified. Nagaland Police Constable Syllabus 2026 Male candidates completing fewer than six pull-ups and female candidates completing fewer than three pull-ups will be disqualified. A maximum of three attempts is permitted. Candidates who fail to meet the required qualifying standard in any of the outdoor tests will not be permitted to continue in the recruitment process.

content_sections.heading: Nagaland Police Constable Written Exam Pattern 2026
content_sections.text: The Nagaland Police Constable written examination will consist of 80 multiple-choice questions carrying 40 marks. Candidates will receive two hours to complete the question paper, which will be set in English.

content_sections.heading: Nagaland Police Constable Written Exam Syllabus 2026
content_sections.text: The written examination may cover the following subjects and knowledge areas specified in the official notification: General Awareness and General Knowledge General Science Indian History Indian Polity Social Sciences Elementary Mathematics Sports Naga Culture and Heritage Nagaland State and Naga Tribes General Mental Aptitude

content_sections.heading: Nagaland Police Constable Interview and NCC Marks 2026
content_sections.text: After the PET and written examination, candidates will be shortlisted for interview based on the aggregate marks obtained in these two stages. The shortlisting ratio is three candidates for each available post. The interview carries 10 marks, and NCC certification may contribute up to 5 additional marks to the overall merit assessment.

content_sections.heading: Nagaland Police Constable Medical Fitness Requirements
content_sections.text: Candidates must satisfy the medical fitness standards prescribed for police service. Medical examination includes assessment of height, weight, chest, vision, hearing and physical fitness. The notification identifies several disqualifying conditions, including: Eyesight below the prescribed standard. Colour blindness. Deafness or serious hearing impairment. Varicose veins. Squint eyes. Amputated limbs or physical extremities. Physical deformities, including flat feet and knocked knees. Adverse drug screening or alcohol abuse test findings. Candidates must also satisfy the medical and physical requirements during the recruitment process and subsequent training.

content_sections.heading: How to Apply Online for Nagaland Police Constable Recruitment 2026
content_sections.text: Eligible applicants must submit their applications through the Nagaland Police Registration Portal between 31 October and 30 November 2026. Offline applications will not be accepted. Important: Applicants must submit only through the official online recruitment portal. Applications submitted to police offices or other establishments will not be accepted.

content_sections.heading: Nagaland Police Constable Documents Required 2026
content_sections.text: Original documents must be produced whenever required during the recruitment process. Applicants should ensure that the details submitted online match their supporting certificates.

content_sections.heading: Nagaland Police Constable Probation and Posting
content_sections.text: Selected candidates will undergo a probation period of two years. Service confirmation will depend on satisfactory completion of probation, medical clearance and verification of antecedents under the applicable rules. Fresh recruits will initially be deployed in India Reserve (IR) Battalions and may be required to serve within or outside Nagaland according to the instructions of the Nagaland Police Department.

Write "आवेदन ग्राम पंचायत सचिव हेतु आवेदन 2026" on the main envelope enclosing all documents.

content_sections.heading: Indian Army TES 57 Recruitment 2026 Important Dates
content_sections.text: Online registration for Indian Army TES 57 begins on 14 October 2026 at 12:00 noon. Candidates must complete the application by 12 November 2026 at 12:00 noon. The SSB interview process is tentatively scheduled for February–March 2027. The actual SSB interview dates, selection centre details and reporting instructions will be communicated through the Indian Army recruitment system.

content_sections.heading: Indian Army TES 57 Vacancy 2026
content_sections.text: The Indian Army has announced 90 provisional vacancies for the 10+2 Technical Entry Scheme - 57. Selected candidates will undergo engineering and military training before being considered for Permanent Commission in the Army. The number of vacancies is subject to change based on the training capacity of Cadets Training Wings and the Indian Army's requirements.

content_sections.heading: Indian Army TES 57 Eligibility Criteria 2026
content_sections.text: Candidates applying for Indian Army TES 57 Recruitment 2026 must have passed Class 12 with Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics, secured at least 60% aggregate marks in these three subjects and appeared in JEE Main 2026. The entry is open to unmarried male candidates who satisfy the prescribed nationality, age and medical standards. Must have passed Class 12 or an equivalent examination from a recognized education board. Must have studied Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics (PCM). Must have secured a minimum aggregate of 60% marks in PCM. The PCM percentage is calculated using Class 12 marks in Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics. Must have appeared in JEE Main 2026. Yes. Appearing in JEE Main 2026 is mandatory for TES-57. The Indian Army will shortlist eligible applicants using the JEE Main 2026 Common Rank List (CRL). Meeting the Class 12 PCM percentage requirement alone does not guarantee an SSB interview call. The 60% requirement applies to the aggregate marks obtained in Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics in Class 12. Candidates must enter their actual PCM percentage up to two decimal places without rounding it off. The notification allows unmarried male candidates who satisfy the prescribed nationality requirements, including: Citizens of India. Subjects of Nepal. Eligible persons of Indian origin who migrated from the countries listed in the notification with the intention of permanently settling in India. Certain candidates require a Government of India eligibility certificate. The notification provides an exemption from this certificate requirement for Gorkha subjects of Nepal. The entry is restricted to unmarried male candidates. Selected candidates must undertake not to marry until they complete the training programme. A candidate who marries after applying will not be selected for training, even if successful in the selection process. Marriage during training can lead to discharge and recovery of the prescribed training expenditure.

content_sections.heading: Indian Army TES 57 Age Limit 2026
content_sections.text: The age limit for Indian Army TES 57 Recruitment 2026 is 16 years 6 months to 19 years 6 months as on 1 July 2027. Candidates must have been born between 1 January 2008 and 1 January 2011, with both dates included. Age Proof: The date of birth recorded in the Matriculation or Class 10 certificate, or the accepted equivalent certificate, will be used. Changes to the recorded date of birth are not permitted.

content_sections.heading: Indian Army TES 57 Selection Process 2026
content_sections.text: Selection for Indian Army TES 57 begins with shortlisting based on JEE Main 2026 CRL, followed by the Services Selection Board (SSB) interview, medical examination and final merit list. The final merit list is based on SSB marks, subject to medical fitness, eligibility and vacancy availability. Application Shortlisting: The Indian Army will shortlist applicants based on JEE Main 2026 Common Rank List and the prescribed cut-off. SSB Interview: Shortlisted candidates will undergo a five-day SSB assessment. Medical Examination: Candidates recommended by the SSB will undergo a medical examination at a military hospital. Final Merit List: Merit will be prepared based on marks obtained in the SSB interview. Joining Letter: Medically fit candidates will receive joining instructions according to merit, eligibility and available vacancies. The TES-57 SSB interviews are tentatively expected between February and March 2027. The SSB assessment is conducted over five days and consists of two stages. Candidates who do not clear Stage I are sent back on the same day. The SSB assessment includes evaluation by psychologists, Group Testing Officers and Interviewing Officers. Selection centre allocation and interview instructions will be communicated to shortlisted candidates through the registered email address, SMS and official recruitment system. The TES-57 final merit list is prepared on the basis of SSB marks. Higher academic qualifications, previous performance and NCC background do not provide additional merit-list weightage. Final joining depends on medical fitness, the candidate's merit position, fulfillment of eligibility conditions and available vacancies.

content_sections.heading: Indian Army TES 57 Training Period 2027
content_sections.text: Selected candidates will undergo four years of integrated military and engineering training. The programme consists of three years at a Cadets Training Wing and one year at the Indian Military Academy, Dehradun. Candidates who successfully complete the four-year training programme will be awarded an Engineering degree. Candidates recommended by the SSB must submit preferences for all three Cadets Training Wings. Final allocation is decided by the Indian Army.

how_to_apply: The notification describes an offline process. The steps below follow the notification and its application form.
Read the notification and confirm that you meet the qualification, experience and age conditions for the post. Confirm that you hold a valid CRR/RCI or equivalent registration where applicable.
Fill in the prescribed application form (one application for each post). Affix a recent passport-size photograph and self-attest it, and tick any one location in the form.

Prepare a Demand Draft of Rs. 300/- per post, drawn in favour of the Director, Ali Yavar Jung National Institute of Speech & Hearing Disabilities (Divyangjan), payable at Mumbai. Write your name and the post applied for on the backside of the Demand Draft.

Attach self-attested photocopies of mark sheets/certificates/proof of age, experience/CRR No., and other relevant documents related to category, salary drawn, disability and so on. Employed candidates should attach a No Objection Certificate from the employer.
Sign the application. Write the Name of the Post Applied for and the Advertisement Number on the top of the envelope. Use separate envelopes if applying for more than one post.

Send the application by Registered/Speed Post/Courier to: The Director, Ali Yavar Jung National Institute of Speech & Hearing Disabilities (Divyangjan), K.C. Marg, Bandra Reclamation, Bandra (W), Mumbai – 400050. It must reach within 21 days from the date of publication of the advertisement in Employment News.

The notification does not mention an online application link or portal. It asks for the application in the prescribed format, duly signed, to be sent to the Director by Registered/Speed Post/Courier. Postal delays are the candidate's responsibility, as the Institute will not be responsible for them.
important_instructions: The contractual appointment will be on a full-time basis. The candidate will not be permitted to take up any other commercial assignment during the period of engagement. The engagement may be terminated by the Competent Authority at any time without assigning any reason by giving 30 days' notice. A consultant/contractual staff member who wishes to resign may do so by giving 30 days' advance notice or remuneration in lieu thereof. Engagement will be governed by the rules, regulations, terms and conditions of the Institute as currently in force or as may be framed, amended, altered or extended from time to time by the DEPwD/Institute/NBER-RCI. Paid leave, wherever admissible, may be granted as per the provisions of the relevant scheme, NBER guidelines and the applicable rules/policy of the concerned Institute/CRC. The term of appointment shall ordinarily be for an initial period not exceeding 3 years, extendable up to a maximum of 5 years. Extension beyond 3 years requires approval of the Governing Council of the Institute/Executive Council of the Institute/CRC. In no case shall the engagement be extended beyond 5 years. For Group 'A' posts, the contract may be renewed for a total duration of up to 3 years based on annual performance appraisal initiated by the Director, AYJNISHD(D), and reviewed by the Joint Secretary and Chairperson, Executive Council of the Institute. For Group 'B' and 'C' posts, the contract may be renewed for a total duration of up to 3 years by the Director, AYJNISHD(D), based on annual performance appraisal and recommendation of the committee constituted by the Director.

content_sections.heading: Selection and Interview
content_sections.text: The recruitment process involves two stages. Stage I consists of a Written Test / OMR / CBT comprising objective-type multiple-choice questions covering General Knowledge, General Science, General Mathematics, General English, Official Language, Professional Knowledge, Reasoning, and Aptitude. The duration is 60 minutes with a 1/3rd negative marking for incorrect answers and a qualifying percentage of 40%. Candidates qualifying Stage I are called for Stage II in a 1:5 ratio, which involves an assessment of talent comprising a practical demonstration in the applied discipline (35 marks) and testimonials/prizes in the applied discipline (15 marks).

content_sections.heading: Kaushambi Anganwadi Worker Vacancy 2026
content_sections.text: A total of 143 Anganwadi Karyakartri posts are advertised across nine projects: 41 for Scheduled Caste, 30 for Other Backward Class and 72 for Unreserved candidates. The notification gives these project-wise figures. Detailed ward-wise and Gram Sabha-wise vacancy details with reservation and eligibility are available on the district notice boards and the departmental website (see below). The notification states that 194 Anganwadi centres of Kaushambi district (Chail 162, Nevada 32 and Muratganj 01, as written) are being merged into Prayagraj district and are in the process of being placed under Bhagwatpur development block of Prayagraj. Recruitment for vacant Anganwadi Karyakartri posts of these 194 centres will be conducted by Prayagraj district. The figures as printed add up to 195, not 194; the notification does not explain this difference.

content_sections.heading: Kaushambi Anganwadi Worker Eligibility Criteria
content_sections.text: The notification lists these conditions for the advertised posts: Only women candidates are eligible. The candidate must be a permanent resident of the ward or Gram Sabha of the vacant post. If no eligible candidate of the required category is available in the Gram Sabha, the candidate must be a permanent resident of the concerned Nyay Panchayat. In urban areas, the online residence certificate issued by the tehsil at the time of applying must clearly show the relevant ward number or name. Candidates must meet the educational qualification and age limit given below. The notification also lists certificate rules; see the documents section below.

content_sections.heading: Kaushambi Anganwadi Worker Qualification
content_sections.text: The minimum educational qualification for all posts is Intermediate (Class 12) or an equivalent qualification. The merit list will be prepared on the basis of educational qualification, from the minimum of Intermediate or equivalent up to a maximum of postgraduate (as stated in the notification).

content_sections.heading: Kaushambi Anganwadi Worker Selection Process
content_sections.text: The notification states that merit will be prepared on the basis of educational qualification, from Intermediate or equivalent up to postgraduate. It does not mention a written exam or interview. The selection committee takes the final decision on filling the posts. Information filled in the online application is used for selection, and no documents are accepted offline. The notification mentions a preference rule in the context of recruitment to the helper (Sahayika) post. Preference is given to applicants in the BPL (below poverty line) category, as determined under UP Social Welfare Section-2 Government Order No. 22/2015/26-2-2015 dated 14 September 2015 (as amended). The order of preference is: first, BPL widows; then, BPL legally divorced or abandoned women; and if no eligible applicant is available, women of BPL families on merit. If no BPL applicant is available, the same process applies to women above the poverty line. Confirm with the official notification whether this rule applies to the Karyakartri posts you are applying for.

content_sections.heading: How to Apply for Kaushambi Anganwadi Worker Recruitment 2026
content_sections.text: Visit the official portal https://www.upanganwadibharti.in. Fill in the online application form in the departmental format, carefully and accurately. Upload clear, legible, self-attested copies of the required records and mention them in the form. Submit the application on or before 21 October 2026, up to 12:00 midnight. Applications sent offline or by post will not be accepted in any case. If any detail, mark or percentage is found wrong or forged, the candidature will be cancelled.

content_sections.heading: UKSSSC Scaler Recruitment 2026 Selection Process
content_sections.text: Selection is completed in two stages : a qualifying Physical Standard Test (PST) and Physical Efficiency Test (PET), followed by a written competitive examination. Only candidates who clear the Race are permitted to attempt the Shot Put, Long Jump and High Jump events. Candidates get up to 3 attempts in each event to meet the qualifying standard. The PST/PET is purely qualifying (no marks are carried forward); candidates found unfit or unable to meet the standards are declared disqualified from the selection process. Only candidates successful in the PST and PET are admitted to the written competitive examination. 100 marks, Objective Type Multiple Choice, offline mode, 2-hour duration; questions relate to the educational qualification prescribed for the post. Syllabus (Annexure-1) is published separately on the Commission’s website, sssc.uk.gov.in. Minimum qualifying marks: 45% for UR/EWS/OBC candidates; 35% for SC/ST candidates – candidates below this are treated as failed in the written exam. Each MCQ has 4 answer options; 1/4th mark is deducted for each wrong answer. Marking more than one option for a question is treated as a wrong answer and penalized the same way, even if one of the marked options is correct. Unattempted questions carry no penalty. Using whitener or scratching/cutting an option on the OMR sheet is prohibited and invites negative marking. An incorrectly filled roll number or booklet series on the OMR sheet means that OMR sheet will not be evaluated, and the candidature is automatically rejected. Merit list: Prepared based on marks obtained in the written exam. Ties are resolved first by age (older candidate ranked higher), then by English alphabetical order of name. Document verification (Abhilekh Sannirikshan) is a mandatory part of the process after the written exam, where all reservation, educational, preferential and experience-related claims are verified against the service rules; absence at document verification leads to rejection of candidature. Answer keys are published on the Commission’s website after the exam; candidates may raise objections within the notified window by paying Rs. 50 per question objected to. Offline or late objections are not considered.
