content_sections.text: The APPSC Group 2 syllabus includes Indian History, Geography, Indian Society, Current Affairs, Mental Ability, Andhra Pradesh History, Indian Constitution, Economy and Science and Technology. Indus Valley Civilization and Vedic Age. Buddhism and Jainism. Mauryan and Gupta Empires. Delhi Sultanate and Mughal Empire. Bhakti and Sufi Movements. Rise of the Maratha Empire. 1857 Revolt and Indian National Movement. Post-Independence Consolidation and Reorganization. Physical Geography and Major Landforms. Climate, Atmosphere and Ocean Currents. Geography of India and Andhra Pradesh. Natural Resources, Agriculture and Industries. Transport, Communication and Tourism. Human Development, Population and Urbanization. Natural Hazards and Disaster Management. Family, Marriage, Kinship, Caste and Tribe. Religion, Ethnicity and Women. Social Issues and Regionalism. Crime Against Women and Child Labour. Public Welfare Policies and Programmes. Constitutional and Statutory Provisions for Vulnerable Groups. International Current Events. National Current Events. Andhra Pradesh Current Affairs. Logical Reasoning and Analytical Reasoning. Statement and Assumptions. Statement and Arguments. Statement and Conclusions. Number and Letter Series. Coding and Decoding. Relations and Shapes. Percentages, Ratio and Proportion. Simple and Compound Interest. Time and Work, Time and Distance. Data Interpretation and Basic Numeracy.

content_sections.heading: APPSC Group 2 Mains Syllabus 2026
content_sections.text: The Group 2 Main Examination includes two papers covering Andhra Pradesh social history, the Indian Constitution, Indian and Andhra Pradesh Economy, and Science and Technology. Prehistoric Cultures in Andhra Pradesh. Satavahanas, Ikshvakus and Vishnukundins. Eastern Chalukyas and Andhra Cholas. Social and Cultural Development from the 11th to 16th Century. Andhra Under British Rule. Growth of the National Movement in Andhra Pradesh. Andhra Movement and Formation of Andhra State in 1953. Formation of Andhra Pradesh and Important Developments from 1956 to 2014. Constitutional Development and Salient Features. Preamble, Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles. Fundamental Duties and Constitutional Amendments. Legislature, Executive and Judiciary. Judicial Review and Judicial Activism. Centre-State Relations. Constitutional Bodies, RTI, Lokpal and Lokayukta. Elections, Electoral Reforms and Anti-Defection Law. 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendments. Structure of Indian Economy and Economic Planning. National Income, Economic Growth and Development. Economic Reforms and NITI Aayog. Money, Banking, RBI and Monetary Policy. Inflation, Fiscal Policy and GST. Agriculture, Industry and Services Sector. Andhra Pradesh State Economy and Public Finance. AP Agriculture and Allied Sectors. Industrial Development, MSMEs and IT Sector in Andhra Pradesh. Science and Technology Policies and Missions. Space Technology and Indian Space Missions. Defence Technology and DRDO. Information Technology, Digital India and Cyber Security. Nuclear Technology and Energy Policy. Renewable and Non-Renewable Energy. Ecology, Ecosystems and Biodiversity. Environmental Pollution and Waste Management. Climate Change and Sustainable Development. Public Health, Disease Burden and Healthcare Initiatives.

content_sections.text: Candidates can submit their applications for APPSC Group 2 Recruitment 2026 through the official Andhra Pradesh Public Service Commission website from 10 November to 30 November 2026. Read the detailed recruitment notification and post-wise eligibility conditions when published. Open the official online application facility for Group-II Recruitment 2026. Follow the registration or login procedure specified by APPSC. Complete the personal, educational and other required details accurately. Select the relevant posts according to your eligibility and the application instructions. Complete the remaining application requirements prescribed in the detailed notification. Review and submit the application before 30 November 2026 at 11:59 PM. Retain the submitted application details for future reference. Important: APPSC accepts applications only through the prescribed online mode. Candidates should read the detailed notification before submitting the application.

selection_process: Paper Subject Marks Duration
Paper-I Civil Laws 100 3 hours
Paper-II Criminal Laws 100 3 hours
Paper-III English (Translation and Essay Writing) 100 3 hours
The selection process for Direct Recruitment consists of the following stages: Screening Test
Written Examination and Viva Voce.
100 multiple choice objective type questions for 100 marks

with a duration of 2 hours. Applicants securing 40% and above marks are short-listed in the ratio of 1:10 of the available vacancies for the Written Examination. Candidates with identical marks are all called for the Written Examination. The Screening Test marks are not added to the Written Examination marks and are not counted for the final order of merit. Securing the minimum qualifying marks does not vest any right to be considered for the Written Examination.

Questions must be answered only in English (except the translation test). Paper-III Part-I carries 40 marks: translating a passage from English to Telugu and from Telugu to English. Part-II carries 60 marks: essay writing on legal subjects only. Candidates must secure 40% marks in each part of Paper-III. Paper-III marks are not taken into account for eligibility for Viva Voce or for selection. Marks in Paper-I
Paper-II and Viva Voce are taken into account for selection.
Direct Recruitment - Open Competition/EWS: Not less than 55% in each of Paper-I and Paper-II
and not less than 60% in aggregate. Direct Recruitment - Backward Class: Not less than 50% in each of Paper-I and Paper-II
and not less than 55% in aggregate. Direct Recruitment - SC
ST and Persons with Benchmark Disabilities: Not less than 45% in each of Paper-I and Paper-II
and not less than 50% in aggregate. Recruitment by Transfer: Not less than 55% in each of Paper-I and Paper-II
and not less than 60% in aggregate.
The Viva Voce carries 50 marks. A candidate who remains absent is deemed disqualified. After the Written Examination result

qualified candidates are called for Viva Voce in the ratio of 1:3 of the available vacancies in the respective categories. Candidates with identical cut-off marks are all called. Minimum aggregate in Written Examination and Viva Voce: 60% for OC/EWS
55% for BC
and 50% for SC/ST and Persons with Benchmark Disabilities under Direct Recruitment; 60% under Recruitment by Transfer. Tie-break: If two or more candidates secure equal marks
the elder in age is considered. If still tied
the candidate with the higher educational qualification
and then the one with the highest marks in the prescribed educational qualification
is considered. Provisional selection is subject to verification of antecedents.

how_to_apply: Eligible candidates can apply for AP High Court Civil Judge (Junior Division) Recruitment 2026 through online mode only. Follow the steps below:
Visit the official High Court of Andhra Pradesh website, https://aphc.gov.in, and open the online application portal (available from 01-10-2026 to 26-10-2026).
Read the notification carefully and select the category (Direct Recruitment or Recruitment by Transfer) and the applicable reservation category.
Fill in the application with correct details and opt for three Screening Test centres in the order of preference.

Upload the required documents. For Direct Recruitment: certificate of date of birth/SSC, Law Degree certificate, and community certificate for SC/ST/BC/Persons with Benchmark Disabilities/EWS claims. BC applicants must upload the latest Non-Creamy Layer certificate issued in 2025 or 2026 (otherwise the candidature is considered under Open Competition). EWS applicants must upload the latest EWS certificate issued in 2025 or 2026 by the Tahsildar, showing gross annual family income below Rs. 8,00,000/-. Persons with Benchmark Disabilities must upload the Medical Board certificate, and ex-servicemen the Discharge Certificate.

For Recruitment by Transfer, also upload proof of declaration of probation, the employer's proceedings permitting the Law Degree course after entering service, and the latest Service and Conduct Certificate. The latest No-objection Certificate from the employer must be submitted at the time of verification of original certificates.
Pay the application/examination fee online (Rs. 1,500/- or Rs. 750/-, as applicable) and submit the application on or before 26-10-2026 (11:59 PM).
Download the Hall Ticket from the High Court website one week before the Screening Test.

Once the application is submitted, candidates cannot edit options or replace documents. Original certificates must be produced on the day mentioned by the High Court for verification, failing which the candidature will be rejected. The High Court will not entertain correspondence, and no information will be sent to unsuccessful candidates. Candidates must regularly visit the High Court website for updates, as no separate information is provided in any other mode. No TA/DA will be paid for the Screening Test, Written Examination or Viva Voce.

content_sections.heading: AP High Court Civil Judge (Junior Division) Recruitment 2026 Vacancy Details
content_sections.text: A total of 119 posts are notified, comprising 96 posts under Direct Recruitment and 23 posts under Recruitment by Transfer. Selection against the BC-E vacancies will be subject to the outcome of Civil Appeal Nos. 2628-2637/2010 pending before the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India. Vertical reservations (Backward Classes A to E, EWS, SC and ST) and horizontal reservations (women and Persons with Benchmark Disabilities) are as per the AP State Judicial (Service & Cadre) Rules, 2026, read with Rules 22 and 22-A of the AP State and Subordinate Service Rules, 1996 (G.O.Ms.No.77 dated 02-08-2023).

content_sections.heading: Eligibility Criteria
content_sections.text: Eligibility conditions differ for Direct Recruitment and Recruitment by Transfer. All Law graduates who obtained their Law Degree within the preceding one year as on the date of notification are eligible to appear for the Civil Judge (Junior Division) notification for 2026. This is as per the judgment in Bhumika Trust Vs. Union of India and others (Writ Petition (Civil) No. 1110/2025, dated 21-08-2026) of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, and pending amendments to the AP State Judicial (Service and Cadre) Rules, 2026. The candidate must have good character and be free from any infirmity that renders him/her unfit for such appointment. Direct Recruitment means appointment of a person who is not in the service of the Government of India/State. Applicants must possess a Degree in Law awarded by any University established by law in India. Applicants must be a confirmed member or approved probationer in one of the eligible categories listed below. High Court of Andhra Pradesh: Section Officers, Court Officers, Scrutiny Officers, Accounts Officers, Court Masters, Personal Secretaries to Hon'ble Judges, Personal Secretaries to Registrars, Deputy Section Officers and Translators, Senior System Officers, Overseer, Assistant Section Officers, Computer Operators, Assistant Librarians, U.D. Stenographers, System Officers, Assistants, Examiners, Assistant Overseer, Typists and Copyists. District Judiciary in Andhra Pradesh: Chief Administrative Officers, Senior Superintendents, Superintendents, Stenographers Grade-I, II and III, Senior Assistants, Junior Assistants and Typists. Prosecution Services of Andhra Pradesh: Assistant Public Prosecutors, Senior Assistant Public Prosecutors and Additional Public Prosecutors Grade-II. Section Officers in the Law Department of the Secretariat and in the Legislature Department of the State of Andhra Pradesh. Managers of the Offices of the Advocate General, Government Pleaders and Public Prosecutors, and the Editor, I.L.R., of the State of Andhra Pradesh. No person who is facing disciplinary charges, or has undergone any punishment or is under subsisting punishment for any irregularity in discharge of duties, shall be eligible under Recruitment by Transfer. A person who is not a citizen of India, or who is dismissed, removed or compulsorily retired from Judicial Service or any service of the Government, Statutory or Local Authority. A person convicted of an offence involving moral turpitude, or arrested in connection with any such crime. A person permanently debarred or disqualified by the High Court, UPSC or any State Public Service Commission from examinations or selections. A person who directly or indirectly influences the recruitment authority for his/her candidature. A person having more than one wife living, or a woman who marries knowingly a person having a wife. content_sections.heading: Salary/Stipend
content_sections.text: The pay and stipend details given in the notification are as follows: Pay Scale: Rs. 77,840 - 1,36,520 for Civil Judge (Junior Division). Training Period (1 year at the Judicial Academy): Selected candidates are designated as "Trainee Judicial Officers" and are paid a fixed emolument equivalent to one-half of the remuneration payable to a Civil Judge (Junior Division), along with the facilities and benefits ordinarily available to trainees in the Academy. Law Clerkship (1 year): After the training, Trainee Judicial Officers undergo one year of structured Law Clerkship, with the same emoluments as during their training and no further allowance. The first six months are under the supervision of the Principal District/District and Sessions Judges or Members of the Higher Judicial Services, and the remaining six months under an Hon'ble Judge of the High Court of Andhra Pradesh. Regular Appointment: On completion of the Law Clerkship, the Hon'ble Judge places a reasoned evaluation report. If found satisfactory, the Trainee Judicial Officer is appointed to the regular post and is entitled to the regular pay scale and other service benefits.

content_sections.heading: Age Limit (as on 01-09-2026)
content_sections.text: Age is calculated as on 01-09-2026, the first day of the month in which the notification was published. Maximum Age: Applicants should not have completed 35 years of age. SC/ST, Backward Classes and EWS: Relaxation of 5 years. Persons with Benchmark Disabilities: Relaxation of 10 years. Defence Services: For an otherwise qualified applicant who served in the Defence services of the Indian Union, the period of service rendered is excluded in computing the age. Maximum Age: Applicants should not have completed 48 years of age. The minimum age is not specified in the notification.

content_sections.heading: Application Fee
content_sections.text: Open Category/EWS/BC Candidates: Rs. 1,500/- towards online application processing fee and examination fee. SC/ST/Persons with Benchmark Disabilities: Rs. 750/-. Only applicants belonging to a community recognized as SC/ST in the State of Andhra Pradesh are entitled to this concession. Payment Mode: Online only. The application/examination fee once paid will not be refunded, even if the application is rejected for any reason or the notification is cancelled.

content_sections.heading: Selection Process
content_sections.text: The selection process for Direct Recruitment consists of the following stages: Screening Test, Written Examination and Viva Voce. 100 multiple choice objective type questions for 100 marks, with a duration of 2 hours. Applicants securing 40% and above marks are short-listed in the ratio of 1:10 of the available vacancies for the Written Examination. Candidates with identical marks are all called for the Written Examination. The Screening Test marks are not added to the Written Examination marks and are not counted for the final order of merit. Securing the minimum qualifying marks does not vest any right to be considered for the Written Examination. Questions must be answered only in English (except the translation test). Paper-III Part-I carries 40 marks: translating a passage from English to Telugu and from Telugu to English. Part-II carries 60 marks: essay writing on legal subjects only. Candidates must secure 40% marks in each part of Paper-III. Paper-III marks are not taken into account for eligibility for Viva Voce or for selection. Marks in Paper-I, Paper-II and Viva Voce are taken into account for selection. Direct Recruitment - Open Competition/EWS: Not less than 55% in each of Paper-I and Paper-II, and not less than 60% in aggregate. Direct Recruitment - Backward Class: Not less than 50% in each of Paper-I and Paper-II, and not less than 55% in aggregate. Direct Recruitment - SC, ST and Persons with Benchmark Disabilities: Not less than 45% in each of Paper-I and Paper-II, and not less than 50% in aggregate. Recruitment by Transfer: Not less than 55% in each of Paper-I and Paper-II, and not less than 60% in aggregate. The Viva Voce carries 50 marks. A candidate who remains absent is deemed disqualified. After the Written Examination result, qualified candidates are called for Viva Voce in the ratio of 1:3 of the available vacancies in the respective categories. Candidates with identical cut-off marks are all called. Minimum aggregate in Written Examination and Viva Voce: 60% for OC/EWS, 55% for BC, and 50% for SC/ST and Persons with Benchmark Disabilities under Direct Recruitment; 60% under Recruitment by Transfer. Tie-break: If two or more candidates secure equal marks, the elder in age is considered. If still tied, the candidate with the higher educational qualification, and then the one with the highest marks in the prescribed educational qualification, is considered. Provisional selection is subject to verification of antecedents. content_sections.heading: How to Apply
content_sections.text: Eligible candidates can apply for AP High Court Civil Judge (Junior Division) Recruitment 2026 through online mode only. Follow the steps below: Visit the official High Court of Andhra Pradesh website, https://aphc.gov.in, and open the online application portal (available from 01-10-2026 to 26-10-2026). Read the notification carefully and select the category (Direct Recruitment or Recruitment by Transfer) and the applicable reservation category. Fill in the application with correct details and opt for three Screening Test centres in the order of preference. Upload the required documents. For Direct Recruitment: certificate of date of birth/SSC, Law Degree certificate, and community certificate for SC/ST/BC/Persons with Benchmark Disabilities/EWS claims. BC applicants must upload the latest Non-Creamy Layer certificate issued in 2025 or 2026 (otherwise the candidature is considered under Open Competition). EWS applicants must upload the latest EWS certificate issued in 2025 or 2026 by the Tahsildar, showing gross annual family income below Rs. 8,00,000/-. Persons with Benchmark Disabilities must upload the Medical Board certificate, and ex-servicemen the Discharge Certificate. For Recruitment by Transfer, also upload proof of declaration of probation, the employer's proceedings permitting the Law Degree course after entering service, and the latest Service and Conduct Certificate. The latest No-objection Certificate from the employer must be submitted at the time of verification of original certificates. Pay the application/examination fee online (Rs. 1,500/- or Rs. 750/-, as applicable) and submit the application on or before 26-10-2026 (11:59 PM). Download the Hall Ticket from the High Court website one week before the Screening Test. Once the application is submitted, candidates cannot edit options or replace documents. Original certificates must be produced on the day mentioned by the High Court for verification, failing which the candidature will be rejected. The High Court will not entertain correspondence, and no information will be sent to unsuccessful candidates. Candidates must regularly visit the High Court website for updates, as no separate information is provided in any other mode. No TA/DA will be paid for the Screening Test, Written Examination or Viva Voce.

content_sections.text: The selected Research Associate will undertake the following key responsibilities: Literature review and background research. Primary and secondary data collection, management and analysis. Preparation of concept notes, technical reports, policy briefs and academic publications. Facilitation of Training Programmes and Support in Training Module Development. Coordination of field studies, stakeholder consultations, workshops and capacity-building programmes. Regular coordination with WaterAid India on survey module design, Training Needs Assessment (TNA), and other project deliverables and timelines. Liaison with government departments, development partners and community stakeholders. Project documentation, monitoring and dissemination of research outputs. Any other research and programme-related assignments as assigned by the Centre.

content_sections.heading: Age Limit
content_sections.text: Persons with Disabilities: 10 years' relaxation in upper age limit. In-service Bihar Government employees with 3+ years of continuous regular service, moving to a higher pay level: 5 years' relaxation. Candidates who served on a contractual basis on the same post in a non-private government/statutory institution: relaxation equal to the contractual service period (as on 01.08.2026 cut-off). Candidates already in contractual service on the post applied for: relaxation equal to actual contractual tenure served. Ex-servicemen: 3 years plus length of military service rendered, provided actual age does not exceed 57 years. Important: A candidate claiming age relaxation as an Ex-serviceman must submit the relevant supporting certificate at the time of application/document verification, or the claim will not be considered.

content_sections.heading: Reservation Policy
content_sections.text: Reservation benefit is available only to candidates who are permanent (domicile) residents of Bihar . Candidates residing outside Bihar are not eligible for any reservation benefit. SC/ST candidates must submit a caste certificate and a domicile certificate. BC/EBC candidates must submit a creamy-layer exclusion certificate and a domicile certificate. EWS candidates must submit an income & asset certificate and a domicile certificate. All such certificates must be issued by a competent authority notified by the respective State Government of the applicant's permanent area of residence. 35% horizontal reservation for women is applicable only to female candidates who are Bihar domiciles, as per vacancy availability. PwBD reservation is admissible only on the basis of a Disability Certificate issued by a duly constituted Medical Board (Central/State Government), with at least 40% benchmark disability. Temporary disability certificates not renewed after expiry will not be accepted. Grandchildren/great-grandchildren of freedom fighters recognized for pension by the Centre are entitled to 2% horizontal reservation, subject to a certificate from the District Magistrate of their home district. Reservation category, once claimed and confirmed in the application, cannot be changed after registration.

content_sections.heading: Selection Process
content_sections.text: Selection is based on a competitive Computer Based Test (CBT) combined with marks for relevant work experience, as per the following breakup: CBT marks are converted to the merit score by multiplying the percentage scored by 0.75 (e.g., 60% in the CBT = 45 marks). CBT: 100 objective (MCQ) questions worth 100 marks, in Hindi and English, of 2 hours duration. Syllabus is based on the subject matter relevant to the post and is published separately on the BTSC website. Negative marking: +1 mark for each correct answer; −0.25 mark for each wrong answer. The exam may be held in multiple shifts/sessions; a normalization process will be applied to prepare the score card. Minimum qualifying marks: 30% in the CBT, for all categories. Work-experience marks are counted only for candidates who qualify the CBT, based on a Salary Payment Certificate (Annexure-I format) issued by the Director, Fisheries/Deputy Director, Fisheries (Division)/District Fisheries Officer-cum-Chief Executive Officer. A category-wise merit list is prepared from qualified candidates, who are then called for Document Verification.

content_sections.heading: Important Conditions
content_sections.text: Only ONE relaxation among the applicable relaxation clauses will be given to a candidate, even if eligible under more than one. Reserved-category candidates applying against unreserved posts will not receive reserved-category relaxations for that vacancy. Documents not mentioned/uploaded in the online application will not be accepted during Document Verification, and the candidate will be solely responsible for any resulting loss of eligibility, reservation, or work-experience marks. Only clear, properly scanned documents should be uploaded; blurred, unclear, dark, or illegible uploads may lead to cancellation of candidature even at the Document Verification stage. Candidates using fake/forged certificates at any stage of the selection process will have their candidature cancelled and face legal action. The Commission is not responsible for internet/banking disruptions; candidates should not wait until the last date to apply. All information regarding this recruitment will be published only on the BTSC website; the Commission is not obliged to separately notify candidates via newspaper, SMS or email.

content_sections.heading: National Authority- CAMPA Under Secretary Job Description
content_sections.text: Under Secretary: Excellent note-taking/drafting skills; experience of dealing with Court Cases, Parliament matters, Vigilance, RTI, etc.; minimum 5-10 years' experience of handling budget and accounts matters in Ministries/Departments of the Government of India; Output-Outcome Monitoring Framework including submission of the same to the CEO; matters related to Parliamentary Standing Committee including preparation of Background Note and Action Taken Replies; submission of replies to RTI applications; looking after works related to establishment, finance, General Administration, framing of rules and regulations, and regulatory matters. Senior Account Officer: Pre-audit, passing of bills, and preparation of Accounts. Section Officer: Establishment, administration, finance and accounts, and regulatory matters. Technical Officer (Forestry): Examination of the Annual Plan of Operations/Policy matters of the State Authorities, monitoring of different activities, formulate proposals for new schemes. Assistant Section Officer: Initial examination of the proposal relating to establishment finance and regulatory matters, and maintenance of a record of the Section. Accountant/Auditor: Preparation of bills and pre-auditing calculations and deduction of dues, taxes, and depositing them with the concerned department. PPS: Providing all types of secretarial assistance to Members like other CSSS Officers. Sr. PS / PA: Providing all type of secretarial assistance to Senior Officers. Legal Assistant/Law Officer: Keeping all legal records ready and preliminary examination of cases from legal angle, submission of draft Petition/ Rejoinders etc.

content_sections.heading: DU LDE 2026 Eligibility Criteria
content_sections.text: This examination is meant for eligible existing employees of the University of Delhi. It is not an open competitive recruitment for outside applicants. Candidates should have 3 years of regular service as Section Officer/Private Secretary in Pay Level 7 or above. Selection is based on merit from among eligible feeder-cadre employees having the required experience, on the basis of written test, service record and interview. Candidates should have 3 years of regular service in the feeder grade of Senior Assistant/Legal Assistant in Pay Level 6. They should also have undergone one week of training in administrative and financial skills conducted by a College, University or another training institution. Eligible candidates include Assistants, Hindi Assistants, Assistant Archivists or incumbents of other ex-cadre posts working in Pay Level 5/Pay Level 4 with at least 3 years of regular service in the cadre. Junior Assistants/Hindi Typists working in Pay Level 2 with at least 3 years of regular service in the cadre are eligible. Group C employees working in Pay Level 1 who possess Senior Secondary (10+2) or equivalent qualification and have completed at least 3 years of regular service in the grade are eligible.

The document mentions feeder-grade Pay Levels only for determining eligibility. content_sections.text: No separate minimum or maximum age limit is specified for these departmental promotional posts in the notification. Eligibility is based primarily on feeder-grade service, qualification and other post-wise conditions.

content_sections.heading: DU Limited Departmental Examination Selection Process
content_sections.text: Selection for Assistant Registrar involves Written Test, Service Record and Interview/Personality Test. Paper I covers General Studies. Paper II covers University Administration, including University rules, statutes, ordinances, governance, examination regulations, recruitment rules, CCS rules, reservation rules, General Financial Rules, leave rules, Budget and Accounts, RTI Act and related administrative subjects. Service Record is based on ACR/APAR for the preceding three years. The Interview/Personality Test assesses academic qualifications, relevant experience, extra-curricular activities, general awareness, communication, problem-solving ability and overall personality. The test duration is 2 hours. The Senior Assistant departmental examination is also for 2 hours. The Assistant departmental examination has a duration of 2 hours. A qualifying on-spot typing test will be conducted on computer. The qualifying typing speed is 30 words per minute. PwBD candidates who are entitled to complete exemption from typing test under Central Government guidelines are exempt from the skill test. The question papers are bilingual in English and Hindi. Candidates may respond in either language, but the same medium must be used throughout the examination.

content_sections.heading: National Book Trust Senior Backend Developer Job Description
content_sections.text: Selected candidates will be required to perform specific roles based on their designated positions: Senior Backend Developer: Design and build core backend systems, including authentication modules, book storage, recommendation engines, and analytics tracking; implement robust content delivery mechanisms and Digital Rights Management (DRM) protocols; optimize server-side performance, database queries, and overall API security. Senior Front End Developer (Android): Build and maintain high-performance Android application interfaces; optimize app performance, speed, and responsiveness across various devices; ensure strict adherence to platform guidelines and usability standards; collaborate closely with backend and design teams; debug and resolve UI/UX issues. Senior Database Administrator: Manage, configure, and optimize enterprise databases for peak performance; ensure strict data security, regular backups, and disaster recovery planning; monitor database performance, query efficiency, and troubleshoot operational issues proactively; handle database migrations, schema updates, and patch implementations. Senior System Administrator: Manage and maintain servers, networks, and overall system infrastructure; ensure high availability, robust security, and regular data backups; monitor system performance and troubleshoot issues proactively; implement user management protocols. Junior Front End Developer Web: Create and maintain responsive, user-friendly web interfaces; ensure seamless cross-browser and multi-device compatibility; optimize frontend performance, rendering speed, and page load times; implement clean UI components based on prototypes and wireframes; debug and resolve frontend, UI/UX, and responsiveness issues. content_sections.heading: Vacancy Details
content_sections.text: The total number of vacancies is 20, which are distributed across participating Research Councils as follows:

content_sections.heading: Who Can Apply
content_sections.text: Candidates must fulfill the essential educational qualification and eligibility criteria prescribed for the Ph.D. fellowships. Candidates from Non-Ayush (Non-Medical) background must have qualified the concerned National Eligibility Test, namely Joint CSIR-UGC test for JRF and LS(NET), DBT- JRF in Biotechnology, Bio technology Eligibility Test (BET), ICAR's AICE- SRF(PGS), and ICMR JRF and willing to undertake research on AYUSH related projects for pursuing Ph.D. programmes in the University/ Institution of their choice. Research project shall be in the fields of Biomedical Sciences with emphasis on Life Sciences such as Microbiology, Physiology, Molecular Biology, Genetics, Human Biology, Bioinformatics, Biotechnology, Immunology, Pharmacology, Zoology, Environment Science, Botany, Veterinary Sciences, and Pharmacy etc.; Chemical Sciences such as Biochemistry, Chemistry including Analytical Chemistry, Inorganic Chemistry, Physical Chemistry and Organic Chemistry - Phyto Chemistry, Medicinal Chemistry & Natural Product Chemistry etc.; Physical Sciences including Biophysics; Social Sciences such as Psychology for Mental diseases and Sociology for Demographic Survey etc.; and Biostatistics.

rows.essential_qualification: Post Graduation in Biomedical Sciences (with emphasis on Life Sciences / Chemical Sciences / Physical Sciences / Social Sciences/ Biostatistics and having a NET certificate with eligible validity period

content_sections.heading: Pay and Tenure
content_sections.text: The fellowship will be provided for pursuing Ph.D. under a recognised University/ institution of choice by the candidates and during their fellowship, they will be termed as Junior Research Fellows (JRFs) for 2 years extendable as Senior Research Fellows (SRF) for 2-3 years, total for maximum 5 years. The monthly emoluments will be Rs. 37,000/- for JRF and Rs. 42,000/- for SRF + House Rent Allowance per month + annual contingency of Rs. 20,000/- to the University/ Institution. In addition, the fellow may submit a project proposal to obtain one time Research Contingency Grant-in-Aid up to Rs. 01.00 lakh within 3 months of joining the fellowship.

content_sections.text: The examination fee is uniform and charged from all candidates irrespective of category or gender. Payment must be made online via Debit Card, Credit Card, UPI, or other online digital modes on or before the closing date. Fee once paid is non-refundable.

content_sections.heading: HPPSC Assistant Director (Digital Forensic) Selection Process 2026
content_sections.text: Stage 1: Objective Type Screening Test / Descriptive Subject Aptitude Test (Paper-I and Paper-II) Stage 2: Personality Test

content_sections.heading: HPPSC Assistant Director (Digital Forensic) Exam Pattern 2026
content_sections.text: The selection involves two written papers conducted on the same day in two sessions: Paper-I (Objective Screening Test): 1 hour duration, 100 marks, consisting of MCQs on General Knowledge of Himachal Pradesh (30 Marks), General Knowledge of National and International Affairs (30 Marks), Hindi language (20 Marks), and English language (20 Marks). Negative marking of 0.25 marks applies for wrong answers, unattempted questions, or blank circles (using option 'E' to avoid negative marking). Paper-II (Descriptive Subject Aptitude Test): 3 hours duration, 120 marks, based on the syllabus to be decided by the Commission. Minimum pass marks are 45% for General category and 40% for reserved categories.

content_sections.heading: HPPSC Assistant Director (Digital Forensic) Application Correction 2026
content_sections.text: Once submitted, candidates cannot make corrections or modifications to the application through the portal. Online Recruitment Applications once submitted allow no changes except category changes as per Rule 5(iv) of the Himachal Pradesh Public Service Commission (Procedure and Transaction of Business) Rules, 2023.

content_sections.heading: NIT Rourkela Project Manager Job Description
content_sections.text: Responsible for day-to-day coordination, monitoring, administration, financial tracking, and documentation of the ANRF-PAIR project, ensuring timely implementation of activities according to approved objectives, milestones, budgets, and ANRF guidelines. Provide project management and coordination support to the Project Director, Co-Director, and Principal Investigators. Facilitate effective collaboration among Hub and Spoke institutions, monitor project progress and deliverables, and coordinate meetings and project activities. Maintain relevant records and assist in preparing technical, administrative, and financial reports. Manage overall coordination of R&D projects involving internal teams and external collaborators or research partners. Act as the main point of contact between technical teams, management, and external partners for transparent communication. Organize and facilitate project meetings, technical reviews, partner updates, and internal planning sessions, preparing minutes and tracking action items. Gather regular updates from Hub and Spoke Institutes to track progress against milestones, with potential travel to hub institutes for information collection and event organization. Prepare and maintain comprehensive project documentation, work plans, progress reports, and status updates. Create and deliver project presentations for internal reviews, partner meetings, and funding agencies. Oversee technical and administrative component execution, identify and resolve execution risks or bottlenecks, and assist in preparing tender documents for procurement.

Failure to satisfy the prescribed medical examination will bar appointment to the service.

content_sections.text: Selection is based solely on a Written Test (OMR/CBT Mode). Questions are prepared as per the syllabus published on the SSB Odisha website ( ssbodisha.ac.in/syllabus ). In case of a tie, preference goes to the candidate with higher aggregate marks in the Bachelor's Degree (or equivalent); if the tie persists, the older candidate is selected. If conducted in OMR mode, the exam is held in different districts of Odisha (based on candidates' preferred district); if conducted in CBT mode, it is held in multiple shifts at designated centres across the state.

candidates with 1 year of sanitation experience in any urban local body anywhere in the state are included in the lottery.

faq.question: Q1. Is the Special Judicial Magistrate position permanent or on contract, and for how long?
faq.answer: The term of the post is one year from the date of assumption of charge, and the terms may be changed as per the directions of the Hon’ble High Court for the State of Telangana. Powers conferred automatically stand withdrawn upon attaining 65 years of age.

faq.question: Q2. Are allowances paid on top of the base remuneration?
faq.answer: Yes, selected candidates are paid a remuneration of Rs. 45,000/- plus Rs. 5,000/- as conveyance allowance per month.

faq.question: Q3. Who is disqualified from applying for this position?
faq.answer: Practicing advocates, members of any State or Local Authority, members of the State Legislature or Parliament, persons dismissed or compulsorily retired for misconduct from government service, persons convicted or facing pending charges for moral turpitude, persons of unsound mind, insolvents, and contractors or businessmen having a subsisting contract with the government are disqualified.

faq.question: Q4. What is the working schedule for these courts?
faq.answer: As per High Court Circular ROC.No.802/SO/97 dated 29.01.1998, Special Judicial Magistrate of Second Class Courts function for 05 days in a week from Monday to Friday on working days between 7.30 AM and 10.30 AM.

(First Class) with a Ph.D. degree in relevant Life Science subjects such as Biochemistry, Molecular Biology, Genetics, Microbiology, Biotechnology, or related disciplines from a recognized university, plus minimum one year of post-doctoral research experience in the relevant field.

rows.desirable_qualification: Experience in research/project-based technical activities mainly in clinical trial; experience in basic molecular biology techniques including nucleic acid extraction and processing for NGS sequencing and analysis; preparation of technical/project reports; experience in clinical research, laboratory-based research, public-health projects; proficiency in large clinical data management.

content_sections.heading: TIFT Senior Program Manager Job Description
content_sections.text: The engaged professionals will manage various responsibilities under the State Innovation Mission – Tripura and sector expert domains: Plan and execute end-to-end incubation, acceleration, and innovation programme cycles, including outreach, application, screening, selection, and onboarding. Serve as the principal day-to-day contact for participating innovators, founders, and startups; connect them with mentors, experts, investors, and ecosystem partners. Maintain synergy between the State Planning Department/TIFT, LKI, and NITI Aayog. Evaluate and assess existing strategies, methodologies, and systems to improve sectoral ecosystems in Tripura. Prepare development strategies, sectoral targets, socio-economic goals, and State Vision@2047 as per the State's requirements. Support procurement, vendor coordination, travel, venue, hospitality, and administrative arrangements in accordance with applicable Government procedures.

content_sections.heading: Who Can Apply
content_sections.text: Candidates must have completed a Ph.D. thesis in Mechanical Engineering/Chemical Engineering with a research focus on Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD). Applicants must possess expertise in gas dynamics, reactive flows, C++ programming, and OpenFOAM-based CFD simulations. Additionally, candidates must have published 2-3 research papers as the first author in SCI-indexed journals, based on their Ph.D. research in compressible flows.

content_sections.heading: Pay and Tenure
content_sections.text: The Post-Doctoral Fellow position is full-time and tenable for two years. The fellowship amount is Rs. 80,000 per month plus HRA as applicable for the 1st year and Rs. 80,000 per month plus HRA as applicable for the 2nd year. A contingency grant of Rs. 50,000 per year is also provided.
